title.title: Weeklyish Running Update - Intense Base!
title.body:
So I put my August running stats into Claude and it came back and told me my Park Runs are too fast to be proper 'base' runs. 

My other runs are all fine - being mid 130s for the runs, but with the Park Run I go up to 145 BPM - as Claude said - quite a HR increase for no meaningful pace increase...

So I am gonna have to run the Park Runs even slower if I'm doing a base run, no worries, I am just getting used to this! 

That said my last Park Run was as a tourist so I was happy enough doing it slow...

### Queenswood Park Run 

- A beautiful day and hilly, had a friend to chat to for the first few hundred meters but then had to up it a bit... still took it quite easy!

### 28 August...

Knowing I was not going to be able to do the Park Run this week I headed out for a Friday run - this'll be my 8K slot on a Thursday I think next week! 

![Screenshot_20260828_083540_Garmin Connect.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/revisesociology/23vPGdVV77Nyp2P1HjCUeCpx36eL18FwgJysvD1EjSXbaaS5VdYk3Q7NMw4YNc4SSGedL.jpg)



### Next weeks plans 

Need to get in a teeny Octopus session but that's about it, otherwise just two to three easy base runs again, one of them longer at 8K.

I am getting a little bored of the slow pace, time to look at what the build phase is all about!

title.title: An Evening at Dilli Haat
title.body:
![IMG_4244.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbEy8CbFsVsNKsT2nMzo4VGgJykqm6F4w4dLGZsGzEp8g/IMG_4244.jpeg)

As the sun began to set over Delhi, I made my way to Dilli Haat, one of those places where the city’s chaos seems to slow down and India’s many cultures come together under one roof. The evening air was filled with the sounds of people chatting, music playing in the distance, and vendors calling out to visitors passing by.


![IMG_4243.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXLtEsS5wYec21R5Gh6FbyPdEVu7TcExGRdsuQzp9FkMH/IMG_4243.jpeg)


Walking through the colourful lanes, every corner had something different to discover. Handcrafted jewellery, traditional clothes, paintings, wooden crafts, pottery and beautiful souvenirs filled the small stalls. What makes Dilli Haat special is that the experience changes as you walk from one stall to another you can almost feel yourself travelling across different parts of India without leaving Delhi.

![IMG_4246.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmeax27umBtAHr4eQYEW9nHddh5eAXLZwAXBgaQhFnCg3N/IMG_4246.jpeg)

By evening, the food stalls had become the liveliest part of the market. The aroma of spices filled the air as people gathered around stalls serving dishes from different states. From momos and chaat to South Indian delicacies and regional favourites, there was something tempting at almost every corner. I stopped for a bite, sat down for a while, and simply watched the crowd move around me.

![IMG_4247.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXPiWyGQKntvE3CrENEhX7vD9rSpfGfJgW3Vidpu6uQPd/IMG_4247.jpeg)

As darkness settled in, the lights around the market made everything feel even more colourful. Families wandered between the stalls, friends laughed over food, tourists explored the crafts, and shopkeepers continued sharing stories about the things they had made or brought from their regions.

![IMG_4248.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXJjkBz5jP1QF7baUVgkWZUSvf7FyGxAHTy938jHRcv2B/IMG_4248.jpeg)

![IMG_4249.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmbc2TyzmHf7gYDk7D6uyFEQat2otxUPmsgsMfuWNGCKTL/IMG_4249.jpeg)

An evening at Dilli Haat isn’t just about shopping or eating. It is about experiencing a little piece of India’s diversity in one place. For a few hours, surrounded by colours, flavours, crafts and people from different walks of life, Delhi felt less like a crowded metropolis and more like a collection of countless little stories coming together.

![IMG_4250.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaiGTpXKZPzWRy5exXqNjdjJjqUU2nJP1LXcxnm7Z7uTD/IMG_4250.jpeg)

![IMG_4251.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPnDRBkroyApjMWi4oYpRWgPhrBz8zfj2jk84vuh4qNSx/IMG_4251.jpeg)

![IMG_4255.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQAAQN3SNBLtwhN9BtzncFwY7JmPkiU1G5G7kV1QWBN9s/IMG_4255.jpeg)

I left Dilli Haat with a full stomach, a few memories, and the feeling that I had travelled through India without ever leaving the streets of Delhi.

![IMG_4258.jpeg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmVfRK91PhyDQEJKwaK1C86EVuZY41mQb736VXNN1a48Uq/IMG_4258.jpeg)

# <center> Epic Prototype Racing at Spa Francorchamps </center>

![hive dividers-02.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johneyreacko/23swq2FaQRbuC6eGradNc8tKePZ9BMSa1LqxgutNTveC6kJnsfXdeKTtHu93LHHVUdSgF.png)

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=5Ngj9Ixqyek&t=483s


___

Today I bring you the first in a series of gameplay videos I am looking to create for Hive. 

This is a commentary video on a really fun race I had a few days ago. It's my first race back after about 2 weeks. Work has been killing me lately, so finding time to jump into the sim has been tough. 

Still, this race DID NOT DISSAPOINT. 

LMP2 is easily my favorite class of race car. It's got the power and downforce of a prototype, but it lacks the annoying little battery nuances of a Hypercar. It's just the perfect balance. 

In this race I chose the Iron Lynx No 9 Oreca 07 LMP2

![Oreca.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johneyreacko/23u5tHXmNVujM5g9nKbbvR3UkfjtuuvC7csFx49isSR66jUNk59QeN6o95hCrA5jBQmES.png)<center><sub> On the right you can see the real life drivers for this car </sub></center>

This race consisted of: 

#### - 34 LMP3 prototypes
#### - 8 LMGTE GT Race Cars 
These are the GTE manufacturers fielded in today's race
|![Aston Martin LMGTE.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johneyreacko/23vsBVAkiK3s8zA8hecCLvH6zuJDj3TF8kSdWS4V7hm9MMnT8P962zDaCze3bSwehJ7cg.png)|![Ferrari GTE.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johneyreacko/23xoxKhZ2qJgik8QiSDjbyjVjxLNA7oyUjR1vNiWQZsoRRzncRCTMNf4ECAYXxE8FH6Ad.png)|![Porsche LMGTE.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johneyreacko/23wzdNz6afB8JckasfDMzt5pPwsMz2PyJx5j2FbFB33FpfHyozYf2niZAMcM1ZMNMHPVJ.png)|
|-|-|-|
|<center> Aston Martin LMGTE</center>|<center> Ferrari 488 LMGTE</center>|<center>Porsche 911 LMGTE</center>|

My personal favorite is the Porsche. The thing turns on a dime! 

But for today, I'm rocking the Oreca prototype! 
___

The race was 30 minutes that went far better than I expected. I was taking it easy, and after a disappointing qualifying round - 17th out of 34 cars - I was aiming for a top 15 finish. 

I never expected to be fighting to keep 8th! 

I had to take advantage of slower traffic and use all of my race-craft to fend of a clearly faster driver. 

This was incredibly fun and I hope you enjoy the video. 

![hive dividers-02.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johneyreacko/23swq2FaQRbuC6eGradNc8tKePZ9BMSa1LqxgutNTveC6kJnsfXdeKTtHu93LHHVUdSgF.png)

![LMU Results 2.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johneyreacko/23xV6UbGGUMRSsDid3dnXfaJiX5qGcRhJqnyStmMWpfCTGKZG19LEEqhFLuPx5U6XhTVs.png)
<center> A solid boost to both my driver rank and safety rank. I'm going to claw my way back to Silver rating!</center>

![LMU Results 3.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/johneyreacko/23xVAYMa6SF1fTxdpvvgvaYNt8EppvRprJ1xkHX5GGqFvqzYSWDEviYwGw8scggWjtXqd.png)<center>Holy crap! </center>
<center>My fastest lap was faster than Hila, P7, P6, P5 and P4!</center>

title.title: Everyone Has Their Own Learning Curve
title.body:
<div class=text-justify>


From my experience so far, I have come to understand that learning differs for everyone. There are certain things I picked up so easily and I was wondering why I stayed a long time before trying them out, and on the other hand, there are also certain things that keep testing my patience, and I will be like, \

but I see many people, even younger ones, doing it with ease. 



Personally, one of those surprising skills I learned easily was writing to the point of me publishing a book outside the Hive platform. It's still surprising to see that potential in me unleashed for good. I have mentioned it before that the major reason why I left being an art student those days in my secondary school was that I hated to read and write long articles, and trust me, art students got that A1, and I never bargained for such. 



I never saw myself as someone who would later enjoy writing, but here we are on another level outside Hive. Just when the motivation came, I started sharing my experiences through writing and, surprisingly; words kept flowing from within, turning into a long article. The more I write, the easier it becomes, and I keep being in awe of myself. It gradually turned into something I could do at any point without feeling forced to do it. 


Sometimes, I scroll back to some articles I wrote on the Dreemport website, and I am like, \

especially to one of my articles that went trending on Dreamport about postpartum and motherhood. The way the story shapes into something amazing along the line when I start writing is something I can't place. This made me realize that perhaps I had this ability within me a long time ago but never had a suitable platform to express myself, thanks to this blockchain. Again, one other skill I found myself struggling with is knitting and crochet. I admired people crafting beautiful wears and bags for themselves using ordinary yarns. Some use it to make cool money, and boom, I started learning the skill, not to make designs for sales but for personal use. But then, that skill gradually taught me patience I didn't have, lol. I had watched people within my vicinity knit different items with ease, including teenagers, and I kept wondering how they do it effortlessly. I know I didn't give up completely learning the skill because I really desired it. I managed to knit some items, including this bag you see me wear in my profile here in Hive, but ask me how long it took me to get one project done. Ordinary, a tote bag that can take these teenagers two days to knit will take me almost one month. I will do mine, make mistakes, undo it, get frustrated along the line, and start all over later. ![1001340744.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/nkemakonam89/23vhwj7gFP4CUywVNdxi1tjQpXDppCEx45C9rcrYvVceCM5K5quF4m5Yk3CaDj429Q4Ut.jpg) A lot of times I was tempted to abandon it because I was getting bothered by how something that takes most people a minute to get done looks complicated in my hands...although I later learned it but was never perfect or satisfied with the level of knowledge I had on the skills. These particular experiences taught me something important about myself, which is that I must not be naturally good at something before learning to do it; it's all about patience and persistent practice without comparing myself to anyone. ## image is mine

Leí esto dos veces porque me tocó un lugar que conozco bien, tanto desde mi trabajo como psicóloga como desde mi propia vida. Eso de confundir empatía con obligación lo he visto (y lo he vivido) tantas veces que ya perdí la cuenta.

Hay algo que quiero decirte con cariño, no como corrección sino como algo que aprendí a las malas. La calma que describes al final, esa decisión de dejar que la tormenta se desvanezca, a mí nunca me llegó tan limpia. Entender el patrón con la cabeza fue lo fácil. El cuerpo tardó años en creérselo. Todavía hay noches que sigo cargando cosas que ya decidí soltar hace tiempo, y no pasa nada, sigo ahí insistiendo.

Te lo digo porque a veces estos textos, tan bien cerrados, le hacen creer a quien lee que el soltar es un acto de voluntad de un solo momento. Y para mucha gente (yo incluida) es más bien una pelea larga, con recaídas, no una epifanía.

De todas formas, gracias por escribirlo así de expuesto. Hace falta más gente diciendo en voz alta que cuidar a todo el mundo menos a una misma no tiene nada de generoso.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQma6QjgqNNbNG8sxN9MVz5wZxVGxiUcR95hfXGnktvgFxx/img_3335.png)



#### Yo Splinters, 


#### Top of the evening from here buddies. It's another Happy Sunday and trust me the day going well so far. There was a bit of sun today which made the temperature more moderate cos it's been raining for days. I couldn't make it to Church today so I had to do some clean up before fighting my battles on Splinterlands for the day. I managed to play in the MODERN league just to meet up with my new task for the season which is hitting 8k GLINT. Ended up winning about 6 games and I'm now on 7752. There's still about 19 hours left and I think I can reach 8k before the season ends. It's doable. Lol. title.title: Movies Review
title.body:
**Marty Supreme**

Marty Mauser, a young man with a dream that nobody respects, will do anything to chase greatness. One of the most talked-about films of the year, with several Oscar nominations. Is it worth watching? Definitely yes.

🟢🟢🟢🟢

* Timothée Chalamet is E-X-C-E-P-T-I-O-N-A-L! One of the best performances of his career, with such a naturalistic style of acting.
* Josh Safdie is also excellent in the director’s chair.
* Great pacing which, despite the film’s long runtime, never makes you feel bored and never loses momentum.
* I like table tennis 🏓, so that’s definitely a positive for me 😅.
* It satirically criticizes the glorification of scams and cheating.
* Gwyneth Paltrow, who I generally don’t like, was actually good here.
* Gritty cinematography.
* The table tennis scenes are filmed in a completely different and unique way, which I found impressive.

🔴🔴🔴🔴

* At times when our protagonist is likable, he can suddenly become quite detestable as a character.
* It flirts with Martin Scorsese-style cinema, or was that just me?
* I didn’t have a problem with it, but the film’s 150-minute runtime might feel exhausting for some viewers.
* There are a few unnecessary scenes.
* The plot has a few holes.

---

**Return to Silent Hill**

A man receives a letter from a former love, inviting him back to Silent Hill, a once-bright town now consumed by darkness. Should you watch it? If you’re a hardcore fan of the game, I honestly don’t know. If not, avoid it 😅.

🟢🟢🟢🟢

* The monsters from the video game might, and I repeat, *might*, appeal to hardcore gamers 🤷‍♂️🤷‍♂️.
* It starts off somewhat... promising, should I say? But after that, chaos.

🔴🔴🔴🔴

* I wasn’t scared.
* James, our main character, is never really developed from beginning to end.
* The CGI is terrible, although maybe that’s also a budget issue.
* I’m not a fan of the video game, so maybe that plays a role too.
* Performances 👎.
* It could, and should, have been fully atmospheric, but... IT ISN’T!
* Annoyingly repetitive.
* The screenplay is all over the place, which is the movie’s biggest problem.
* There is absolutely no basic narrative coherence, not even a little.
* An exercise in excess in every possible way.
* Abrupt, consecutive action scenes.

title.title: The Fading Allure of the European Union: Why Membership No Longer Holds Appeal
title.body:
In an era defined by sovereignty, economic pragmatism, and growing skepticism toward distant bureaucracies, a striking reality has emerged: fewer and fewer nations or peoples actively desire membership in the European Union. The once-magnetic project of ever-closer union has lost its pull. Two clear examples illustrate this shift—the United Kingdom’s decisive exit through Brexit and Iceland’s firm refusal to resume or pursue accession negotiations.

The United Kingdom’s departure stands as the most dramatic rejection of EU membership in modern history. In the 2016 referendum, a majority of British voters chose to leave the bloc after more than four decades of membership. The campaign centered on reclaiming control over borders, laws, trade policy, and democratic accountability. Critics of the EU argued that Brussels had steadily eroded national sovereignty while imposing regulations that constrained economic flexibility. The subsequent withdrawal process, completed in 2020, confirmed that a major European economy preferred independence to continued integration. Far from triggering a wave of regret, Brexit has instead reinforced the view among many that membership comes with costs that outweigh the benefits of the single market and shared institutions.

Iceland provides a quieter but equally telling case. The Nordic island nation applied for EU membership in 2009 amid the global financial crisis, seeking stability and access to markets. Yet public and political enthusiasm quickly evaporated. Concerns over the Common Fisheries Policy—vital to Iceland’s economy—agricultural rules, and the potential loss of monetary and regulatory independence proved decisive. Negotiations were frozen, and successive governments made clear they had no intention of restarting the process. Icelanders have repeatedly signaled, through polls and political choices, that they prefer their existing European Economic Area arrangements and bilateral ties over full membership. The message is unambiguous: the EU’s institutional demands are no longer attractive enough to justify the trade-offs.

These cases are not isolated. Across the continent and beyond, enthusiasm for joining or remaining has cooled. Candidate countries often face lengthy, condition-laden processes that highlight the EU’s internal rigidities rather than its opportunities. Within the Union itself, debates over fiscal transfers, migration policy, and regulatory overreach continue to fuel discontent. The original postwar vision of peace through economic integration retains historical importance, yet contemporary realities—divergent national interests, demographic pressures, and the desire for policy autonomy—have diminished its appeal.

The thesis holds: the magnetic force that once drew nations toward Brussels has weakened. Brexit demonstrated that exit is possible and, for some, preferable. Iceland’s consistent “no” to negotiations shows that even countries closely linked to Europe can reject deeper entanglement. As long as the European Union prioritizes centralization over flexibility, the ranks of those eager to join—or remain—will continue to thin. Sovereignty, it seems, has become the more compelling proposition.

title.title: Stress-free Married
title.body:
>

> That was a good wedding.

*I am tired from it though.*

What I liked about this particular wedding was while there were some speeches, there wasn't a lot of program. Instead, the focus was more on people spending time together and while there were a lot of unknowns to each other, everyone seemed pretty great - even after a few drinks. As one of the +1 people there (I knew my wife's friends of course), I was still able to strike up good conversations and have a lot of fun with people, who were surprisingly open (this is Finland) and happy to get into the weeds. Though for once, I tried to keep it very light.

---


![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23vsL9zD5Hb17qG6ndjBpG2zq7E8mwTYahAF7EA3oSHr9HBvn54yuZbMSHgQNFSZPbn56.png)


---

<div class=\

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23wWvsuhtqU2tnBZaBsW4FyuvujQLfx4roe8vUkcBFgPfhxs1LDqLaFFy5ptUyWFDCr9D.png --- The ceremony and the reception were at an old villa (not a typical Finnish style) that has been converted to an events location with a few rooms for guests, outside of a small town. The wedding party stayed there, while others like us were in hotels nearby or B&Bs. The town you might have heard of, but maybe didn't know it was a town, or that it was Finnish, since it is \

- where the scissor and knife company started. As a kid at school we had Fiskars scissors. The town has a 400-year industrial history, and it is a beautiful place filled with buildings dating back a few hundred years. I will add a couple images of the town toward the end. \n\n<div class=\

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23wgKcjmrWx8KQP5a7zna9anCsv9bWFHZtu7uoWjJMCQqJvj9wBC4GpzegdVCkFxFxnQ5.png --- The father of the bride and then the happy couple. They are a little older as a couple and don't have kids, so it is a bit different perhaps for them to get married now. They put a fair bit of money into the venue and food and still were able to keep the evening casual and light. And because most guests were also older, the atmosphere was also a bit different to the weddings we have been to in recent years. Less stressed, more experienced. It was well thought out and we moved across the road from the reception place to a very old fire station to kick-on for the evening. ---

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23xKvnFf2qZy4NkzmmiZdZNnuL9ZYaesQdBBkTYeNsinKULn7ztK1xke1RqfWYNjVR1ke.png --- > Where the dancing took place. I only danced a bit at the end, but most people really got into it, singing away, having a few drinks and having a good time. People for the most part followed the dress code, though there were a few ties instead of bowties amongst the men. Not many, but a few. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/Ep1Vznf9CfL6RqsmnUH1QJ3NKLEQ32EKkeCMQ71TSDLduN4LPjJKUb124zXawTmNSwi.png) > And my wife wore her graduation dress. This was taken toward the end of the night and she is still looking in good shape, even though for once she had a couple drinks. We normally don't drink much, but last night I had a few more than I normally have. No hangover though. > Some of her friends remembered the dress. ---

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23yTqicSnxtGKA5aeyH8LAjajNQ8dXVsAmR1FFvp66zhgZepHNcobPsNW3Lo1BzHSsNGx.png --- The evening ended relatively early at around 1am for us and we headed back to the hotel. In the morning, a group of four couples (all friends of my wife) met for breakfast and just chilled out for a a bit, before retiring back to the room before *going to brunch.* I went for a walk to see the town though, as I have never been in the area and it looks very different to the rest of Finland, because there are so many oak trees. The town had the feeling of some American movie set in the south, where people would meet and gossip in the main square, and have baking contests. And the river that winds through it was really weird. I am not sure if they have shaped it, but where I walked it was incredibly shallow and maybe only a meter deep at the deepest I saw. This was of course used heavily for industry in the past, but it is now just a destination that people go for the beauty and the factories are all closed. ![image.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/Eos1H1RFNT3G7CTSiaLo2XNFzL2VrMC6sPfs7snHiUV4bT61aTgf62Ard7QVVmQVFgP.png)

>https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/tarazkp/23tvYHq3HhPXoUHnUX26Wab78wE1SyXb4FAd6juZwkXH3HP4u4xCq5yJNZPhYnNX2SNk8.png --- > I was sceptical about the brunch. But we had signed and paid up, so we went along back to the reception location. I thought it was a bit of a silly idea to have people turn up for brunch the next morning, but it was actually really great. About half the guests attended. We ate together and then spent a couple hours just hanging out, friends talking to each other about the night before, the location and catching up on whatever was going on and it was a really relaxed end to the event. And when we were driving back (we went with friends), people commented how strange it was to feel so relaxed after a wedding, despite the drinking, lack of sleep and all the out of the ordinary. The event was also child-free, which probably added to the relaxation of the parents, but I think it was because there was little programming pressure on the evening and no rushed goodbyes in the morning that people could just ease away from the weekend. > Still tired, but happily surprised. I think that my wife and I will visit this town again in the future, maybe for an anniversary or something or when my brother comes to visit. It would be pretty amazing once the fall colours burst out in a few weeks, but any decent warm day in the summer would put it in a good light. A good weekend. title.title: The Letter Under the White Face Towel
title.body:
She said it in a very way that I almost burst into laugh. 

It was a very hot Sunday afternoon, and I was already outside the church premises, in a church I usually attend in Lagos State. I was helping a friend with something on his phone. The church generator was making a familiar clicking sound as it was sounding like the petrol in it is about to finish. And somewhere near the church street, a truck kept sounding its horn because that around to the street was very narrow. 


My friend that I was helping with something on his phone opened the boot of his car and brought out a small carton filled with some files that it looks like he hasn't touched for weeks. In it were some old photographs, personal documents, receipts, some notes I can barely see what was written on, and clothes that still smelled faintly of something that has been stored up for a while.


Then she brought out a purple envelope and brought out the letter in it.


The inner letter was folded just twice, and the edges were slightly brown. Before giving me the envelope, he placed it inside one of the white face towels he brought it out with. 



“Keep the face towel safe with you,” he said. \

body.title: I Will Find You - Review and Opinion [Esp-Eng]
body.body:
>

![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmX8mhwsvFFYNkZLbDiBg8nEyUr8X68TTAMXXVm28YPgJ7/i_will_find_you-143124277-large.jpg)

[Fuente](https://www.filmaffinity.com/es/filmimages.php?movie_id=250217)
Hace unos días vi una película en Netflix que, por el elenco, me imaginé que sería buena. La película de llama \

Era una película de suspenso que contaba la historia de David, nuestro protagonista, quien fue encarcelado por acabar con la vida de alguien muy pero muy cercano a él, y de una manera bastante terrible, cuyo único destino es morir en prisión, ya que está pagando una cadena perpetua por este crimen. ​Todo el mundo, incluso uno por un momento, piensa que simplemente es la justicia haciendo de las suyas, hasta que escuchas al protagonista e insiste en que él no tiene nada que ver con lo que ocurrió. Sin mencionar el hecho de que la muerte de este ser querido al que tanto amaba sigue causando en él un dolor demasiado profundo y del que no puede sanar correctamente por estar en el lugar incorrecto. ​Así transcurre el tiempo y, durante cinco años, David sigue pagando por un crimen que dice que nunca cometió, hasta que, luego de no ver ningún rostro conocido después de todo este tiempo, llega una visita superinesperada que le devuelve una pizca de esperanza a su vida. Aquel rostro conocido no solamente llega con una noticia que puede cambiarlo todo para David, sino que también le recuerda que, después de tanto tiempo, puede volver a confiar en alguien. ​La película te mantiene en suspenso. Al principio no sabes quién de todos está diciendo la verdad y, durante toda la película, no puedes saber tampoco quién es bueno y quién es malo, e incluso cuáles son las razones del malo para hacer lo que hace. A medida que la iba viendo, tenía un montón de teorías de quiénes eran los que estaban involucrados en todo este crimen e incluso pensé en algunas de las razones, pero me equivoqué en todo. ​La verdad es que es una de esas películas que termina de una manera superinesperada. El final no es nada de lo que pensabas y, la verdad, en lo personal me gustan estas películas en las que todo termina siendo una sorpresa. Por supuesto, la película te hace mantenerte a la expectativa de lo que va a ocurrir y ansioso por saber finalmente quién está involucrado en todo esto y el porqué. >A few days ago, I watched a movie on Netflix that, based on the cast, I figured would be good. The movie is called “I’ll Find You.” It was a thriller that told the story of David, our protagonist, who was imprisoned for taking the life of someone very, very close to him—and in a rather terrible way—and whose only fate is to die in prison, since he’s serving a life sentence for this crime. > >Everyone—even if just for a moment—thinks it’s simply justice running its course, until you hear the protagonist insist that he had nothing to do with what happened. Not to mention the fact that the death of this loved one, whom he loved so dearly, continues to cause him such deep pain that he can’t properly heal from it because he’s in the wrong place. > >Time passes, and for five years, David continues to pay for a crime he claims he never committed—until, after not seeing a single familiar face in all that time, a completely unexpected visitor arrives, bringing a glimmer of hope back into his life. That familiar face not only arrives with news that could change everything for David, but also reminds him that, after so long, he can trust someone again. > >​The movie keeps you on the edge of your seat. At first, you don’t know who’s telling the truth, and throughout the entire movie, you can’t figure out who’s good and who’s bad—or even what the bad guy’s motives are for doing what he does. As I watched it, I had a bunch of theories about who was involved in this whole crime and even thought of some possible motives, but I was wrong about everything. > >​The truth is, it’s one of those movies that ends in a totally unexpected way. The ending is nothing like what you thought, and honestly, personally, I love these movies where everything turns out to be a surprise. Of course, the movie keeps you on the edge of your seat, wondering what’s going to happen next and eager to finally find out who’s involved in all of this and why. ![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaFPyostf7LQhVfWGVt3AtvrRVBnxh7dT44VTcPW2fb4M/i_will_find_you-743032365-large.jpg)
[Fuente](https://www.filmaffinity.com/es/filmimages.php?movie_id=250217)
​Puedo decir que es una película que avanza rápido y es bastante movida, así que no solamente es entretenida de ver, sino que no te permite distraerte, sino estar atento a todo lo que está ocurriendo. Ya sabemos que hoy en día, por la poca concentración que todos tenemos debido a los videos cortos, esto es algo superpositivo de una película, así que ya por ese lado tiene varios puntos positivos. ​Esta película me dejó varios puntos sobre los cuales reflexionar. El primero de ellos es lo necesario que es tener a alguien, aunque sea una sola persona, que crea en tu palabra, que crea en ti cuando te hace falta. Nos encontramos completamente solos y hasta podemos perder la esperanza y resignarnos, pero, a su vez, podemos lograr demasiadas cosas cuando aunque sea una persona cree lo que le estamos diciendo. Así que me hizo pensar en la importancia de hacer buenos amigos y de tener gente en la vida que siempre te motive a ser mejor y que te conozca tanto que sepa de lo que eres y no eres capaz. ​Por otro lado, al terminar la película me quedé con esta sensación rara en el cuerpo, de lo loco que es hoy en día el poder que tiene una persona por el simple hecho de tener los medios económicos para comprar lo que sea y a quien sea. Da algo de miedo darse cuenta de que vivimos en un mundo en el que una persona puede pagar por su inocencia y simplemente seguir con su vida normal como si nada hubiera pasado. Es el caso de que el ser humano le ha dado toda autoridad al dinero y este puede corromper hasta a la persona más buena si no tiene cuidado. ​Y, por último, también me dejó pensando mucho en el concepto de amor que los seres humanos tenemos. Muchas veces este va condicionado a la forma en la que fuimos criados y, si no trabajamos en ello, puede llevarnos a causar daño a esa persona que tanto decimos que amamos. Debemos aprender y tener muy claro lo que es el verdadero amor y cómo este jamás hace nada que pueda lastimar a nuestro ser amado e incluso a las personas que son importantes para él. >I can say that it’s a fast-paced, action-packed movie, so it’s not only entertaining to watch, but it also keeps you on your toes—you can’t let your attention wander. We all know that these days, with our short attention spans due to short videos, this is a huge plus for a movie, so it already has several strengths in that regard. > >This movie gave me several points to reflect on. The first is how essential it is to have someone—even just one person—who believes what you say and believes in you when you need it most. We can find ourselves completely alone and may even lose hope and give up, but at the same time, we can achieve so much when even just one person believes what we’re saying. So it made me think about the importance of making good friends and having people in your life who always motivate you to be better—people who know you so well that they understand what you’re capable of and what you’re not. > >On the other hand, when the movie ended, I was left with this strange feeling—about how crazy it is these days that one person can wield so much power simply because they have the financial means to buy anything and anyone. It’s a little scary to realize that we live in a world where a person can pay for their innocence and simply go on with their normal life as if nothing had happened. The fact is that human beings have given all authority to money, and it can corrupt even the kindest person if they aren’t careful. > >And finally, it also made me think a lot about the concept of love that we humans have. Often, this concept is shaped by the way we were raised, and if we don’t work on it, it can lead us to hurt the very person we claim to love so much. We must learn and be very clear about what true love is and how it never does anything that could hurt our loved one—or even the people who are important to them.

body.title: Si no se lo dirías a la cara, no es crítica, es odio | If you wouldn't say it to their face, it isn't criticism, it's hate
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNiHUrQs8iG2EDNToUu23DMnmteWYyFWvwu1HxFVi5qZx/1788115051550.png)

Hola, familia de Holos&Lotus. Vengo con un tema que llevo mascando hace rato. Me paso muchas horas en redes, demasiadas quizás, y hay algo que siempre me ha resultado interesante y a la vez me ha molestado profundamente: cómo tratamos a la gente cuando hay una pantalla de por medio. Lo comenté hace un tiempo en Twitter, de pasada, casi como desahogo, pero se quedó dando vueltas en mi cabeza y quiero traerlo aquí, con más calma, porque me interesa debatirlo de verdad con ustedes, no solo soltarlo y ya.

El anonimato alienta la deshumanización. Zimbardo lo llamó desindividuación desde los setenta: cuando una persona siente que no la pueden identificar, el peso de sus actos se diluye, la responsabilidad deja de sentirse propia y la consecuencia parece, de pronto, reversible. No es una teoría abstracta. Es lo que pasa cada vez que alguien abre una cuenta sin foto, sin nombre real, y escribe algo que jamás diría mirando a los ojos.

Pero hay algo que pesa más que el anonimato en sí: hace diez años el ciberbullying se trataba como lo que era, un problema serio, con campañas, con adultos preocupados, con la sensación colectiva de que herir a alguien por una pantalla seguía siendo herir. Hoy ese mismo comportamiento se disfrazó de otra cosa. Dejar un comentario ofensivo, pasivo-agresivo, directamente cruel, debajo de la foto de un influencer, un artista, cualquiera con algo de exposición pública, ya no se lee como agresión. Se lee como opinión. Como crítica válida. Como algo que esa persona \

el día que decidió mostrarse.\n\nAhí está la trampa moral, y vale la pena mirarla de frente. La idea de que exponerse públicamente es un consentimiento tácito para recibir cualquier cosa a cambio no resiste el menor análisis serio. Nadie firma, al abrir una cuenta o al aceptar un rol público, una cláusula que diga \

, funciona como un permiso que quien odia se otorga a sí mismo después de odiar, nunca antes: se construye para justificar lo que ya se hizo, no para autorizarlo con antelación.

Y aquí toca ir un paso más allá, porque el anonimato solo se queda corto como explicación. Hay gente que insulta con su nombre y su cara puestos, sin esconderse, y lo hace con la misma frialdad que el usuario sin foto. Lo que cambia no es solo si te pueden identificar. Es la distancia. Suler lo describió como efecto de desinhibición online: la pantalla, con o sin nombre real detrás, ya funciona como un colchón psicológico entre lo que escribes y la cara de quien lo va a leer. No ves el gesto que provoca tu mensaje. No hay silencio después de decirlo. El anonimato, más que la causa real, termina siendo la excusa más cómoda para no mirar de frente que la crueldad, con nombre o sin él, se volvió más fácil de ejecutar y más fácil de perdonarse.

Llevemos esto al punto donde de verdad cuesta mirar. Hay casos documentados, no aislados, de personas públicas que atravesaron crisis de salud mental severas, algunas con desenlaces irreversibles, después de meses sostenidos de comentarios que individualmente parecían \

. Ninguno de esos comentarios, por separado, se sintió como una agresión grave para quien lo escribió. La suma sí lo fue. Y ese es exactamente el mecanismo que la desindividuación permite: nadie se siente responsable del daño total porque nadie escribió el daño total, cada quien escribió solo su fragmento, anónimo o no, siempre a distancia.\n\nAsí que la próxima vez que el dedo esté sobre el teclado listo para dejar ese comentario que \

, vale la pena esa pausa que cuesta: ¿lo dirías igual si esa persona pudiera ver tu cara mientras lo lees? Si la respuesta es no, ya sabés lo que realmente es.

---

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNiHUrQs8iG2EDNToUu23DMnmteWYyFWvwu1HxFVi5qZx/1788115051550.png)


Hey, Holos&Lotus family. I'm bringing something I've been chewing on for a while. I spend a lot of hours on social media, probably too many, and there's something that's always felt interesting to me and deeply bothered me at the same time: how we treat people the moment a screen sits between us. I mentioned it briefly on Twitter a while back, almost as a way of venting, but it stayed on my mind and I wanted to bring it here, with more room to think, because I genuinely want to debate this with you, not just throw it out there and move on.

Anonymity fuels dehumanization. Zimbardo called it deindividuation back in the seventies: when a person feels unidentifiable, the weight of their actions thins out, responsibility stops feeling personal, and consequence suddenly seems reversible. It isn't an abstract theory. It's what happens every time someone opens an account with no photo, no real name, and writes something they'd never say while looking someone in the eye.

But there's something that unsettles more than anonymity itself: ten years ago, cyberbullying was treated as exactly what it was, a serious problem, with campaigns, with worried adults, with a shared sense that hurting someone through a screen was still hurting them. Today that same behavior wears a different costume. Leaving an offensive, passive-aggressive, outright cruel comment under an influencer's photo, an artist's post, anyone with a bit of public exposure, no longer reads as aggression. It reads as opinion. As valid criticism. As something that person \

the day they chose to be seen.\n\nThat's the moral trap, and it's worth looking at directly. The idea that exposing yourself publicly is tacit consent to receive anything in return doesn't survive serious scrutiny. Nobody signs a clause, on opening an account or accepting a public role, that says \

works less like an ethical stance and more like a permission the hater grants themselves after hating, not before: it gets built to justify what already happened, not to authorize it in advance.

And here it's worth pushing one step further, because anonymity alone falls short as an explanation. Plenty of people insult with their real name and face attached, no hiding at all, with the same coldness as the faceless account. What changes isn't only whether you can be identified. It's distance. Suler described this as the online disinhibition effect: the screen, whether or not a real name sits behind it, already works as a psychological cushion between what you write and the face of whoever will read it. You don't see the wince your message causes. There's no awkward silence after saying it out loud. Anonymity, more than the real cause, ends up being the most convenient excuse we've found so we don't have to look straight at the fact that cruelty, named or not, got easier to commit and easier to forgive ourselves for.

Let's take this to the point that genuinely stings. There are documented cases, not isolated ones, of public figures who went through severe mental health crises, some with irreversible outcomes, after months of sustained comments that individually looked like \

None of those comments, on its own, felt like serious aggression to whoever wrote it. The sum was. And that's exactly the mechanism deindividuation enables: nobody feels responsible for the total damage because nobody wrote the total damage, each person only wrote their own fragment, anonymous or not, always at a distance.\n\nSo next time your finger is over the keyboard, ready to leave that comment that's \

it's worth that pause, the one that costs something: would you say it the same way if that person could see your face while reading it? If the answer is no, you already know what it actually is.

---

Though initial archery headshots dropped a few zombies quietly, one alerted the nest, triggering a massive horde attack that quickly overwhelmed and killed me. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfGLzH5NoAHNJHtQnRniTbLJYv2WCNH1XvkgjZ8Vuhcen/screenshot_2_.png) Perched high on the safehouse pole, I pulled out my binoculars and scoped out a large warehouse sitting in the distance, marking it as my next target. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXFr6onFzPMKS6Ni7YUFzx9sjNQaeoxYLKWyETsXsomUr/screenshot_3_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWnZYMcru7K1RojWvfQ2hxeXRQPuhurKWUC3z59yHwxcm/screenshot_4_.png) Dropping down from the tower, I sprinted across the place and climbed a neighboring building to keep off the streets. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRNtANHkvknEnMy8uJszJVo1NwBVdNvmyt6Gkb9b5MQz7/screenshot_5_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX5tzA7w7qADedDtRQP4HJ82fKowxeVZNPzf6awhtJNKe/screenshot_6_.png) Glancing over the ledge, I saw the ground level packed end-to-end with roaming infected. Safely out of their reach, I spotted a high, broken window along the warehouse wall that offered a clean entry point into the interior. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNdu2kZow1k9Foqr9QJx7pT2PVLsWi7kpnXQ7uQecnTrh/screenshot_7_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX7549CKmnrm1QJzDu3p5k1ijCrkQW7Xp6VjYqa1ZqH63/screenshot_8_.png) I scrambled through the glass frame and landed inside the dimly lit upper levels of the structure. A quick scan revealed multiple infected lurking among the rafters and walkways. ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWMBUb5QXXYmHbELe3Wr1gpLoUrei1tdYgqLUiwy4eAYb/screenshot_9_.png) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWJyH4YeM5t7fib1MGe8YkQfC86zSX84sPMqXjpSZA5Qk/screenshot_10_.png) Drawing my bow, I lined up precise headshots, dropping the first few hostiles cleanly without making a sound. They poured out from every corner, rushing my position all at once. Trapped in close quarters with nowhere to fall back, I was rapidly surrounded and taken down by the horde. I'll show what happens next later. --- I personally took all the screenshots from my play and I used a logo of the game from online to use in the thumbnail. This is Pikachuuuuu signing off. title.title: Building User Interfaces: A Comprehensive Review of V0 by Vercel AI — A Developer's Perspective
title.body: /> _Screenshot of the tool's interface_ What is v0 by Vercel? --------------------- It is an AI-powered tool that generates complete user interfaces and websites—along with the underlying code—at the click of a button. You can simply provide a text description of what you want to build or even upload a design image. It enables developers and designers to create interfaces and websites in mere seconds, eliminating the need to write code from scratch. How does V0 by Vercel work? --------------------------- You can simply provide a text description or upload an image of the interface or website design you want. The AI then analyzes the input, designs the interface, and displays it for you. Afterward, you can request modifications to specific elements using text commands before copying the ready-to-use code directly into your project. Is V0 by Vercel a paid service? ------------------------------- It offers a free plan upon sign-up that provides a monthly credit allowance sufficient for building interfaces and generating code at no cost; in my opinion, this is adequate for experimentation, making adjustments, and personal use. There are also paid plans—typically starting at $20 per month—that offer significantly more credit and faster generation speeds. * * *

/> _A screenshot to include when requesting a sales page design._ * * * Key Features of V0 by Vercel ---------------------------- * **Building Integrated Interfaces and Applications:** It has the ability to transform text or images into interactive interfaces and fully functional web components. * **Writing and Debugging Code:** It can generate modern, clean, and organized code, while also allowing for modifications and error correction via text chat. * **Saving Time and Effort:** It saves you hours of manual coding and styling, completing the task in just a few seconds. * **Ready-to-edit styles and templates:** Provides a starting point with a variety of templates that are fully customizable. * **High-quality design:** Built upon modern global design standards and professional libraries like shadcn/UI, ensuring a sleek, contemporary look that is responsive across all screen sizes. * * *

/> * * * _Screenshot after an edit request_ Drawbacks of Vercel’s v0 ------------------------ * **Potential for errors and hallucinations:** Like any AI tool, it may generate code containing bugs or elements that are not accurately interpreted; this necessitates human review and intervention to modify and verify the code. * **Free plan limitations:** The free plan offers limited credits that can be quickly exhausted during experimentation and editing, compelling you to switch to a paid plan for more features and a larger credit allowance. * **Lack of a human touch:** Although it instantly generates the interface and code, a developer proficient in React and Tailwind is required to fully integrate and develop it within the project; in other words, it is not suitable for absolute beginners. * * * Developer's Take ---------------- This tool has created quite a buzz in the programming world; it is excellent and saves a great deal of time and effort for developers and those looking to learn programming.

body.body:
Respecting what the community needs while listening to your own body is what a good leader does! Deciding not to force a big project when it just isnt the right time—specially after doing 10 whole years of events—takes a lot of guts and visual smarts.

Here are a few quick reasons why this was the right Move:

* **Saving the Money:** Steering clear of the proposal right now keeps the funds safe while prices are low. Waiting to bring it back when things are stronger makes way more sence.
* **Keeping the Idea Great:** Waiting untill European sponsors are ready means *ChainCulture* can be super awesome instead of rushed. Keeping the venue contacts warm and looking at that cultural Grant in December is really smart planning.
* **Taking care of Yourself:** Ten years of planning party stuff is a ton of work! Stepping back to rest protects your own energy and keeps you from getting burned out.

Turning HiveFest XI into a community-run event is such a cool way to see what decentraliztion is all about. It lets everyone who already bought plane tickets still hang out without hurting the chain.

Thank you for ten years of hard work, for keeping things totally honest, and for putting everyone else first. Cant wait to see what the city captains do next!

body.title: History, heritage, and a hint of mystery on the tracks.
body.body:
Travelling to hill station is quite enjoyable. Set up in high altitude region of the mountain many people visit these spot to spend aome memorable time. However, Hill stations often have haunted folklore associated with them. The unique combination of dense, foggy landscapes, isolated environments, and lingering colonial history naturally inspires human imagination and eerie tales. On top of that, some of the well known authors like Ruskin Bond set classic ghost and mystery stories in hill stations like Mussoorie and Landour, cementing these regions in the public imagination as homes for the supernatural.


On my last visit to Solan, I was fascinated by the quietness of one such railway station. There are few of the station that were built right under the mountains. However one of the station does have one such haunted folklore that needs to be shared. It is Barog Railway Station situated in Kalka-Shimla train route.


![1000319134.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/23z7HnJEsrnZibW6oSAaK3CPrvF2LnVr49vyASWQxCC6orANLFPaXt7fZSU7zLq83fbVh.jpg)

Barog is famous for the longest straight tunnel on the railway line. When the train stopped at the platform, the atmosphere remains same as of any other Indian railway station. There is a unique stillness and quiten3ss in the atmosphere. People get down to buy some snacks while few started recording at the besutiful scenic beauty. One of the locals travelling with me, then disclosed the facts that the rsilways station is a haunted one. And there is a an old stories that goes around the British rule. I was surprised to learn about the story. As It was unbelievable to find such a beautiful location with a haunted tale 


![1000319136.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/EpXH5bTGbHj9L8vRb16HPN5P37sPKQjSS5RqEuiL28x6wxtNAYykxTDgnwqkm4Qovz8.jpg)

Many hill stations in India were built during the British era as summer retreats. Old, decaying Victorian buildings and tragic accidents from that harsh construction era leave behind a legacy of sorrow and dark folklore. This one is not different. When we reached the platform, it was a business as usual. But I got curious to know more about the stories. I reach out the local person again and asked him to share the entire stories. The old fella was also get excited to tell me the haunted tale.

![1000319130.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/23ynN5AurUjwbUM51xX4dDc5D6GWCu2Zp3FR753CqsFQL1fciGfuFHTYfbduH6gTsh5TJ.jpg)

The local stories that is associated took us to the British Era. The Tunnel is named after **Colonel Barog**, a British engineer who miscalculated the digging from both ends and failed to make the paths meet. He unable to get tye exact exit of the tunnel. This made the britisher to fine him. He was heavily ridiculed, leading him to commit suicide inside the incomplete tunnel. Locals say the area is haunted by his friendly spirit.

![1000323720.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/EoK5P7ZWHcL1if1BDK6MVHKAHb3HK8HVJSVGnqN4UmBpnuCV7udFtUfadoLjUqcuvka.jpg)

But there is no reason to get scared at the rsilway station as the actual tunnel, Under wh8ch he committed suicide was 1KM away from this spot. Tye tunnel was still incomplete, and rhis one was made as a makeshift for commuting purpose. Today, many toy train in this route passes through this tunnel and remembers the poor engineer.

![1000319135.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/EoiVDpQqfvjUPQAGHMNfofrWtYQQsVULNNoz4WaH68G2ePCRGHSwbvSUJ4Wa4ZRvi2s.jpg)

Todays, people get down at the station buy snacks take selfie and enjoy tye cool abd pleasant weather. There were many hawkers selling snack item at your seat. Those snack were worth eating. The vegetable cutlet is a popupar dish to try at this station.


![1000323249.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/23z774VDG5AQc3vNFywUQu73QzHHZ2rHc1ykn7pt7CPAwE2f1tiXP9Y8C6UMS3Z5NwP9z.jpg)

The station retains its original 1903 wooden architecture, antique. Unlike typical terrifying ghost stories, local legend portrays Colonel Barog as a gentle, lonely spirit who sometimes chats or shares a laugh with visitors inside the dark, echoing tunnel. I listned the whole stories and went on with loads of imagination in mind.

![1000323719.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/242hRzVmHXfZnUNJEatVxPKbXfounKNcJvBffhBUk5sD6Ger3kYZ5xmsydSMcn4SEY1Mc.jpg)

Connected to the UNESCO World Heritage Kalka-Shimla Railway line, the myth adds a layer of romanticized mystery to an already popular scenic destination. The railway line is one of the few which runs on steam engine. There are quite a few operational but this line always pulls a lot of visitors. 






**In good faith - Peace!!**



![1000037470.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/steemflow/Eo8M1obna2cYnnMAc2ZC3wWMW9ZqZHvk9StEga6aY2cTsKmweW7zFBDm7D13YHVoC5N.png)

body.title: My Actifit Report Card: August 29 2026
body.body:
Saturday started out fairly great. Cathrine spent the night, and in the morning, I woke her up gently. She had, as per usual, fallen asleep pretty quick once I tucked myself close to her 🥰 I asked if she wanted some coffee, and she said yes. I had already made the coffee because I knew what her answer would be 😂 Somewhere around 10:30-11:00 she had to leave to take care of some stuff. We had arranged to go see a common friend and would bring her oldest son along. Our friend has just got a new apartment. Cost him about 1.45 BTC, with the current BTC price. Quite a nice place, actually 👌🏼 Before this, she asked if I would go see my dad as he live nearby. At first, I hadn't thought about it, but with her arguments for why SHE would have done it, if she were me, I decided to just go visit him without him knowing. When I was about 5 minutes away from his house, I sent him this image and then called him to let him know he should have some coffee ready 🤣 ![](https://usermedia.actifit.io/e212adba-8e43-40de-b93c-597ff88a394e.jpg) The visit itself was a remarkable success 🙌🏼 This is a rare thing for us as we usually end up arguing fairly quickly - not this time, though. I spent almost 2 hours there before meeting up with my friend, Cathrine, and her son. I must say, the impact she has on me is immense. I have never, as in ***NEVER*** met anyone who is as thorough as she is. Everything she does and plans for is just... not perfect, but so caring and loving. This state of things, be it a dream or not, must never end. I have truly re-met my soul mate ❤️ --- When we had finished visiting our friend, I drove with her back to their current place, and a bit later, I went home. All in all... what a great day! And her and I... **WOW!!** --- Thank you for reading! **Stay *acti*ve, stay *fit***

body.title: Good Games and Their Adventures Are Not Easily Forgotten: Skyrim (Eng-Esp)
body.body:
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmWVmNKFBvyzwE3JDhAhcGTEPU6jSkjmuDRLuX7qyYvu1n/1788113991777.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSHA4tStpAgWqvbwLsVMbELBAfi3rV48MayLDaMbUEuGc/1788113992039.jpg)



# <center>Good Games and Their Adventures Are Not Easily Forgotten: Skyrim</center>

---

<center>*English*</center>

<div style=\

> Continuing our streak of nostalgia for past-generation games, today I brought out my physical copy of **The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim** for the Xbox 360. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmP36KwUzQVbQ5umsY3AwdRWWyQAZxtvc3H5TxvDwZP6Mb/1788113992280.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVEEhz6MGa73eMUmZHQb1uXSu8AhWQVsm38S4ELB7ViDm/1788113992522.jpg) Yes, we are talking about the original, vanilla 2011 release. I honestly lost track of how many hours—or rather, weeks—I poured into this game back in the day. It felt like a world that simply never ended. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYfQA5WiBdpQTsscGfNtssUxyK1QPpmwH482rXLowHgc5/1788113992667.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVpWRJkBiujkUDmPkiLiSLtkyfzsHFeZr3r5Y1bJWj3m1/1788114021823.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmatHdpuJQ2r1Rw9nqYo6H58LBQLZCVWLBJfwUVK33qVXq/1788114022006.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmQd6Puxq1RKJmwbVy9x14oWE3hZAg5fs6eTVsjubH73sr/1788114022262.jpg) Opening up the case, the first thing that caught my attention was the surprisingly thick manual. It takes a considerable number of pages to break down all the core mechanics: alchemy, blacksmithing, cooking, magic, and combat. Even after all these years, reading through those pages reminds me of how deep and immersive those systems felt. It instantly brought back memories of my adventures across the region, from the cozy ambiance of buying and decorating my own houses to the tense fights inside ancient ruins and forgotten caves. # Of course, inside the box I found yet another promotional flyer for *Prey 2*... That makes three of them so far in my collection! They definitely poured a serious budget into marketing that game back then, haha. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX9SHKHJe4u5Ni7EtZhAE39cyhdeFREcGHFwC6LvDZyhF/1788114022385.jpg) However, my absolute favorite detail was the reversible cover art inside the sleeve. While the front features the iconic emblem and the back shows the standard game information, the interior facing the disc displays a breathtaking landscape. It depicts the Dragonborn standing atop a mountain peak, looking out over the snow-capped mountains, vast tundras, winding rivers, and open plains of Skyrim. I had to carefully slip the paper out just to photograph it, because it is truly a beautiful piece of art worth sharing. ---
*Español*

> Continuando con la nostalgia de juegos de generaciones pasadas, el día de hoy les traigo mi copia física de **The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim** para la Xbox 360. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfAXPR5funSa5mLw8xV1qcvDoFhmnzCB1LuUVSJKdev8m/1788114022521.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSGcEh7akD692Ltt81ZmLHjs8AiZaZ4PkYeuFALexfw1e/1788114051498.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeU7YkFmMMeCC7ymGC3G8rqtnneDsJoRmzvm8KnHuX2zi/1788114051642.jpg) Sí, la versión vanilla original de por allá del lejano 2011. Sinceramente no sé cuántas horas —o mejor dicho, semanas— le invertí a este título en su momento; era una aventura que simplemente sentías que nunca se acababa. # Al abrir el estuche, lo primero que me llamó la atención fue el manual impreso, el cual tiene un grosor de páginas bastante considerable. En él explicaban en detalle las mecánicas de alquimia, herrería, cocina, magia, combate y todas las posibilidades que ofrecía el mundo. A pesar de todos los años que han transcurrido, me sigue pareciendo una cantidad enorme de sistemas inmersivos que me hacen recordar todas las experiencias vividas: desde la calidez de comprar y equipar tus propias casas hasta los encarnizados combates en cuevas y mazmorras antiguas. # ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc2ZYwXLeAzeuRYPXrfRVvUxovzfiL2Vs1tnBeiHYSuiL/1788114051777.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYcSuwtALyj7JrtuTZotfJZ4Vu88pkeroy83m6WU9daWk/1788114051919.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUUaoTTf87srZJmXyEnPXVEeBPX3kToV1DhhVeGEKz3PS/1788114052074.jpg) ![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRu5DomBis5GJ9VukbvFunwFYPZc7TTNwMtT81aSEbUkw/1788114065239.jpg) Además, dentro del estuche encontré otro folleto publicitario de *Prey 2*... ¡Este ya es el tercero que me topo en la colección! Definitivamente le invirtieron una buena suma a la publicidad de ese proyecto en su época, jajaja. # Finalmente, el detalle que más me fascinó fue la lámina decorativa reversible de la portada. Mientras que por fuera muestra el diseño clásico de la caja con la información del juego, el reverso que queda de cara al disco es una ilustración impresionante del Sangre de Dragón en la cima de una montaña, contemplando los picos nevados, las tundras, los ríos y los paisajes de la región de Skyrim. Tuve que sacar la carátula con cuidado para fotografiarla porque de verdad es hermosa y vale totalmente la pena compartirla por aquí. ---
| *From my infinite humbleness... / Desde mi infinita humildad...* | | :---: | | @noxys |

body.body: >\nPoslední srpnový týden se vydařil. Bude dlouhý výlet s ATV :-)\n

> The last week of August was a success. It will be a long trip with ATW :-) --- ---
**Welcome to the evaluation of the sixteenth round of the seventh annual photo contest for all Hive users Vítejte u vyhodnocení šestnáctého kola sedmého ročníku fotografické soutěže pro všechny uživatele Hive**

𝓐𝓻𝓸𝓾𝓷𝓭 𝓣𝓱𝓮 𝓦𝓸𝓻𝓵𝓭

--- ---
>\nSedm fotografií, sedm zastávek na našem nedělním výletu s ATW. 5 * Evropa a 2 * USA\n

> Seven photos, seven stops on our Sunday trip with ATW. 5 in Europe and 2 in the USA
[ ![mapa16-7a.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23wqnoKCaa1NDpAeB5HzpkzcrFchFDaTycVvRQQyYZrRSYdEiRrxTMrzddbw3RbFd3obw.png) ](https://mapy.com/s/cunanafoge)
>\nCelkem vyrovnané hlasování v anketě nerozhodlo o hlavní ceně. Jasno udělalo hlasování na discordu.\n

> The overall even voting in the poll did not decide the main prize. The vote on Discord made it clear.
![anketa16-7.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/Ep7zqZnxPZtTakqVKrq2uKEmUDGVwTQBHxABPf8PeSyRAV39CDTM5DSLG2ho4q5i51z.png) *discord* Covered bridge – 1 Entrance to the castle – 2 Goblin Valley State Park – 3 Krupajsko vrelo (Krupaj spring) – 1 Loket castle – 2 Mount Allison – 3 Sculpture – 1
---

> Klasická připomínka:
Všechny soutěžní fotografie odkazují na původní články autorů fotografií.

> Classic reminder:
All competition photos link to the original articles of the authors of the photos. ---
![linka1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23swXQgUNzHCUaoqVQ7xJsMWUUjSApjCzgkGyzcvzGpiGuHbnAkuDqrzatb2oYeGtHJ15.png)

> Historické stavby v České republice mají ve světě dobrý ohlas. Tak se na některé podíváme.

Začneme v Lokti nad Ohří v Karlovarském kraji. @wahaceggy nás pozval obdivovat královský hrad Loket. Fotografie získala druhou cenu.

> Historical buildings in the Czech Republic have a good reputation in the world. Let's take a look at some of them.

We'll start in Loket nad Ohří in the Karlovy Vary region. @wahaceggy invited us to admire the royal castle of Loket. The photo won second prize.
[ ![wahaceggy16-7.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/EptZyBV7JdmVW119ejhGS9k5kvMFLf5fLQmSvuBJV3J1EZVuP1Lt1ZzR4cfbBjtmE7w.jpg) ](https://peakd.com/@wahaceggy/lkt-mt2ks76j-wgl4t1au)
---
>\nDruhou stavbou je, nám už známý, zámek Horšovský Týn. @krakonos nám nabídl pohled na vstup z náměstí města. Fotografie získala třetí cenu.\n

> The second building is the already familiar Horšovský Týn castle (Plzeň region). @krakonos offered us a view of the entrance from the town square. The photo won third prize.
[ ![krakonos16-7.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/243BixUyanzDEV3Uy1r9dRE6KCgUydpfnpQC6hATUDrvkuNz1PBToqNDNtz3fKvF7JS3y.jpeg) ](https://peakd.com/@krakonos/actifit-krakonos-20260828t162823512z)
---
>\n@cezary-io „opustil“ svůj oblíbený Osterley Park a přesunul se do Kew Gardes v Londýně. Nabídl nám pohled na zajímavou plastiku uprostřed zeleně. Fotografie získala druhou cenu.\n

his favorite Osterley Park and moved to Kew Gardens in London (UK). He offered us a view of an interesting sculpture in the middle of greenery. The photo won second prize.
[ ![cezary-io16-7.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23tm6rxCEJWvs9FkNvPuG37B1HiYKy5L8fkDwXEaA4ZGJD6bJ2Ymbtqprr4H68JnC6fix.jpeg) ](https://peakd.com/@cezary-io/actifit-cezary-io-20260825t192546776z)
---
>\nPohádkoví trpaslíci mohou vypadat všelijak :-). Třeba jako ti v Goblin Valley State Park v Utahu. @klub-wloczykijow tak pokračuje v pozvánkách na jihozápad USA. Fotografie získala první cenu.\n

>\n@manuvert doesn't show up much in our competition. But this time he really \

with a photo from the west coast of the USA. Mount Allison near Fremont, California looks like it was painted :-). The photo won a special prize with the right to participate in the additional competition for the best photo of the month of August.

---

[ ![suzana72-16-7.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23wC5VZRDRvnAvRVEobTg3B41kg9LNP9tXkakXkRakhDvhNEvnQbWRM3DXqAprcyxWGbi.jpeg) ](https://peakd.com/hive-184437/@suzana72/krupaj-spring)

> Our last stop is Kolárovo. They have the longest wooden covered bridge in Slovakia. @hairyfairy invited us here. The photo received a prize for participating in the competition.
[ ![hairyfairy16.7.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23wqg3q1749QyfS1yKc5iQuX2LToTpSGWzazvhUjvQEE7M9mtydcCfZdA3WFn84kUs232.jpeg) ](https://peakd.com/hive-184437/@hairyfairy/vylety-z-jihoslovenskych-termalu-not-only-extraordinary-mill-in-south-slovakia)
--- ---
>\nMyslím, že poslední srpnový nedělní výlet s ATW vám nabídl pestrou paletu zajímavých míst. Bude to tak i příště?\n

> I think that last Sunday trip with ATW in August offered you a wide variety of interesting places. Will it be the same next time? ---

> Než se rozloučíme,
zbývá už jen rozdat ceny za vítězné fotografie,

> Before we part,
all that remains is to give away the prizes for the winning photos,
![p1.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/bucipuci/23t8CSPFBxuJiwgVCqmoyULtjHpadw1VqMKLVU62R2k3BPiCSZpVfttLEAHxHJBnVCseq.png)

> thank the authors of the photos for inviting them to interesting places, congratulate the winners and also thank the jury from discord: ---

body.body: >Hello everyone! 👋😊 Today I want to share another one of my digital illustrations created in **Adobe Illustrator**. 💻🎨 This time, I designed an adorable **Kawaii-style character** with a soft and colorful aesthetic. 🥰🌸 For this illustration, I wanted to create a character with a sweet and friendly expression. The big expressive eyes, rosy cheeks, brown hair, and small details around the character help give the design more personality. 👀💕✨

/>

One of my favorite elements is the cute **white cat sitting on top of her head**. 🐱🤍 I think this detail adds a fun and unique touch to the illustration and makes the character feel even more charming.

I also combined different colors in the outfit, including pink, blue, and darker tones, to create contrast while maintaining the soft Kawaii style. 🎀💙🩷

Creating these illustrations in Illustrator allows me to continue practicing different aspects of digital design, especially working with **vector shapes, outlines, colors, expressions, and character details**. Every new design is an opportunity to learn something new and improve my creative process. ✨

🛠️ **Software:** Adobe Illustrator  
🎨 **Style:** Kawaii / Manga  
💻 **Type:** Vector Digital Illustration  
🐱 **Special detail:** A cute cat on her head 🤍

I hope you like this new design as much as I enjoyed creating it! 😊🎨

What do you think about the little cat on top of her head? 🐱😂💕 I would love to read your opinion in the comments! 👇✨

* * *

<h1 style=\

>
¡Hola a todos! 👋😊 Hoy quiero compartir con ustedes otra de mis ilustraciones digitales creada en **Adobe Illustrator**. 💻🎨 En esta ocasión diseñé un adorable personaje con un estilo **Kawaii**, lleno de colores suaves y pequeños detalles. 🥰🌸 Para esta ilustración quería crear un personaje con una expresión dulce y amigable. Los grandes ojos expresivos, los cachetes sonrojados, el cabello castaño y los pequeños detalles alrededor del personaje ayudan a darle mucha más personalidad al diseño. 👀💕✨

/>

Uno de mis elementos favoritos es el adorable **gatito blanco que está sentado sobre su cabeza**. 🐱🤍 Creo que este pequeño detalle le da un toque divertido y diferente a la ilustración, haciendo que el personaje tenga aún más encanto.

También combiné diferentes colores en su vestuario, incluyendo tonos rosados, azules y colores más oscuros, para crear contraste sin perder la estética suave y tierna del estilo Kawaii. 🎀💙🩷

Crear este tipo de ilustraciones en Illustrator me permite seguir practicando diferentes aspectos del diseño digital, especialmente el trabajo con **formas vectoriales, contornos, colores, expresiones y detalles de personajes**. Cada nuevo diseño es una oportunidad para aprender algo diferente y seguir mejorando mi proceso creativo. ✨🎨

🛠️ **Programa utilizado:** Adobe Illustrator  
🎨 **Estilo:** Kawaii / Manga  
💻 **Tipo de trabajo:** Ilustración digital vectorial  
🐱 **Detalle especial:** ¡Un adorable gatito sobre su cabeza! 🤍

¡Espero que les guste este nuevo diseño tanto como a mí me gustó crearlo! 😊🎨

¿Qué opinan del pequeño gatito sobre su cabeza? 🐱😂💕 ¡Me encantaría leer sus opiniones en los comentarios! 👇✨

body.body:
People have been suggesting for ages that part of the growing mental health struggles for many is the disconnect between their own reality and comparing it to the curated images of perfection others project in social media. I worry about the world my nieces and nephew are growing into. It was bad enough when legacy media was the main media. The internet and its attention economy absolutely have a dark side.

A bad analogy: if I only post pictures of my Friend-Shaped Car after a trip through the car wash, and after photoshopping out paint chips, and never mention the real work it takes to keep it running, you have a false picture of my car, and it might make your lived automotive reality seem more burdensome than it is. And if everyone is posting these carefully-curated car pictures, you get a false impression that you can never measure up.

body.title: Una pequeña planta de acorazonada formándose junto a una de guindadera/ A small, heart-shaped plant forming next to a sour cherry sapling[ESP/ENG]
body.body:
![20260829_175520.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmXfk6EfMKEqHKn52LJTaENoaQmFZQ3CEWYaH4w7QqkgyL/20260829_175520.jpg)

Buen dia amigos, espero la estén pasando muy bien, el dia de hoy les hablaré sobre esta pequeña planta de corazón la cual creció en medio de una planta de guindadera.

Son plantas que crecen por medio de bulbos, quizas estaba en ese porron antes que la guindadera, de igual manera anda recuperando terreno.

Que agradable es llegar al jardín y ver estas hermosas plantas formandose, además atraen buenas energías y es lo que gusta.

Siempre me ha encantado la forma de sus hojas, posee un arte espectacular, y puede durar mucho tiempo intacta, solo debemos darle el mejor cuidado.

>Good day, friends; I hope you are all doing well. Today, I’d like to talk to you about this little heart-shaped plant that sprouted right in the middle of a trailing plant.

>These plants grow from bulbs; perhaps it was already in that pot before the trailing plant took hold, but either way, it is reclaiming its space.

>It is so pleasant to come out to the garden and see these beautiful plants taking shape; plus, they attract good energy, which is something I really love.

>I have always adored the shape of its leaves—they possess a spectacular, artistic quality—and the plant can remain intact for a long time, provided we give it the best care.

![20260829_175523.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmagjARn5s3uT56Jkmtj4V7FEKgZ1MNbgDswDTT51Fkh2V/20260829_175523.jpg)

![20260829_175518.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmPDRemX3DBP4aERXKzYND5JP6WXsSwNyLtxAenw3dJytn/20260829_175518.jpg)

A muchas personas les gustaria una de ellas como regalo y es por ello que siempre tengo algunas preparadas en porron. 

Si bien es cierto suelen ser atacadas por gusanos en algunas ciertas épocas del año, los podemos alejar con algunos tratamientos. 

El riego de agua debe ser controlado porque están en porron, debemos asegurarnos de que no se encharque el lugar. 

Teléfono: A20
Bendiciones. 

>Many people would love to receive one of them as a gift, which is why I always keep a few ready in pots.

>Although they are prone to attacks by worms at certain times of the year, we can keep them away with the right treatments.

>Watering must be carefully controlled since they are in pots; we need to ensure that water does not pool around them.

![M74: A Grand Design Spiral](https://apod.nasa.gov/apod/image/2608/m74_hst_960.jpg)

***

>If not the most grand, then this spiral galaxy is at least one of the most photogenic.  An island universe of about 100 billion stars, 32 million light-years away toward the constellation Pisces, M74 presents a gorgeous face-on view.  Classified as an Sc galaxy, the grand design of M74's graceful spiral arms are traced by bright blue star clusters and dark cosmic dust lanes.  Constructed from archival images, this sharp composite is from the Hubble Space Telescope.  Spanning about 30,000 light-years across the face of M74, it includes exposures recording emission from hydrogen atoms, highlighting the reddish glow of the galaxy's large star-forming regions.
