links.title: When Gardening Becomes Overwhelming - by Sunscape
links.body:
![hivegarden-removal-5.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUooEfoneonDob4gMCrzvrxRTMJRycZMZaR75sxQGdSkf/hivegarden-removal-5.jpg)

We grow seedlings, plant them out into the garden, and before we know it, we are ripping it all out.  We put it in, we take it out!  This has to be the first year in my entire life where keeping up with it all has been overwhelming.  Not just for myself, but my hubby has had a rough year between his knee and a shoulder, which both need surgery. 

Needless to say, we are both feeling the pressure of clearing out all the gardens before his knee surgery in a few weeks.


![hivegarden-removal-2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmawL1PFR3iknpBBFHNhDChdCMcMv6Gi4RwY4Uv1MyhBTc/hivegarden-removal-2.jpg)

Many of the zinnia plants that were hiding the butternut squash needed to be pulled.  Of course, the squash and melons growing behind them were full of powdery mildew, so those got pulled too.

![hivegarden-removal-4.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQ8FVCzxhL1JowiCeDN8vkk5fYCQv7iTdPxPePFmgnUHx/hivegarden-removal-4.jpg)

All the summer phlox was past peak as well. We cut all those in the front of the house back for the season.  They need dividing before winter since they have literally taken over a large portion of the garden. Mika is on point, supervising the entire job. It isn't often that she gets to be out in the front yard.  

![hivegarden-removal-3.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSTdnk2HLDV7u3LcuBZSkGccf66DUmjvk8zFPcE35rvTr/hivegarden-removal-3.jpg)

All the vines have been removed, and I can see the border zinnias again.  


![hivegarden-removal-squash.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmT9mzRrnmGv6md3Eza6TV63u85DDBAZgZMPMDsMgkyqLN/hivegarden-removal-squash.jpg)

All that is left is to pull the tall zinnia plants in two weeks.  I want to save them for the bees and goldfinches, which are still actively enjoying the flowers.


![hivegarden-removal-8.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmRU8JtG1EdG9cfDPwQdLYsd8cLx6zU7yj6WMpbNnUoJey/hivegarden-removal-8.jpg)

For over 18 years, I have had Ostrich Ferns planted along the North side of the house, surrounding the back porch.  I have truly loved the way they look all summer long, but when I feel like taking care of all the gardens is getting to be too much, I make radical decisions.  Thus, I had hubby dig out every one of the ferns.


![hivegarden-removal-7.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcKzJ3ao7h8bWiTiXnVSyJZWFyPfTaAnxf3AuSN5xpp98/hivegarden-removal-7.jpg)

It took most of the morning to remove all of them.  I don't know what I will do with all the empty space, but at least it is a lot less for us to cut back every fall. 


![hivegarden-removal-9.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmSEhymqe7Ci3WQWsSgwLMwYaez9nZdaNZEvbemNSfrcgR/hivegarden-removal-9.jpg)

We ended up filling up that barrel four times that day.  There were others planted in shady spots that came out too.  It was a hard choice for me to make, but less is better as we age, right?


![IMG_7854.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmWCo2WkqsW92AtkravT6JMDiq8Xe2JV2DDafjALX5wuVG/IMG_7854.JPG)

A major decision was made to eliminate this enormous garden where all my lilac trees and shrubs have been growing for years.  Neither of us can keep up with all the weeds that grow in there among the ground cover.  


![IMG_7855.JPG](https://images.hive.blog/DQmaFGhpeBMThxikC1wNCdmuqEtdJsupYQx2ZZAza4Mf68L/IMG_7855.JPG)
My husband had been working on digging out weeds for three weeks when I made the suggestion that having to do that every year was going to be too much going forward. 

The first step was to clear away all the boulders surrounding the entire garden. We put them all in when we were younger and much stronger than now.  See, we put it in, and we take it out. 

![hivegarden-removal-16.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmZjNF6v8hfLJk46Yfhr94LaKMu89QQ8KLAkCzJBDGZcrK/hivegarden-removal-16.jpg)

At first, I thought I would keep the Korean Lilac and the bird post, making a small circular bed around them.  The more we worked on removing everything, the more I realized that they had to go too. So sad.


![hivegarden-removal-c.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcYNPD67RyoMCYEAhp7wFxiqwxdsDeiCgyZRiLZZ1fxFv/hivegarden-removal-c.jpg)

It looks so strange now that all the trees and shrubs have been cut down.  More rocks have to be removed; that will be done over the next two weeks.

![hivegarden-removal-20.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUY4EP84eaXgJ8H7YAdgJGckJY2BuZfqq8uFMskFBsVNv/hivegarden-removal-20.jpg)

I know I am going to miss the wonderful aroma from the lilacs when spring rolls around.  Yet, I know we made the right decision to remove the entire garden.  Now, we have to find a contractor to come in with a bobcat to remove all the soil and stumps.   In the spring, we will sow grass seed and turn it back into a lawn.

I've been contemplating what I would be able to handle alone if and when my husband transitions.  He is 10 years older than I am, and his physical strength has been diminishing for the past two years.  I can see how hard it is for him to do so much gardening. Thus, we are both overwhelmed, emotionally, physically, and mentally too. 

I am seeing clearly that \

.  


![banner-sunscape-2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmYr3stqM7yx8cpipf8v6F4YgkM2aD282NSQrGYzJZqCxE/banner-sunscape-2.jpg)


![banner-f.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmUHeye11LMUAaCybY2N9bYWHirMNK8Zk9M9c5LLsfBB6M/banner-f.png)

links.title: Fleurs-plantes sechées
links.body:
![3FCDD391-D70A-40E7-B1C5-49928AC20213_1_105_c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/AKCGKHKeLrsYJop1tT1gNRaHF5Uo5t35ZGduQWjVMdFLhmcHSYY8atd8zxQd1n4.jpeg)
Na weken verzamelen en drogen was het dit weekeinde eindelijk zover: ik ben gestart met het maken van het droog-bloemstuk voor op de grote eettafel. De takjes had ik al wat voorbereid en zoveel als mogelijk van stekels en doorns ontdaan. Alles klaargelegd en voor de zekerheid nog even het filmpje bekeken wat ik van (bloemist) Iris heb gemaakt in Le Phaux, waar ze uitleg gaf hoe zo'n tafelstuk op te bouwen.

![EBEDB06B-6931-4D75-A295-D5CD89C2D7DE_1_105_c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/EokdeDYA71gLZN2dpvDHygPS9ybyenfX22QqYY5uryAWdPqsv4sp53fukN2Bx7r5CVc.jpeg)
Je moet dus beginnen met het grijze steekschuim weg te werken. Dat heb ik als eerste met mos bekleed en dat met krammetjes vastgezet. Vervolgens onderaan allerlei blad geprikt, en daar leerde ik meteen dat je dat met droogbloemen/planten heel voorzichtig moet doen, want voor je het weet knakt het takje of breekt er een blaadje af. Bovenop heb ik de gedroogde hortensias uit de tuin naast elkaar geplaatst, omdat die een goeie basis geven om de rest in te steken.

Onze eettafel is nogal groot, dus kon het stuk ook wel wat 'lengte' krijgen, daarvoor heb ik grote donkerroodpaarse gedroogde peulen van de -volgens mij- acacia gebruikt. Dat was nog niet eenvoudig om die door het mos en in het steekschuim te krijgen, met een mes heb ik maar even geholpen om een snede te maken. Die peulen zijn heel leuk gedraaid gedroogd, dat geeft bij het stuk een leuke 'schwung'. 

![CC93D201-663A-4D59-B5B6-6E76B0B95CEC_1_105_c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/23x19NhpChTV11FWcTNLNfg8kt9Jr6pwqVDhfkTkrveGskPmUsVt2PQQkF912fnJDkaiZ.jpeg)


Vervolgens dan maar de rest van alle verzamelde takjes voorzichtig erin prikken. Een beetje hier, een beetje daar, merde breekt er toch weer een takje of een blaadje af, ander takje ervoor in de plaats. Zo ben je lekker een tijdje bezig. Af en toe de handschoenen aan, want de blauwe distels, kaardenbollen en katoendistels prikken enorm. Zodra die erin zitten, moet je blijven uitkijken dat je je niet alsnog aan die stekels prikt. Een gevaarlijke bezigheid, haha. 

![2D2269CE-9F9C-4CDE-ADDF-73EBD6915455_1_105_c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/23x196GXWZ3uwT2DT6byGomgwZmZd3Ni4gBxLLkD8uboiVPNAMRrmaN548ymymSb3DXS3.jpeg)

Een van de lessen van Iris was om de takken of bloemen in drievoud of vijfvoud te gebruiken, dat zou voor een mooi evenwicht zorgen. Ondanks dat de zilveren schaal best groot is, kwam ik er al snel achter dat ik het bij drie moest houden. Vijf stuks van alles zou veel te veel zijn!

Op een gegeven moment had ik alle belangrijke takken wel geprikt. Toen bleek dat je nog goed rondom de schaal moet kijken, want er zaten nog best wat open plekjes. Die ben ik als laatste gaan vol steken met de judaspenning.  Et voilá, het resultaat!

![FB7E406C-11B9-4AD4-A803-BAF864FF1834_1_105_c.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/23zGenp3JRN35WiqSQPLAbtP2GPqXwMr7tPFmN9djJ2wTUf5DsMSe6SEMTgj7HGSzmbbT.jpeg)
Ik ben vooral verrast door de enorme hoeveelheid kleur die erin zit! Echt heel blij met het resultaat. Bart gelukkig ook, hij vind het mooi dat zijn mooie zilveren schaal nu gevuld is en nog mooier op tafel staat!


![E94D4F70-7B1B-42A5-859C-FDFBB757BFD1_1_201_a.heic](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/243M9P49FxgeiTsRd1gQSsfsDL3F2rDt7jBdSNijbs9YcdsZj8ggaRVuwpMazCubN3RLb.jpg)
Nadat het grote tafelstuk klaar was, was het nog een behoorlijke bende op tafel. Best nog redelijk wat takken over, dus ook maar meteen een 'jardinière' gevuld. Die is een stuk kleiner en staat naast een muur. Dat brengt weer een andere vormgeving met zich mee. Wat platter aan de achterkant en meer naar de zij- en voorkant uitstekend. Ook die is niet onaardig geworden, toch?

Wat een leuk experiment dit! Het grote enthousiasme van Iris is op mij overgeslagen. Mochten jullie ooit in Maasland zijn, gaan jullie dan een bloemetje bij haar kopen - [Roots Flowers and Plants](https://www.instagram.com/rootsflowersandplants/) - ? Ook nog een bedankje aan Sylvia van Meurs die zo lief was de judaspenning voor mij te plukken. En natuurlijk aan Bart voor zijn geduld met mijn verzamelwoede. Een deel van het huis is weken 'ontploft' geweest met takjes en bladeren die te drogen hingen. Nu is het in de eetkamer in ieder geval weer een beetje aan kant!

#### Hameau du Buisson
![](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/23wMY1Z7r9V725N6zunnWSJVY4T5oJdaSsLNusSsBeLE3VNVQxZ1VSBsVwahTWXLnGBSR)

Gebeurde er nog meer deze week? Jazeker! Afgelopen donderdag zijn we met Hélène en Justine naar de 'Jeudi du Buisson' geweest. Hameau du Buisson is een gehuchtje zo'n tien kilometer de Cevennen in. Via een flink bochtige weg en een paar stevige haarspelden verder ben je dan wel op een prachtige plek met fraai uitzicht over de bergen, een typisch Cevennens landschap. 

In de zomer organiseren ze iedere donderdag een diner met lokale producten en wijnproeverij van een wijndomein uit de buurt. Je zit er aan grote tafels bij elkaar en het eten wordt in grote schalen opgediend, waarbij je dat met je tafel zelf mag verdelen/uitdelen. Heel gezellig. De foto hierboven is van hun eigen website, want toen wij er waren, was het behoorlijk bewolkt en misschien zou er ook wel wat regen gaan vallen. De wijnproeverij xxxxxxxx 
We hebben dus niet buiten in de tuin gegeten, maar in de feestzaal binnen. We hebben lekker met Hélène en Justine bijgekletst, aten zoete uientaart met goed gevulde salade, een heerlijke saucisse -worst- die in spiraalvorm was gebakken met aligot en toe een mirabellen-myrtille crumble. Miam miam, zeggen ze hier, niet mjam mjam zoals wij in NL zeggen. 

Bart had het met Justine over zijn glas-in-lood werk en daar was ze heel enthousiast over. In haar huis heeft ze een raampje waar ze iets van glas in lood zou willen hebben. Daar gaat ze nu over nadenken, Bart heeft aangeboden haar te helpen of les te geven als ze het zelf zou willen maken. Vrijdag is ze meteen na de markt even langsgekomen om ons atelier te bewonderen. 


#### Portes de Sintipo
![porte-sthippo-1.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/AKU6VsPGyA6tpaBPaTutpd4R9gc2M4WnNo1LJhP9Xry18nw5gqmsyEAALA3xTKH.jpeg)
Bart maakte deze week nog veel meer tekeningen van deuren in Sintipo. Wil je ze allemaal zien, kijk dan in de [NFTshowroom van Bart](https://nftshowroom.com/bartman67/gallery). 

En ik ben de laatste paar keer gaan zwemmen - morgen sluit het zwembad helaas al weer -. 
![porte-sthippo-2.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/AKchui3HXKgkw6VPvX5eDpr9MPuFKhQK4qbkYnCzTLVCsCMdsYySXoghV8h7MRd.jpeg)
Zaterdag was het 'forum des associations' in Sintipo, dat is de dag waar alle verenigingen van het dorp zich presenteren in de sporthal. Je kan je daar voor nieuwe sporten of hobbies gaan inschrijven. Jaarlijks terugkerend festijn is de inschrijving voor de gym: daar staat 's ochtends vroeg al een lange rij om in te schrijven, zelfs al voordat het Forum officieel is geopend. Die lange rij heeft ook wel wat gezelligs, je staat met je buren in de rij te kletsen en zo leerde ik een leuke dame kennen die de naam Neige heeft (= sneeuw). 

![porte-sthippo-3.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/marjoleinsch/AKuvjpnEWyTW7PREqUyVcaik2AqmhZZuibDpjzRQaBNQt4qq7MoaZrjF5c7jXV3.jpeg)
Na het Forum bij de Pradet met Jeannet -hee, dat rijmt- nog een koffie gedronken en even bijgekletst. 's Avonds aten we de fameuze 'Régis-pizza'. En vandaag... lekker rustig thuis en niks.

body.title: sproing is sprunging
body.body: There was a nice bout of sun and warmer temperatures and the plants that wake up or start serious new growth when the weather is warmer started stirring.\n\n<div class=\

/> The jasmine smells awesome by the way. And then along came a REALLY cold snap that was so cold that JJ declared it was the coldest he's ever been when walking the dog and that he saw frost on cars and the road and grass was \

, and two of our four young chickens died :<

![young chickens looking for bugs in newly raked soil](https://technonaturalist.net/blog/2026/08/sproing-is-sprunging/young-chickens_hu_9a3a2fac608381cd.avif)

The ones no longer with us are Mosaic (bottom-most of the three near the fence) and Pearl (mostly white).

I kind of rattled off insulation plans in JJ's general direction and he \

all of them, the cheapest option we could think of was stringing up some cardboard over the door to cut down the wind chill.  Later that same day JJ came back and said he suspected that it had always been fine before because the jasmine plant and two passionfruit plants had completely covered the coop before so there was a lot of protection from the elements.  Some time back our neighbour accidentally killed a large part of the jasmine on the fence while cleaning up (they did apologise, they hadn't meant to kill it) and we were glad to find out the following growing season that the bit over the chicken coop had somehow survived, and more recently JJ pulled out the mature passionfruits as they had stopped fruiting and replaced them.  So we're hoping by next winter all the new/regrowing plants will have grown enough cover over the chicken coop and no more freezing winters, though we will still need to consider stopgap measures for the next time he decides that the passionfruits need to be replaced again.

The Calathea that I transplanted into the tree bed is still hanging on by a single leaf but it's not dead yet.

![Calathea hanging on by a leaf](https://technonaturalist.net/blog/2026/08/sproing-is-sprunging/calathea-leaf_hu_ff430d3c0a085dfd.avif)

The phoenix Hypoestes is rising from the corpse of its predecessor (or putting on new growth I haven't figured out which way that went yet).

![Hyoestes that grew out of a rotting Hypoestes](https://technonaturalist.net/blog/2026/08/sproing-is-sprunging/phoenix-hypoestes_hu_773988fd3d0a02a8.avif)

I found more bugs!

<div class=\

/> The camera did not want to focus on the ladybugs and I have no idea what the caterpillar is. I think that one is the same one grown a little bigger and not that far away in the insect patch chewing on a plant I had been uncertain about pulling or not. Also that lavender decided to flower, it did not have any when we bought and planted it. Speaking of the insect patch, it's still going good. It would not surprise me in the slightest if every single seed I threw in that area had actually come up. ![plants in insect patch](https://technonaturalist.net/blog/2026/08/sproing-is-sprunging/insect-patch_hu_82f824f98356ae80.avif) And not much longer after I took that photo I found flowers!
/> Unlike the chicken forage patch where I think some grass is struggling up and I can't tell if some other sprouts are \

(some have been at least loosely identified as wild lettuce, chickweed and four-leaved allseed) or stuff I planted.  I transplanted some of the surprisingly numerous chickweed into it, two of them had all their leaves eaten probably by caterpillars and one shrivelled up like it was too dry but they otherwise seem to be doing alright.

I'm really getting on JJ's case about transplating the not-sunflowers as they need to go in before the nasturtiums get moved.  I get that there is a correct time to be doing it even though we are doubtful that the poor things will survive the transplant but the situation with the nasturtiums and the aloe vera is beyond ridiculous.

![nasturtiums have completely swamped the aloe vera patch](https://technonaturalist.net/blog/2026/08/sproing-is-sprunging/swarming-nasturtium_hu_d9f02cd9038d3401.avif)

At least their flowers complement I guess.

<div class=\

/> He eventually started after it looked like spring was definitely springing and weeded the sleeper bed before transplanting some of the aloes into pots and beginning the transfer of the rest of them into the fence bed.

/> I did have a brief moment of HOW YOU PLANT when I saw the first aloe in the fence bed before realising that none of the aloes are straight. I happened to notice that what I thought was more Easter lilies growing in a \
spot (not that random, there was another undefined garden bed somewhere around there once upon a time) in the cottage garden had produced these cute tiny bell flowers.\n\n<div class=\

/> Them not being Easter lilies will explain the lack of giant trumpet flowers at the same time as the actual Easter lilies which would be why I took so long to notice them. PlantNet reckons they're [Summer Snowflakes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Summer_snowflake). Just like the Easter lilies they're horribly dangerous (to dogs, cats, chickens and children if nommed on) so of course I'm going to be moving them to the porch bed as it seems they will survive the occasional roof runoff flooding that's seems to happen when it rains. Now I'm wondering what the tree bed might contain as they still haven't flowered. Right next to the Snowflakes were these daisies. ![some kind of daisy](https://technonaturalist.net/blog/2026/08/sproing-is-sprunging/daisies_hu_a93a96f5dd2576f6.avif) PlantNet very loosely identified them as either [Cotula turbinata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cotula_turbinata) or [Roman Chamomile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roman_chamomile). I visited a friend and noticed she had some in her garden and asked about them and she said they were horrible prickly things that made the lawn horrible and prickly and uncomfortable to walk on barefoot and promptly ripped out the patch that I'd noticed so I guess they're going seeing as the plan is for the cottage garden to be barefoot friendly. They can at least go into the sleeper bed according to the internet. And then there was this thing in the corner which again I only noticed because there were \

bright red flowers.  I had observed it as an unusual grass tussock for a while and as it was conveniently located and not spreading like the rest of the grass I decided it could stay where it was.

![possibly a Chasmanthe aethopica 'cobra lily' - red tubular flowers with grassy leaves](https://technonaturalist.net/blog/2026/08/sproing-is-sprunging/maybe-chasmanthe-aethopica_hu_33691245e16309e6.avif)

The things one finds when actually interested in outside x_x It's maybe a Chasmanthe aethiopica.  Whoever had this house before really liked lilies.  Or maybe just bulbs in general and the more delicate bulbs didn't survive us.

I told J the tree bed must have been celebrating the Dockers season as one of the violas somehow ended up with these immense purple flowers.

<div class=\

/> I tried to take the photo of the purple and white ones at the same distance to show the size comparison of the flowers but it was a very inaccurate judgement as I also had to keep an eye on the chickens who were mowing the lawn at the time. The tomato that JJ had temporarily transplanted into the wall bed and not expected to survive or fruit survived and put out some flowers. ![unexpected tomato flowers](https://technonaturalist.net/blog/2026/08/sproing-is-sprunging/flowering-tomato_hu_6bffea8c72b0416e.avif) And I finally made myself start the gravel path in the food garden.

/> It is going to be improperly done with as much compacting as me tromping on the ground can manage and not a grain of builders sand or weedmat/lining to be seen and the internet reckons I am very definitely going to regret these terrible decisions in a few years' time. The aquaponics plans have been pushed back to next year or the year after as my mum wants to do a massive family holiday to Malaysia next year for a milestone birthday so the aquaponics money went on that instead. ## plans - ⬜ move beehive and birdbath (which is primarily easy water source for the bees) into bee garden - ⬜ replant birdbath pockets - ⏸️ relocate and set up aquaponics properly - ⏸️ two ponds need replacing and we might be getting another one - ⏸️ pvc pipes - ⏸️ shubunkin (5-20 apparently) - ▶️ transplant chickweed to chicken area - ⬜ transplant not-sunflowers to chicken area - ⬜ transplant nasturtiums to chicken area - ⬜ trans/plant sweet potato to chicken area - ▶️ transplant aloe to pots or fence bed - ⬜ dig out tree stumps - ⬜ attempt to transplant the apparently immortal Crapemyrtle to where the bigger tree stump was - ⬜ make seed mix out of creeping thyme, kidney weed and white star creeper and go ham - ⬜ separate Easter lilies, replant big bulbs and whatever smaller bulbs will fit, cure some small bulbs for friend that requested some - ⬜ dig up whatever the hell is coming up in the tree bed and transplant ~~to Easter lily patch~~ wherever is appropriate - ⬜ replace all ice cream containers and buckets with bird bath dishes ### side quests - ⬜ desktop aquaponics - ⬜ Youngest's old fish tank setup - ⬜ really small dwc raft or materials to make one OR modified planter for constant flow system as suggested by J - ⬜ heater - ⬜ betta - ⬜ see where neighbour got shrimp and snails from or if they have a population excess to rehome

body.title: Together Let's Defeat The Child Marriage Prevention Act Of 2026!
body.body: ![Jackelberry is the author of this image/Source: Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2014/10/07/16/24/us-capitol-477987_1280.jpg) This past evening I was watching a video on YouTube that criticized Dr. Jordan Peterson for pressuring American men to get married and start a family. The video mostly made sense, because I don't believe that anyone should get married and start a family by a certain age because of societal pressures. Below is that same video. The Institutions Of Family And Marriage Have Run The Dangerous Risk Of Becoming Mere Elitist Social Conventions Here In The United States https://youtu.be/wDEVmBSpkLQ?si=CevgDSLIiadf_08I Where I do have a problem with this video is when the male voiceover demonizes people having gotten married at 13 years old in years past. I don't think anyone should be getting married and starting a family by any kind of deadline. However, by the same token, I don't condone government overreach to prevent teenagers from getting married before they're legally old enough to vote either. Ladies and gentlemen? This topic has me extremely angry. Only two days after I published my article titled \

a Democrat Congresswoman named Gwen Moore from Wisconsin introduced the Child Marriage Prevention Act of 2026 to the Congress.  She did so with the support of U.S. House Representative Danny Davis of Illinois as well as U.S. House Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi of Wisconsin.  (Is Mr. Krishnamoothi even an American?)

Luckily, the American Civil Liberties Union is fighting against this same bill tooth and nail.  None of the Republican delegates in the United States House of Representatives are supporting it.  However, we have to remember that the national mid-term elections are coming up this November.  Therefore, I am depending on all of you to do whatever you have to do to get this same bill defeated before it has a chance to cause damage.

I don't know much about Ms. Moore, Mr. Davis, or Mr. Krishnamoorthi; but if you live in Wisconsin, then you need to vote Ms. Moore and Mr. Kirshnamoorthi out of office.  If you live in Illinois, you need to vote Mr. Davis out of office.

Now, don't get me wrong.  I don't like the adverse impact that the One Big, Beautiful Bill is going to have on our public healthcare system here in the United States once it goes into full effect next year.  The Republicans on Capitol Hill made sure that that same bill got to President Donald J. Trump's desk so that he could sign it into law.

Nevertheless, the Child Marriage Prevention Act of 2026 must never be signed into law or all chaos is going to break loose.  It's not specifically to stop small children under 11 years of age from getting married.  It's waging war against teenage sex and attempting to remove the legality from teenage sex.  For those same reasons, I will likely be voting for all Republican candidates in the national mid-term elections here in the United States

A similar bill is currently on its way to California Governor Gavin Newsome for approval, and already I can sense the dramatic spike in cop killers in the Golden State if that bill ever gets signed into law.  That same state jurisdiction is already experiencing a problem with the police maintaining law and order there.

Fraidy Reiss of Unchained At Last is a misandrist, and she is dead set on ensuring that American men of all ages get needlessly locked up in prison for one reason or another.  She has no sons, so she doesn't care what happens to these men.  She believes that every man who disagrees with her is a \
Wow!  How her kind absolutely love that same word \
\n\nWhen hotheaded self-appointed child advocates and the likes throw around words like \
and the likes, you have to question whether these individuals have looked up the real definition of those terms in the Fifth Edition of the *Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders* (\

) or if these same people even know what that publication is. It makes it no mystery that our nation has a 21 percent illiteracy rate and that 54 percent of Americans read below the third grade level. I've already read this same bill, and it contains the same garbage that the Child Marriage Prevention Act of 2024 contained. If you want to read it yourself, here is the **[link](https://www.congress.gov/bill/119th-congress/house-bill/9758/text/ih)** to it. Because the Tahirih Justice Center crafted this same bill, they should be stripped of their Federal tax exemption status under 26 U.S.C. § 501(c)(3), because they are not supposed to participate in legislation according to that same statutory code. I'm not going to go into all the nitty-gritty about this same bill. I did so in my article about the 2024 version of it; so if you want to delve into the nitty-gritty, you're free to read that same article of mine. What I'm going to do is elaborate on some of my strong concerns about it instead. ## 1.  Courtney Stodden's Involvement In Legislation Against Teenage Marriage Recently I came across a video in which Courtney Stodden is launching some kind of campaign against underage marriage. I think that she is making a big mistake in doing so. Whether or not a teenager can legally get married in our nation before they're old enough to vote in an election should not be up to the elected officials of our nation but rather the decision of voters. I am completely on board with elected officials introducing referendums to the voters to decide this matter on a state level, but I don't approve of government overreach. I also don't condone our Federal government infringing upon the sovereignty of our state jurisdictions. As for Ms. Stodden's allegedly topsy-turvy marriage to an older man when she was 16 years old, let me say that there are two sides to every story. Therefore, I believe that her ex-husband Doug Hutchison should also be heard. The late Nelly Rivas was 14 years old when she fell in love with the late Argentine president Juan Perón, who was in his late fifties, and vice versa back in the 1950s, and she had no problem with him. Then again, they never had the opportunity to marry each other because of detrimental political events in their nation. In any event, here is the video below of Ms. Stodden speaking to the nation. She is opening herself up to major problems by trusting men-hating radical feminists like Fraidy Reiss of Unchained At Last and Jeanne Smoot of the Tahirih Justice Center. I honestly do not believe that Mr. Hutchison manipulated her or harmed her in any manner. Courtney Stodden Has Gotten Involved In Activism To Impose A Blanket Ban On Juveniles Getting Married https://youtu.be/Iqt4C8c7pBg?si=PuoKmKxH5ASaDo3Z I believe that it is a double standard that in certain states like New York, a 16- and 17-year-old minor can be tried as an adult for a crime or even automatically gets tried as one, whereas they cannot legally marry until the age of 18 in that same state jurisdiction. It's as though law-enforcement officials love these double standards in our state laws so that they can have their cake and eat it too. For these reasons, people are losing trust in the police and others like them. Of course, all the men-hating misandrists came out of the woodwork in the video above and insulted and belittled Mr. Hutchison. Then, of course, if their 15-year-old sons go running around their neighborhoods, getting every 12- and 13-year-old girl pregnant and mistreating them, their favorite line is, \

Sorry, Ms. Stodden, but I will not buy into the crap that considers teenage sex to be a form of child molestation.  Once the Child Marriage Prevention Act of 2026 becomes a law, our nation is going to be taking itself back to the days of the Salem witch trials; and there will be no coming back from that vortex.

If you have followed me for a long time here on this same writing platform, you'll likely notice that I've published articles about Ms. Stodden and Mr. Hutchison back when their marriage was going smoothly and they were defending it against the harsh criticism of all the little minds that wish to absorb everyone into their make-believe world of age-appropriate perfection and wholesome purity.

Chris Hansen is not a hero or any kind of guru.  He's a criminal, a cult leader, and a dangerous influencer who wants to pull our entire nation downward to its final destruction.  Now, because of him, there are copycats who are domestic terrorists at best.  Of course, that's another article for another time.

The problem I'm having with Ms. Stodden's use of the term \

and the likes is that that same word has been given so many different definitions that it is difficult to take it seriously anymore. The fact of the matter is that Ms. Stodden and Mr. Hutchison were subjected to many social pressures after they tied the knot a little over a decade ago, whereas Bo Derek and John Derek didn't confront those same social pressures when they tied the knot years before then. They couldn't handle the social pressures, and it destroyed their marriage. My response to Kelley L. Carter's remark about people feeling cringy about Ms. Stodden's marriage to Mr. Hutchison is that those people obviously have deep-seated insecurities about their own sexuality. I would much prefer to have Mr. Hutchison as my next-door neighbor than Levi Johnston, because if anyone is a pervert, it's Levi Johnston rather than Mr. Hutchison. The fact of the matter is these crusaders against teenage marriage sparked by their war on sex are gradually turning our nation into a maximum security prison. It's going to get to the point that we will be voting to elect a prison warden every four years to occupy the White House instead of a president if we let these radical feminists gain full control over our domestic policies. ## 2.  Proof In The Pudding Against Legislation For A Blanket Ban Of Marriage Before Age 18 One night as I was viewing various YouTube videos, I came across one very interesting video from a woman named Susie Rempel. She became pregnant at the age of 13 and had a baby at 14 years old. How old was her boyfriend when she became pregnant? He was 18 years old. Yes, you got it. She was 13 years old and he was 18 years old when she became pregnant with his baby. Before I give you any more details about her story, watch her video below. Susie Rempel Describes What It Was Like For Her To Give Birth At The Age Of Fourteen https://youtu.be/kZd0xh0b_lQ?si=5JpHQQkc8YiMjj7r Ms. Rempel is now married to the father of her baby. She is now 18 years old, and I assume that he would be 23 years old. She and her husband are both Mennonites. And, yes, I realize that I am an agnostic, and I don't normally defend religious people; but this young lady deserves to be defended by anyone of any faith or of no faith at all. She's a brave woman. Ms. Rempel currently lives in Texas. I don't know where she was living when she became pregnant with her first child at age 13. After she told her parents about that pregnancy, she discussed with them about getting married to the father of her baby. This point in time would have been after many state jurisdictions had placed a blanket ban on underage marriage. Then again, perhaps she and her husband lived on a compound that was not readily accessible to the state police. The point I wish to make here is that Ms. Rempel's parents could have pressed criminal charges against her husband. Her husband could be sitting in a state correctional facility now, worrying about whether or not he is going to make it into the next day without someone harming him. Nevertheless, Ms. Rempel's parents decided not to bring the authorities into the picture. Instead, they allowed her to marry the father of her firstborn child and build a life with him. Now, three babies later, she and her husband are happily married and have a bright future together. Ms. Rempel's true story in her video above provides all the more reasons why radical feminists like Fraidy Reiss, Jeanne Smoot, and others like them should not be permitted to tamper with our nation's marriage laws pertaining to juveniles and why \

should not be a strict-liability offense.  Shame on Ms. Reiss, Ms. Smoot, Cassandra Levesque, and others like them for threatening couples like Ms. Rempel and her husband with nonsensical sex laws and ridiculous blanket bans on teenage marriage.

The problem with our society is that every time anyone gets wind of a story like that of Ms. Rempel, they get these horrendous images in their heads of people like David Eisenhauer.  If you don't know who he is, he was an 18-year-old man who murdered a 13-year-old girl named Nicole Lovell after he had sexual intercourse with her and she had threatened to out him to the world if he broke off their relationship in light of a pregnancy scare back in 2016.

Radical feminists like Ms. Reiss, Ms. Smoot, and others like them know that they can play on the fears and the insecurities of American people who choose to think the worse of couples in which the girl is 13, 14, or 15 years old and the boyfriend is five or more years older than her.  They know what makes weak-minded people tick, and the prison-industrial complex knows which elected officials they can bribe to push harsh sex laws and unreasonable marriage laws pertaining to juveniles here in our nation.

It doesn't take a rocket scientist to realize what is going on with our society and how elected officials are taking us closer and closer to becoming a Fascist totalitarian police state.  The only thing standing between us and this awful fate is President Trump.  He has the ability to veto the Child Marriage Prevention Bill of 2026, and he should do so.  Of course, he needs for us to contact him and ask him to do so after clicking on this same **[link](https://www.whitehouse.gov/contact/)**.

It is obvious that President Trump doesn't like this same bill.  If enough of us contact him and ask him to veto it, he will likely hear our cries for him to do so.  Of course, after 2028 arrives, we have to prepare ourselves to vote another president into the White House who will stand behind his course of action in that event.  Unfortunately, President Trump will not be able to run for reelection two years from now.  However, he will occupy the White House until January 20, 2029, and that's a good thing.

Also, don't be afraid to write to your elected officials on Capitol Hill and tell them that you want them to vote against this same bill.  If they receive enough letters from those of us who oppose this bill, they will likely take our views into consideration even if they do not share those same views with us.  Remember that they work for us rather than the other way around.

![Efraimstochter is the author of this picture/Source:  Pixabay](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2016/04/12/09/24/hairstyle-1323925_1280.jpg)

## 3.   Final Thoughts

The Child Marriage Prevention Act of 2026, if passed, is not going to improve the quality of life or the public safety here in the United States.  Nobody can convince me that if Susie Rempel's husband had been sent to prison on a statutory-rape conviction five years ago, she and her offspring would have been so much better off than they are now.

It brings to mind a young man named Bobby whom I had met back in college whose parents appeared to have fallen into similar circumstances as Ms. Rempel and her husband, and the non-involvement of the authorities secured him a prosperous life.  That is, his mother was 15 years old and his father was 22 years old when they got married, and I suspect that Bobby's mother was pregnant with Bobby before she and his father got married.

It is those same men that Fraidy Reiss calls \

that end up being good husbands and good fathers to the female teenage juveniles that they marry. Radical feminists like Ms. Reiss are attempting to turn our nation into some kind of prison-loving society. Meanwhile, real victims of sexual abuse can no longer trust the police with their complaints against the people that victimize them. Norman Michael Achin lays down these same facts in his video below. Norman Michael Achin Explains How Americans, Including Sexual Abuse Victims, No Longer Trust Our Criminal Justice System To Protect Them https://youtu.be/BUTKUCYzejY?si=E4Jhkvh2Zln_r3Z1 A spike in statutory-rape arrests because of a ridiculous blanket ban on teenage marriage is going to cause civilians to become further alienated from the police and the criminal justice system itself than they already are, if our president signs the Child Marriage Prevention Act of 2026 into law. This is where we, as Americans, need to stand up against our elected officials and say \

to this same bill. 

When a teenage girl younger than 18 years of age marries an adult man over the age of 21 or even over the age of 18, it is not legalized pedophilia.  Pedophiles are sexually attracted to prepubescent children rather than to teenagers.  Moreover, a pedophile is going to lose interest in their victim after that victims mature beyond their childhood.

There are women in their seventies and eighties that married their noticeably older husbands when they were 13 or 14 years old, and many of these women have positive stories to tell about their marriages.  No radical feminist can take that away from any of them.

Now, I am not a male chauvinist pig.  I want more than anything for my mother and other female members of my family, young and old, to live to see the day that a woman gets elected as president of the United States of America.  However, at the same time, I don't want radical feminists turning our nation into a replica of political oppression, because that is exactly what these women want to do.

Let's stand up to this circus show that has erupted on Capitol Hill.  The Child Marriage Prevention Act of 2026 is not going to serve the greater good here in our nation no matter how attractive it may look to anyone whose marriage before the age of majority to someone older didn't play out as intended.

Radical feminists wish to use this same bill to encourage men to murder one another here in our nation.  Why do I claim this?  I do so, because most police officers are men; and imposing a blanket ban on underage teenage marriage is going to produce a spike in statutory-rape arrests and convictions, which will escalate the number of police officers that get murdered everywhere here in our nation.  How can anyone call this good?

body.title: Visit Spain - Bioparc, València
body.body:
> Hi 👋 ![Visit Spain - Bioparc.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/Ep5pWrh8smJSkTRbgETjEgLUhrVHP1XmASoBEnE6R8HcNMwnrTJ4biCBLYhTKrQ7vR1.jpg) Our family trip to Spain continued with a very different kind of adventure: a full day at Bioparc Valencia, an African themed zoo built right inside the city's beautiful Turia Gardens. This time my wife and son came along for what turned out to be one of the best days of the whole trip.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
A nossa viagem em família por Espanha continuou com um tipo de aventura muito diferente: um dia inteiro no Bioparc Valencia, um jardim zoológico com temática africana construído dentro dos belíssimos Jardins do Turia. Desta vez, a minha mulher e o meu filho vieram connosco para aquele que acabou por ser um dos melhores dias de toda a viagem. ![01.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EpNpNSbEaEk7paodU7WRjXhgwbNcBkhcWeWgGwDG4b7rZNx4G1FRSUkkNTdnHUL6syZ.jpeg) ![002.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EnsZvZvYh9CpoJN2ubVrE1BsZNwwdho2qbDzgQBcZyQ9NH9ATAVXUrffZKqnmaEdcyC.jpeg) Before even reaching the entrance, this huge metal elephant sculpture caught our eye. Standing tall against the clear blue sky, its wood and iron body is a great warm up for what waits inside: a park built entirely around elephants, giraffes and everything else you would expect from an African savanna.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Ainda antes de chegarmos à entrada, esta enorme escultura de elefante em metal chamou a nossa atenção. Erguendo-se imponente contra o céu azul, o seu corpo de madeira e ferro é um ótimo aperitivo para o que nos espera lá dentro: um parque construído inteiramente em torno de elefantes, girafas e tudo o mais que se espera de uma savana africana. ![004.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EprS5FcZ878Jy2G6NME7z1k49on5Z3Q9Vfpb6KUnvGrvHVmb1A6S1hH2T1yNyFcRA8j.jpeg) Once inside, the African savanna area did not disappoint. Huge boulders and a dry looking baobab tree set the scene, and it did not take long before we spotted our first elephants moving calmly between the rocks.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Uma vez lá dentro, a área da savana africana não desiludiu. Enormes rochas e um embondeiro de aspeto seco compunham o cenário, e não demorou muito até avistarmos os nossos primeiros elefantes a moverem-se calmamente entre as rochas. ![005.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EprU7KJ6LJVWu6ega5AEp5tmtgnLvtkKx58w4azouZDnLTm5XDraBRXFstRyrNxdBM3.jpeg) A short walk further and we found ourselves right next to a small herd resting in the shade of that same giant baobab. Seeing them this close, with no bars or fences breaking the view, is exactly what makes Bioparc special.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Uma curta caminhada em frente e encontramo-nos mesmo ao lado de um pequeno rebanho descansando à sombra daquele mesmo embondeiro gigante. Vê-los tão de perto, sem grades ou vedações a interromper a vista, é exatamente o que torna o Bioparc especial. ![006.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/Eo4Az3D4YJzTpnengq4QGqxtXDJMz2nJ4MmUUH85BVJEhkwd8nMRKk856Abxr1CBe9t.jpeg) The paths between exhibits are almost as pretty as the animals themselves. Palm trees and hanging branches line the walkways, so every turn feels like stepping deeper into a different continent.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Os caminhos entre os recintos são quase tão bonitos como os próprios animais. Palmeiras e ramos pendentes ladeiam as passarelas, de modo que cada curva dá a sensação de estar a entrar num continente diferente. ![007.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/Eq9VF2jowDugB5Kv3jz67N1KxjAkW3EwJXz7eg2SkhncwYViFgDL45YaZLKpRZf7nQD.jpeg) From one of the viewpoints we got this wide shot of the open savanna, with an ostrich, a giraffe, small antelope and a few ibises sharing the same grassy hill. It is a huge enclosure and the animals really do roam freely across it.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
De um dos miradouros, conseguimos esta foto panorâmica da savana aberta, com uma avestruz, uma girafa, pequenos antílopes e alguns íbis a partilhar a mesma colina relvada. É um recinto enorme e os animais circulam realmente livremente por ele. ![009.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EoeD4UBQqPaiN3NSzuwvNB1Qf37K9NJZvzfrgpUdTeKjqK1f7k55HBHc9gZxDNC9b4t.jpeg) A little further along, a wooden lookout gave us a closer view over the giraffe area, with the palm trees and thatched roofs of the African village style buildings in the background.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Um pouco mais à frente, um miradouro de madeira proporcionou-nos uma vista mais aproximada da zona das girafas, com as palmeiras e os telhados de palha das construções em estilo de aldeia africana como pano de fundo. ![011.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EogNMXAF7kNYXdabgPZTSwxxM8h34BUQuxCnAdWAEL8tUnDdEcoWTbaRNhxpBQhMLoX.jpeg) One of the most curious corners of the park is this water tank, part of the Kitum Cave area, where fish swim while small rock dwelling mammals move along the far bank. My son pressed his face right against the glass to watch the fish go by.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Um dos cantos mais curiosos do parque é este tanque de água, parte da área da Gruta Kitum, onde os peixes nadam enquanto pequenos mamíferos que vivem nas rochas se movem ao longo da margem oposta. O meu filho encostou a cara ao vidro para observar os peixes a passar. ![012.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EpA2RdSmLuGQgG7YMqxWMU83RLy31KY46VEsqw3PKFyAL2giLgZujfUJS4gfiWkAmM9.jpeg) More palm lined paths took us further into the park, with a pair of ducks resting by one of the many little ponds scattered through the reserve.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Mais caminhos ladeados por palmeiras levaram-nos mais para o interior do parque, com um casal de patos a descansar num dos muitos pequenos lagos espalhados pela reserva. ![015.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/Eou7mb5rd8y6NYDr3kDAWtRA2A7GK8Dk62vdqaypPa9ihGKZRo6Npi7fgUv18KTrrvA.jpeg) Overhead, a group of dark ibises rested on the rocks inside one of the aviary areas, half hidden by the trees and the fine netting that keeps the birds safely inside the park.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Em cima, um grupo de íbis-escuros repousava sobre as rochas dentro de uma das áreas do aviário, parcialmente escondidos pelas árvores e pela fina rede que mantém as aves em segurança dentro do parque. ![016.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EpNmzpwnHNLjeW9bLpTuSn4LqpDZnygTeJZXYbvuy9is5z4Hf9ae3QKU9kWFPqH3k7m.jpeg) Looking up through the branches we caught another pair of the same birds, perched high on a rock ledge, enjoying the shade on a hot morning.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Olhando por entre os ramos, avistamos outro casal da mesma ave, empoleirado no cimo de uma saliência rochosa, aproveitando a sombra numa manhã quente. ![017.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EowG4QsnGzWfsB9L4oB15U6C547TCzbLyu1mQXNb5N98TufYQTk9RYfuMacApmtA9y9.jpeg) This cattle egret clearly felt right at home. It landed on the railing next to the restaurant, only a couple of meters from our table, and stayed there long enough for a proper close up.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Esta garça-vaqueira sentiu-se claramente em casa. Ela pousou no corrimão junto ao restaurante, a apenas alguns metros da nossa mesa, e ficou lá o tempo suficiente para um close-up perfeito. ![018.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/Eokc5Thw7BWvWHqAMsR6wzumxVrvtQQqxJpw9SmDzxRgcpwCwgutuZYoUzGQtcimaXs.jpeg) Further along the path, hanging vines framed a quiet green clearing scattered with boulders and an old fallen trunk, one of many peaceful corners where the animals can rest away from the main walkways.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Mais adiante no trilho, lianas pendentes emolduravam uma clareira verde e tranquila, salpicada de pedras e um velho tronco caído, um dos muitos recantos pacíficos onde os animais podem descansar longe das vias principais. ![019.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EpNnzcGa9qGjmint47mSHhUBV6PdK12zY2Heg4jBiwSx9Q5MvJLUmFBkrNm4G52cbPi.jpeg) The trail curved past more of the thatched roof buildings that give the whole park its African village feel, with a small group of antelope grazing in the distance.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
O trilho serpenteava por entre mais construções com telhados de colmo, que conferem ao parque um ar de aldeia africana, com um pequeno grupo de antílopes a pastar ao longe. ![020.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EpNoM2CeVc1attaD6NtyZm1omP7X3r3FfTPbdEYgzdmqaFvzCTEDUiQAjcZG28Ub58Y.jpeg) A little closer to the restaurant area, three antelope wandered right across the open grass, completely unbothered by the visitors watching from the path.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Um pouco mais perto da zona do restaurante, três antílopes deambulavam pela relva aberta, completamente alheios aos visitantes que os observavam a partir do trilho. ![021.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EpA2bTiuBUtmJXXA2Ew4JZqLEv6y1XLL7v6FCcWgSh4daKJdnazFtzF3cHiAUpfrTbq.jpeg) Another view of the same winding trail, this time with a couple of ducks strolling along the sandy edge of the pond.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Outra vista do mesmo trilho sinuoso, desta vez com um casal de patos a passear pela margem arenosa do lago. ![022.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EpnDCpubT12LkscN27rARnAUVwrnBnCLDugQVRr86XDTbbe1T4g6YFrZUPWyop1wWkH.jpeg) One of the most striking birds we saw all day was this saddle billed stork, wading along the shoreline with its bright red and black beak reflecting in the water.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Uma das aves mais impressionantes que vimos durante todo o dia foi esta cegonha-de-bico-de-sela, a caminhar pela margem com o seu bico vermelho e preto brilhante a refletir na água. ![023.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EoGxN8755s7ab7RyJ4N96CxPB8bcVeiuASWG92Pf8N1p3cdLD9QEz6rwQBDmC3KnmXF.jpeg) Nearby, a reddish brown buffalo grazed quietly on the sandy ground near its rocky den, keeping mostly to itself under the shade of the trees.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Perto dali, um búfalo castanho-avermelhado pastava tranquilamente no chão arenoso perto da sua toca rochosa, mantendo-se praticamente isolado sob a sombra das árvores. ![025.jpeg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/portugalcoin/EoEpcqL8BhE5rho2nmJDiA441LuXVUscg1nY1hhqQ79k8mtTwLCyouux284zkoiAKbr.jpeg) We ended our visit at the chimpanzee island, watching the group move between the rocks and the little waterfall while other visitors gathered around to do the same. It was the perfect last stop for a day that had already given us so much.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
Terminámos a nossa visita na ilha dos chimpanzés, observando o grupo a movimentar-se entre as rochas e a pequena cascata, enquanto outros visitantes se reuniam para fazer o mesmo. Foi a paragem final perfeita para um dia que já tanto nos tinha proporcionado. Bioparc Valencia turned out to be one of those places that works just as well for a four year old as it does for the adults. My son ran from one enclosure to the next without ever losing interest, and I do not think we have taken this many wildlife photos in a single day in a long time. If you are ever in Valencia with family, this one is well worth the ticket.
PT - Português 🇵🇹
O Bioparc Valencia revelou-se um daqueles locais que agradam tanto a crianças de quatro anos como a adultos. O meu filho correu de um recinto para o outro sem perder o interesse em momento algum, e acho que já há algum tempo que não tirávamos tantas fotografias de animais selvagens num único dia. Se estiver em Valência com a família, vale muito a pena o bilhete. [//]:# (!worldmappin 39.47767 lat -0.41079 long Visit Spain - Bioparc, València d3scr)

body.title: Are Young People Forgetting How to Go Out?
body.body:
I recently listened to this super interesting podcast. A youngster explained the trend in going out. A journalist initially wrote an article. Then decided to speak it out loud as well, for all of us to listen to.

The story background: *A holiday village - Renesse - in the Netherlands.*

A super popular beach village in the southwestern part of my tiny country, the Netherlands. Popular mostly in summer. Vacation destination for teenagers, students and families. A place with many holiday homes, campings, and whatnot. A place where the local entertainment scene thrived in the two months separating school years, in the heart of our summer. Decade(s) ago, many bars and clubs enjoyed peak times.

Today ... One club left.

**One!**

And even on club nights - often enough - only a handful of people show up.

**Where are the people?**

They are around, in town and about. On campings and the beach. But the youngsters stay away from the one club left. Those that took the effort to buy a ticket found themselves on an almost empty dance floor.

The trend is clear, not only in Renesse, but throughout the whole country. A trend I've seen happen firsthand in past years. Since COVID, young people seem to be going out much less to the traditional places where people have been going for the last twenty, thirty years. Perhaps the last fifty to a hundred years.

Bars. Clubs. Discos and Festivals.

**Those places don’t seem to be as attractive anymore.**

She explained that during COVID, young people - school kids in particular - learned something else. They still wanted to meet each other. They still wanted to hang out. They couldn't do this in bars, clubs and at festivals, obviously. Therefore, they learned to gather and enjoy at other spots, whatever those may be. I suppose at home, or in some barn when living outside the city.

What struck me when listening to this young lady. The other reasons she gave for not going out ...

**Efficiency!**

Going out to said places - bars, clubs and festivals - should be efficient! It costs a lot of money these days. True, since COVID it feels like entertainment has been inflated by somewhere between 50 and 100%. \

**But is going out supposed to be efficient?**

\
She speaks the voice of many of her generation. \

, she added.

Are we measuring going out and having fun, with alcohol and/or other substances, against efficiency? Where is the world turning into? Isn't the whole point to be not efficient? To let loose? To forget about our daily lives? To have fun with our friends, acquaintances and strangers? To enjoy?

I'd say, not efficient in terms of productivity, but super efficient for winding down, de-stressing, and gaining the energy to deal with our everyday lives. I even dare to say that going carpe diem mode for an evening, a night, a day (festival), or multiple thereof in places of joy avoids us needing psychologists and therapy sessions. A staggering 70% of youngsters feel depressed, some more, some less. But really? 70%! 7 out of 10. Being efficient has its price, a price these youngsters seem to be willing to pay.

I'm still amazed at how people think. Most think of alcohol hangovers. They can be bad, for sure. So do not drink too much alcohol. If you like the experience of being out-of-the-world, keep the alcohol in the bottle. Take something else. Many 'something elses' give the average person a better experience, a better feeling, without hangovers, or hangovers with a positive feeling instead of the negative ones.

**Phones**

The club owner in Renesse told the journalist: Often when people enter for a night, they do seem to be most interested in talking and their phones. He experimented with the sound. Whenever the music became loud, it is difficult to hear each other; Youngsters switched their attention to their screens, their phones. When he let the technician turn down the sound levels, he noticed the same people getting into conversation mode. Not all; More than some stayed glued to their phone.

The phone, eye, and glue thingy has already led to more clubs forbidding phones on the dance floor. Some even tape the phone cameras when entering the club or festival grounds. One club I've been to even removed people when they were caught more than once using a phone on the dance floor. At least five guards constantly watching the crowd, 400 people max. Whenever a screen lit up, one had to be afraid one of the guards jumping in front and give a warning, at best. Super annoying, such 'stasi'-like approach, but PERFECT in getting the peeps to enjoy the music and each other.

**My advice**

To the young people and all others, for all generations. Find regularly carpe diem mode. Let loose. Enjoy the moment. Forget about everything else. Reload and feel re-energised.

**What do you do to wind down and re-energise?**

body.title: El Cuerpo como Ecosistema: Mi Viaje con el Quiste Sebáceo [Spanish-English]
body.body:
## VERSIÓN EN ESPAÑOL


![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbPgPCh7dx9xsNs584aLiEBTMpgRo6PdYca96tHXSQXxC/1787785825563.jpg)

[Fuente/es.dreamstime.com](https://es.dreamstime.com/el-cuerpo-humano-se-transforma-en-un-ecosistema-de-la-naturaleza-una-imagen-art%C3%ADstica-surrealista-lleno-paisaje-interior-plantas-image401207338)


Hace apenas unas semanas me sometí a una cirugía para remover un quiste sebáceo en el cuello. Lo que podría haber sido simplemente una anécdota médica menor se convirtió en una profunda lección sobre cómo entendemos nuestro cuerpo y nuestra relación con él. Durante el proceso de recuperación, he reflexionado extensamente sobre algo que nuestras sociedades modernas hemos olvidado: nuestro cuerpo no es una galería de arte que debe ser perfecta e inmutable, sino un ecosistema vivo, dinámico y completamente interconectado.

Cuando el dermatólogo me explicó qué era el quiste sebáceo, descubrí algo fascinante. No era un \

que se había desarrollado en mi cuerpo por error. Era el resultado natural de cómo funciona nuestro sistema biológico. Una glándula sebácea había producido exceso de queratina, creando una pequeña bolsa bajo la piel. Mi cuerpo no estaba fallando; estaba haciendo exactamente lo que los cuerpos hacen: existir, cambiar, crecer, y sí, ocasionalmente desarrollar cosas que necesitan ser removidas. Era vida en acción.\n\nEsta realización me llevó a una verdad más amplia: estamos constantemente bombardeados por imágenes de cuerpos \
. La industria de la belleza nos ha enseñado a ver nuestros cuerpos como galerías de arte que deben ser admiradas estáticamente, donde cualquier \

es una falla que debe ser corregida, escondida o eliminada. Pero esto es profundamente alejado de la realidad biológica de lo que somos.

**Nuestro cuerpo es un ecosistema vivo.**

Dentro de cada uno de nosotros hay billones de células trabajando en armonía constante. Tenemos bacterias que nos ayudan a digerir, sistemas inmunológicos que nos defienden, procesos inflamatorios que nos protegen, y cambios hormonal que nos transforman constantemente. Nuestro cuerpo no es estático; es fluido, dinámico, siempre en proceso de transformación. Cada cicatriz cuenta una historia. Cada marca, cada cambio, cada \

es evidencia de que hemos vivido.

Cuando me desperté de la anestesia y vi la pequeña incisión en mi cuello, no sentí horror o vergüenza. En cambio, sentí gratitud. Mi cuerpo había respondido exactamente como debería. El sistema inmunológico activó su defensa, el cuerpo comenzó a sanar, y en unos días la herida cerró con la precisión de millones de años de evolución. Mi cuerpo no había fallado; había funcionado perfectamente.

Esta experiencia me ha cambiado cómo veo los cambios en mi cuerpo. Las arrugas no son enemigos; son prueba de que he sonreído. Las estrías no son cicatrices vergonzosas; son evidencia de que mi cuerpo se ha expandido para hacerme crecer. El envejecimiento no es algo que deba combatirse; es el privilegio de seguir viviendo.

En nuestra cultura del cuerpo perfecto, olvidamos que la verdadera belleza radica en la funcionalidad, en la salud, en la capacidad de nuestro cuerpo de regenerarse y adaptarse. Un cuerpo no es hermoso porque sea una réplica de una imagen de revista; es hermoso porque está vivo, porque siente, porque se mueve, porque cambia y se transforma.

Aprender a ver mi cuerpo como un ecosistema ha sido liberador. Significa que no necesito ser perfecto. Significa que puedo tener cicatrices. Puedo envejecer. Puedo cambiar. Mi cuerpo puede hacer cosas sorprendentes que van más allá de cómo se ve en una fotografía. Puede respirar, puede sentir, puede sanar, puede crear.

He aprendido que la verdadera salud no es estética; es sistémica. Es el balance perfecto de todos esos billones de células trabajando juntas. Es respetar los procesos naturales de nuestro cuerpo, incluso cuando a veces nos llevan a necesitar intervenciones médicas.

Mi pequeño quiste sebáceo fue un maestro inesperado. Me enseñó que soy un milagro biológico viviente, que mi cuerpo es mucho más que su apariencia, y que abrazar nuestra naturaleza viviente es infinitamente más hermoso que pretender ser una obra de arte inmóvil.

A cualquiera que esté lidiando con cambios corporales, cicatrices, o cualquier \

: tu cuerpo es un ecosistema asombroso. Merece respeto, cuidado y amor, no porque sea perfecto, sino porque es vivo.

---

## ENGLISH VERSION

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbPgPCh7dx9xsNs584aLiEBTMpgRo6PdYca96tHXSQXxC/1787785825563.jpg)

[Fuente/es.dreamstime.com](https://es.dreamstime.com/el-cuerpo-humano-se-transforma-en-un-ecosistema-de-la-naturaleza-una-imagen-art%C3%ADstica-surrealista-lleno-paisaje-interior-plantas-image401207338)

I underwent surgery just a few weeks ago to remove a sebaceous cyst on my neck. What could have been merely a minor medical anecdote became a profound lesson about how we understand our bodies and our relationship with them. During my recovery, I've reflected extensively on something modern societies have forgotten: our bodies are not art galleries meant to be perfect and immutable, but living, dynamic ecosystems that are completely interconnected.

When the dermatologist explained what a sebaceous cyst was, I discovered something fascinating. It wasn't a \

that had developed in my body by mistake. It was a natural result of how our biological system functions. A sebaceous gland had produced excess keratin, creating a small sac under the skin. My body wasn't failing; it was doing exactly what bodies do: exist, change, grow, and yes, occasionally develop things that need to be removed. It was life in action.\n\nThis realization led me to a broader truth: we are constantly bombarded with images of \
skin. The beauty industry has taught us to see our bodies as art galleries that must be admired statically, where any \

is a flaw that must be corrected, hidden, or eliminated. But this is profoundly disconnected from the biological reality of what we are.

**Our body is a living ecosystem.**

Within each of us are trillions of cells working in constant harmony. We have bacteria that help us digest, immune systems that defend us, inflammatory processes that protect us, and hormonal changes that constantly transform us. Our body is not static; it is fluid, dynamic, always in the process of transformation. Every scar tells a story. Every mark, every change, every \

is evidence that we have lived.

When I woke up from anesthesia and saw the small incision on my neck, I didn't feel horror or shame. Instead, I felt gratitude. My body had responded exactly as it should. The immune system activated its defense, the body began to heal, and within days the wound closed with the precision of millions of years of evolution. My body hadn't failed; it had functioned perfectly.

This experience has changed how I see changes in my body. Wrinkles aren't enemies; they're proof that I've smiled. Stretch marks aren't shameful scars; they're evidence that my body has expanded to help me grow. Aging isn't something to be fought; it's the privilege of continuing to live.

In our culture of the perfect body, we forget that true beauty lies in functionality, in health, in our body's ability to regenerate and adapt. A body isn't beautiful because it's a replica of a magazine image; it's beautiful because it's alive, because it feels, because it moves, because it changes and transforms.

Learning to see my body as an ecosystem has been liberating. It means I don't need to be perfect. It means I can have scars. I can age. I can change. My body can do extraordinary things that go far beyond how it looks in a photograph. It can breathe, it can feel, it can heal, it can create.

I've learned that true health isn't aesthetic; it's systemic. It's the perfect balance of all those trillions of cells working together. It's respecting the natural processes of our bodies, even when they sometimes lead us to need medical intervention.

My little sebaceous cyst was an unexpected teacher. It taught me that I am a living biological miracle, that my body is much more than its appearance, and that embracing our living nature is infinitely more beautiful than pretending to be a motionless work of art.

To anyone dealing with bodily changes, scars, or any \
: your body is an amazing ecosystem. It deserves respect, care, and love—not because it's perfect, but because it's alive.\n\n---

# Learn Rust Series (#42) - Drop Order, the Drop Check & Leak Safety

Episode 20 introduced `Drop` and the RAII idea that a value cleans up after itself the instant it goes out of scope. That was the happy, ten-thousand-foot view. Today we descend to ground level and look at the three details that trip people up once they start writing destructors for real: the exact _order_ things drop in, the compiler analysis called the **drop check** that keeps a destructor from reading a dangling reference, and Rust's genuinely surprising stance that _leaking_ memory is safe while _using_ freed memory is not.

That last point catches almost everybody off guard the first time, so let me say it plainly up front. Rust's safety guarantee is not \

in C++ too, in the narrow sense that it does not corrupt memory -- it just wastes it.

In **Python**, you almost never think about any of this, because the interpreter reference-counts every object and frees it the moment the count hits zero, with a backup cycle collector for the loops that plain counting would leak (the exact problem episode 35 solved explicitly with `Weak`). Python does expose a `__del__` finalizer, but its timing is famously unreliable and you are warned not to depend on it -- the opposite of Rust's deterministic, scope-bound `Drop`. And Python leaks are possible too (a lingering reference in a global keeps an object alive forever), which is the same story every managed language tells.

In **Go**, the garbage collector owns every heap object and you never call free at all. Instead of destructors you get `defer`, which schedules cleanup at function-return time -- deterministic for things like closing files, but nothing like Rust's per-value, ownership-driven teardown. Go leaks the same way: keep a reference in a live goroutine or a package-level variable and the object never gets collected.

Three languages, one shared truth: every one of them treats leaking as safe-but-undesirable, and none of them but Rust catches destructor-ordering-versus-lifetime mistakes at compile time. That drop check is a genuinely Rust-specific piece of engineering, and it is doing quiet work on your behalf every time you add a `Drop` impl to a borrowing type.

## What did we actually learn?

- **Drop order** follows three rules: locals drop in reverse declaration order (stack-like), struct fields drop in declaration order (top to bottom), and a value's own `Drop::drop` runs _before_ its fields. Arrange fields deliberately when teardown order matters (flush before close).
- **The drop check (dropck)** ensures that any reference a `Drop` impl might read still outlives the value. This is why adding a `Drop` impl to a borrowing type can introduce fresh lifetime errors -- you have promised to touch the borrow at the last moment.
- **Leaks are safe; use-after-free is not.** Rust guarantees you never touch freed memory, _not_ that every destructor runs. A leak wastes memory but cannot cause undefined behaviour, so safe code is allowed to leak.
- **`Box::leak`** turns an owned allocation into a `'static` reference that lives forever -- handy for one-time global state. **`std::mem::forget`** skips a value's destructor without freeing what it owns.
- **`ManuallyDrop<T>`** suppresses automatic drop and lets you fire the destructor yourself, exactly once, at a moment you choose. `ManuallyDrop::drop` is `unsafe` because a double call or later use is a use-after-free.
- Other languages treat leaking as safe-but-wasteful too, but only Rust's dropck turns destructor-versus-lifetime ordering bugs into compile errors.

## Exercises

Three exercises, from gentle to chewier. Type them out and _run_ them -- drop order in particular only sticks once you have watched the print statements fire in an order that surprised you.

1. Make a struct with three `Loud` fields (each printing its name in `Drop`) and no `Drop` impl of its own. Predict the print order, run it, then reorder the fields and confirm the output changes to match the new declaration order.
2. Add a `Drop` impl to a borrowing struct `Holder<'a>(&'a String)` that reads its reference in `drop`. Write a `main` where the borrowed `String` is declared _after_ the `Holder`, so it would drop first, read the exact dropck error the compiler gives you, and write a one-line comment naming which value \

and why.
3. Use `ManuallyDrop` to hold two resources whose `Drop` prints, and release them in the _opposite_ order from their declaration. Then, as a second step, `std::mem::forget` a third resource and confirm from the output that its destructor never runs at all.

That second step of exercise 3 -- deliberately skipping a destructor -- and the whole `forget`/`ManuallyDrop`/`ptr::read` dance from the `try_unwrap` solution are pointing straight at where we go next: the small standard-library toolkit for moving values into and out of places safely, without ever leaving a hole for a double-free. Chew on it ;-)

Thanks for reading -- see you in the next episode!

## Hoy mi domingo musical. [Rise Slow · Kimo Sounds](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bRPlrNOvjyo&list=PLZnXcVuaqUAY)
#
<div class=\

>

Hoy es mi domingo musical y les traigo esto que está como decimos aquí en mi país, esta calientico salido del horno, bueno les soy sincero nunca había publicado o escrito algo relacionado con este género musical, que para mí es algo así como nuevo, y no dejo de reconocer que el ritmo es pegajoso, pero lo mejor de todo es la letra, sinceramente cuando la escuche no sabía ni papa que decía la letra así que de una la investigue no me quede con eso.

El tema se llama \

de  Kimo Sounds, es un género que mezcla de Deep House con música electrónica suave, al principio uno escucha y el ritmo de una vez me engancho, pero al ponerme a traducir la letra me encontré con un mensaje de esos que lo ponen a uno a pensar bastante o bueno te ponen a reflexivo porque es una letra muy básica.

La canción habla de la resiliencia y de cómo uno va creciendo y superando las cosas en la vida a su propio ritmo, sin andar haciendo ningún show y ustedes saben que yo critico eso, porque de pana el venezolano es muy farandulero además la letra tampoco anda buscando aprobación de nadie, sobre todo se enfoca en esas luchas internas que uno lleva así tipo calladito, en las noches cuando nadie te ve ni te escucha, pero uno sigue dándole constante día tras día, me gustó mucho porque nos recuerda que no hay necesidad de andar apurados, lo importante es levantarse, aunque sea despacio, pero con pasos firmes.

Hay una parte de la letra de Kimo Sounds que me llamó mucho la atención y cito:

>\

>Nadie vio las noches en que me mantuve firme / nadie me escuchó cuando no hice ruido / no necesité luz para hallar mi camino / solo seguí avanzando en la oscuridad cada día

A veces hace falta escuchar temas así para recordar que los verdaderos procesos llevan algo de tiempo y son mucho más valorados además que cada quien lleva su paso.

Today is my musical Sunday, and I bring you something that is, as we say here in my country, hot off the press. Well, to be honest, I had never published or written anything related to this musical genre, which for me is kind of new. I can't deny that the rhythm is catchy, but the best part of all is the lyrics. Honestly, when I listened to it, I had no clue what the lyrics were saying, so I immediately researched it—I didn't stay curious.

The song is called \

by Kimo Sounds. It belongs to a genre that blends Deep House with smooth electronic music. At first, you listen to it and the beat instantly hooks you, but when I started translating the lyrics, I found one of those messages that really makes you think, or well, makes you reflect, because it has very straightforward lyrics.

The song talks about resilience and how one grows and overcomes things in life at their own pace, without putting on any show—and you know I criticize that, because honestly, Venezuelans can be quite attention-seeking. Plus, the lyrics aren't looking for anyone's approval. Above all, it focuses on those internal struggles you carry quietly, during the nights when no one sees or hears you, but you keep pushing forward day after day. I really liked it because it reminds us that there's no need to be in a rush; the important thing is to get up, even if it's slow, but with steady steps.

>\

body.body: Several years ago I bought a flatbed scanner with a slide adapter to scan some old film slides that my grandparents had. After I finished scanning those, I picked up several batches of slides from Goodwill and on eBay out of curiosity. I am not sure why these commonly wind up at such places but I know that at least some of them have ultimately come from estate sales. Maybe family members just don't know what to do with them. I've seen them advertised as being for arts and crafts but I was more interested in the actual contents. Each slide is literally a snapshot in history. These pictures span from as early as the late 1940s to as late as the early 1990s. There are thousands of these slides. I will be scanning some from time to time and posting them here as an interesting way to look back at the past.\n\nI'm using the term \
to refer to a group of slides I bought in a single purchase. Usually they are from the same ultimate origin. Typically, a batch will have 100s or even 1000s of slides.\n\nI'm using the term \

to refer to a subset of a batch that I scan together. There are normally four slides in one set because that's how many slides my scanner can scan at once. Likewise, a post will typically have one set of four slides. It's just easier to keep track of that way.\n\nThis batch contains photos spanning from the late 1950s to the early 1980s. Other than these slides coming from eBay, I have no idea of their ultimate origin other than the clues provided in the photos themselves. The photographer seems to have been from Lansing, Michigan and many of the photos are from there. I think I've identified the photographer, see <a href = \

>this post for more details. These were all scanned with an Epson Perfection V600 Photo scanner. All of the photos in this set were taken in the early 1970s. All were likely taken in the Lansing Michigan area. The first photo was taken in January 1973 and is labeled 'Grandma'. It looks like it was her birthday based on all of the cards on the table. The next three photos were all processed in April 1971 and are all labeled 'Program Posters'. These appear to be advertising various upcoming events at a community center, including dancing, swimming, and an Easter event.

>
Program Posters
See the previous post in this series
>here. \n\nThe entire batch that has been scanned and uploaded so far can also be found

>here. I’m not normally given to dishing out praise on the police forces of Yorkshire knowing what I know about these forces failure to stop the Islamic Rape Gangs that have terrorised and scarred the Yorkshire area among others.  However a recent article by Dr Richard North on Turbulent Times has caused me to change my stance somewhat and praise West Yorkshire Police.

According to Dr North, West Yorkshire Police have managed to bust a significant money laundering gang that may have dealt with at least £266 million in criminal assets.  This operation Dr North said was not a local one it was taking in dirty money from criminal groups across the country and funnelling it via the main company involved in the money laundering.

This the culmination it appears of a decade long investigation and the amounts involved in this case are probably just the tip of a very large iceberg with similar money laundering operations likely to also be in operation.  Dr North’s story is an amazing tale of dogged investigation into an area of criminality that might often be difficult for investigators to penetrate if money gained by criminality has been ‘washed’ to make it appear legitimate.

Read the story via the link below.

https://www.turbulenttimes.co.uk/news/front-page/policing-money-laundering/
