body.title: Les millors zones del món per nedar entre taurons: una aventura inoblidable
body.body:
Nedar o bussejar entre taurons és una de les experiències més emocionants i transformadores que es poden viure a la natura. Aquests animals, sovint mal interpretats pel cinema i la cultura popular, són essencials per a l’equilibri dels ecosistemes marins. Amb operadors responsables i mesures de seguretat adequades, es pot gaudir d’encontres propers de manera relativament segura, alhora que es contribueix a la conservació a través del turisme sostenible.

Aquí tens una selecció de les millors destinacions del món per compartir l’aigua amb aquests depredadors majestuosos.

### 1. Llacuna de Beqa (Fiji) – La capital mundial dels taurons
Considerada per molts experts com la millor destinació global per densitat i diversitat, la Llacuna de Beqa (prop de Pacific Harbour, a l’illa de Viti Levu) ofereix encontres amb fins a vuit espècies diferents en una sola immersió: taurons toro (bull sharks), taurons tigre, taurons grisos d’escull, taurons de puntes platejades, taurons llimona i taurons nodrissa, entre d’altres. 

Forma part de la Reserva Marina de Shark Reef, on el turisme de busseig ajuda a protegir l’hàbitat. Les immersions solen ser amb alimentació controlada i es fan sense gàbia, amb protocols estrictes de seguretat. La visibilitat sol ser bona i l’experiència és accessible durant tot l’any, amb condicions especialment bones a l’estiu austral.

### 2. Tiger Beach (Bahames) – Taurons tigre garantits
Situada a l’oest de Grand Bahama, Tiger Beach és el lloc més fiable del planeta per nedar (sense gàbia) amb taurons tigre. En aigües cristal·lines i poc profundes, es poden observar grups de taurons tigre, juntament amb taurons llimona, taurons d’escull del Carib i taurons nodrissa. 

La temporada alta de taurons tigre sol ser d’octubre a març. Els operadors experimentats fan briefings detallats i controlen les interaccions. És una de les experiències més properes i fotogèniques del món.

### 3. Illa de Guadalupe (Mèxic) – El regne del gran tauró blanc
Aquesta illa volcànica remotíssima, al Pacífic mexicà, és un dels millors llocs del món per a immersions en gàbia amb grans taurons blancs. La visibilitat excepcional (sovint 30-45 metres) i les aigües relativament temperades permeten observar aquests animals impressionants en el seu hàbitat natural, on s’alimenten de foques.

Les expedicions solen ser en vaixells liveaboard de diversos dies (temporada principal d’agost a novembre/desembre). És una experiència premium i molt regulada per protegir l’espècie i l’entorn.

### 4. Gansbaai i rodalies (Sud-àfrica) – L’“Alley dels taurons”
A la costa occidental de Sud-àfrica, especialment a Gansbaai (prop de Dyer Island), es realitzen immersions en gàbia amb grans taurons blancs des de fa dècades. La zona concentra una gran població de foques, que atrau els taurons. 

També es poden fer sortides a altres espècies (com taurons blaus o mako) o combinar-ho amb el fenomen de la “Sardine Run”. La visibilitat varia i la temporada alta sol ser entre maig i setembre. És una de les opcions més accessibles per a qui vol veure grans blancs.

### 5. Illes Galápagos (Equador) – Escoles de peixos martell
A Darwin i Wolf, dos dels punts més remots de l’arxipèlag, es poden observar centenars de peixos martell en estacions de neteja, a més de taurons de Galápagos, seda i altres espècies pelàgiques. És una destinació per a bussejadors experimentats, normalment en liveaboards, amb corrents forts i condicions exigents, però amb recompenses espectaculars.

### Altres destinacions destacades
- **Polinèsia Francesa (Fakarava i Rangiroa)**: Passos amb grans concentracions de taurons grisos d’escull, martell i ocasionalment tigre. Aigües cristal·lines i paisatges de postal.  
- **Illes Neptune (Austràlia)**: Immersions en gàbia amb grans taurons blancs, amb bona reputació de seguretat i visibilitat.  
- **Aliwal Shoal (Sud-àfrica)**: Taurons de dents irregulars (ragged-tooth) i diversitat estacional.  
- **Hawaii (Oahu o Maui)**: Experiències amb taurons de diversos tipus, incloent-hi alguns de més accessibles per a no bussejadors certificats.  
- **Per a taurons balena (els “gentils gegants”)**: Isla Mujeres (Mèxic) o Ningaloo Reef (Austràlia) ofereixen snorkel amb aquests animals filtrejadors, una experiència totalment diferent i molt segura.

### Consells de seguretat i responsabilitat
Sempre tria operadors amb bona reputació, llicències i protocols clars. Respecta les distàncies, no toquis els animals i segueix les instruccions dels guies. Moltes d’aquestes destinacions depenen del turisme de taurons per justificar la protecció dels ecosistemes, així que el teu viatge pot tenir un impacte positiu.

Nedar entre taurons no és només una dosi d’adrenalina: és una oportunitat per canviar la percepció sobre aquests animals i connectar amb l’oceà d’una manera profunda. Si et prepares bé i triés destinacions responsables, viuràs una de les aventures més memorables de la teva vida.  

¡Bon viatge submarí!

***

Bulldogs

My father used to call it fighting with the bulldogs. Political rivalries with the other employees—particularly the male ones. The bulldogs. Fighting over territory, credit, power, control, promotion—you name it—the whole corporate nightmare in the office. Dad loved the technical part of his profession: mechanical engineering, but the societal part—hell incarnated. I was the same way back when I worked as a contractor going from once assignment to the next in that swamp incorporated. Watch out for the back stabbing and dirty tricks they'd play. So glad I'm out of that soup. Retired. I barely squeaked by with my share of conflict crap and unpleasant memories. Makes you realize the world is filled with assholes—the creme de la creme of sick individuals and the higher up the ladder the sicker and the bigger the bulldogs they are.

body.title: A Siquijor escapade (Day 2)
body.body:
Hello hello I am back and now to continue my little romance and adventure XD 
So we had that lazy day, right? and we agreed on an adventure together and so we did an adventure. So getting around the island, we had the option of renting a car, motorcycle or a tuk tuk and since the car was expensive and neither of us knew how to drive a motorcycle, we went with the tuktuk option. Again, he would not let me pay for anything, I swear XD IDK if I was just used to dating broke guys or if this really is how gentlemen treat their ladies. Like  know he wasn't rich but he really got upset whenever I had to pull out my wallet in the entire duration of our trip together and every single time I wanted to buy something for myself, he wouldn't even hesitate to pay for it first because he knows I would count first because my coin purse is a mess.

Going back to the activities we did on day 2, our first sto was the 400 year old balete tree that they ended up turning into a fish spa. The idea is cool because they're trying to maintain the tree, the fish nourish I but also protect the roots plus it gathers funds to help maintain it o an overall win, I would say. 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmfEcasYtXV7PC71DWBWsgeiSkov9VdLpG6qNiQNABmCQe/messenger_creation_5480766a_b93d_47c7_b876_bc8b48c491af.jpeg)

I unfortunately did not have enough dead skin for the fishes to feast on and I blame my weekly exfoliation habit for that but he fishes went crazy on my man's feet cuz he ha so mu dead skin on him and even the bi fishes hounded his feet like that. 
![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUVBhYvRXFtbHxFFoAaR94VLJGCVbxiPVR9KFreg1uR9L/messenger_creation_be78f7d7_78cd_40c7_9e16_84ab3f3aca65.jpg)
Then there was this rally cute and confused fish that didn't know whether it wanted to eat or not but it was literally confused enough that I got to pet it XD I do think this fish may be my spirit animal because we're both just confused af XD

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcmRgPg46tF54ZTXyTouTkHZm2nGsWJZbkQVho6RrAVwB/messenger_creation_889d691a_853a_451c_b7cd_2109e1e0d79e.jpg)

Then we did a bit of souvenir shopping and had an early lunch at the café in there. I wouldn't say the coffee was fantastic since coffee is definitely not what Siquijor I famous for but it was enough to keep me going for the day XD

next destination was in Cambugahay falls which wasn't so far from the tree, maybe like a 5 minute ride 

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmc11ay1XdpCaNj11uyR8nUbaX4SBSRmZcz1nJhHwgxP94/messenger_creation_fd19df79_c5a2_4a10_b139_ad1be047ac25.jpg)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZK6RGWL8ezD9Bqbr7pxwpvUqivAoBBXyWJRG1MfygAq2/messenger_creation_38b1a72b_cc07_40b5_a4fe_cd7165725c8a.jpg)
> [//]:# (!worldmappin 9.13990 lat 123.62666 long  d3scr)

It was really pretty there but I think I prefer my usual waterfalls spots for the clearer water. the water was still pretty nice though, really cold and refreshing. And I think for me, I just enjoyed floating in the water because my man said I could just cling onto his back and he'd walk us around the falls XD I mean, he is a 6'4\

Is there a backup plan? If there's a forest and a lake, then all that's missing for complete happiness is a sunrise? Although... if there's fatigue... then a sunset :)

body.title: [TV] \
| Lanterns - Episode Review [ES - EN]
body.body:
es el título del segundo episodio de **Lanterns**, el cual está enfocado en la línea temporal del 2016, en donde Hal y John deben seguir lidiando con su relación de tutor y aprendiz, en el momento en que deben resolver el caso de por qué un alienígena decidió inmolarse en una estación policial antes de confirmar que su estancia en la Tierra era debido a una venganza. Esta fue una decisión acertada por los guionistas de la serie, ya que pone en pausa lo que considero que es el gran caso a resolver en la temporada.
> \

is the title of the second episode of **Lanterns**, which focuses on the 2016 timeline, where Hal and John must continue to navigate their mentor-apprentice relationship while trying to solve the case of why an alien chose to blow himself up at a police station before confirming that his presence on Earth was motivated by revenge. This was a wise decision by the show’s writers, as it puts on hold what I consider to be the season’s main mystery.
![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTMiZQi1a99D3mAwtU7shVFGVbWduyM2xNF7cYATy9Jbx/1000369334.png)
[Fuente / Source](https://justonemoreep.com/2026/08/24/lanterns-s01e02-trust-fall-critique/)

El segundo episodio, posiblemente para algunos no generó el impacto que sí tuvo el primero; personalmente, pienso que fue muy acertado en su aporte a la narrativa y el lore de lo que ofrece el mundo donde habitan estos personajes; no tengo ninguna duda de que cada suceso fue sumamente importante para el desarrollo de sus protagonistas porque por primera vez los vemos tener escenas individuales, lo cual fue interesante porque de una manera u otra, generaron respuestas y misterio del caso que investigaron en la línea temporal del 2016. El hecho de que en un principio del episodio, Hal y John, tomen caminos diferentes en un tiempo breve fue interesante porque descubrimos algunos aspectos de Jordan y también nos vamos generando una idea de lo que puede lograr Stewart cuando sea su momento de ser un Linterna Verde.
> The second episode may not have had the same impact on some viewers as the first did; personally, I think it made a very effective contribution to the narrative and the lore of the world these characters inhabit; I have no doubt that every event was extremely important for the development of the main characters because, for the first time, we see them in individual scenes—which was interesting because, in one way or another, they provided answers and added mystery to the case they were investigating in the 2016 timeline. The fact that, early in the episode, Hal and John briefly go their separate ways was interesting because we discovered some aspects of Jordan and also began to get a sense of what Stewart is capable of when his time comes to become a Green Lantern.
![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmQCcijCAT2oLKomjfqLwKUVKhZBdqTvyagteMVkntLBz1/1000369335.png)
[Fuente / Source](https://www.episodicmedium.tv/review-lanterns-trust-fall-season-1-episode-2/)

En este segundo episodio, con un ritmo muy fluido, lo cual hizo ver que fuese corto, presentó un nivel adecuado de misterio, acción y una carga de humor que no se presenció tanto en el primer episodio; justamente ese humor provino en su mayoría por parte del personaje de Hal, que necesitó de su encanto para poder ir descubriendo ciertas pistas que pueden acercarlo a una resolución de un caso que puede estar muy ligado a lo que fue la elección de Jordan como Linterna. En ese aspecto, me pareció genial que este episodio pueda usar la investigación para suavizar la historia, no restando el factor adulto o haciéndola infantil, sino para hacerla entretenida por la inclusión de escenas de acción y, como señalé anteriormente, escenas de humor.
> In this second episode, which had a very smooth pace—making it feel short—there was just the right amount of mystery, action, and a dose of humor that wasn’t as prominent in the first episode; that humor came mostly from Hal’s character, who had to rely on his charm to uncover certain clues that might bring him closer to solving a case that may be closely tied to Jordan’s selection as a Green Lantern. In that regard, I thought it was great that this episode used the investigation to lighten the story—not by toning down the mature elements or making it childish, but by making it entertaining through the inclusion of action scenes and, as I mentioned earlier, humorous moments.
![](https://images.hive.blog/DQmcTCTfNrQZUCRHXJTVxxEmc2GjCQ6ASv6pYfo28xphqMP/1000369336.png)
[Fuente / Source](https://www.techradar.com/streaming/hbo-max/sinestro-in-lanterns-explained)

Hay un tema muy importante en **Trust Fall** y es con respecto a la relación entre Hal y John, como tutor y aprendiz, lo cual es demostrado como una competencia entre ambos en donde primeramente existe la imposición de rango por parte de Hal para después ser sorprendido por el poder de Hal en generar una proyección por un largo tiempo sin la necesidad de portar el anillo; ambas experiencias o la manera de entrenar y usar lo aprendido genera más misterios a esta historia, y nos provee una idea de como será la relación entre un experimentado Linterna Verde y un joven hombre que parece descubrir o saber cuál es su potencial y sentir que está siendo retraído por alguien que posiblemente no sea digno de portar el anillo; esa idea se me hace más que fascinante y por supuesto me genera muchas expectativas porque eso puede estar muy relacionado con el futuro de la historia. Como pensamiento final con respecto a mi opinión sobre este segundo episodio, creo que fue un perfecto complemento y seguramente habrá episodios iguales, y prefiero no referirme a esos episodios como de relleno porque aporta muchas cosas, tiene un fanservice adecuado y, aunque no tenga un cliffhanger tan impactante como en el anterior, de igual manera ofrece una parte importante de la historia de Hal Jordan.
> There is a very important theme in **Trust Fall**, and it concerns the relationship between Hal and John—as mentor and apprentice—which is portrayed as a competition between the two, where Hal initially imposes his authority, only to be later surprised by Hal’s ability to maintain a projection for an extended period without needing to wear the ring; Both of these experiences—as well as the methods of training and applying what’s been learned—add more mystery to this story and give us a glimpse of what the relationship between an experienced Green Lantern and a young man might be like. This young man seems to be discovering or realizing his potential, yet feels held back by someone who may not be worthy of wearing the ring; I find that idea absolutely fascinating, and of course it raises my expectations, as it may be closely tied to the story’s future. As a final thought regarding my opinion on this second episode, I think it was a perfect complement, and there will surely be similar episodes. I prefer not to refer to those episodes as “filler” because they contribute a lot, have just the right amount of fan service, and—even if they don’t have a cliffhanger as impactful as the previous one—they still offer an important part of Hal Jordan’s story.

body.title: Angry Clouds & Directed Discipline: (audio: noxsoma.substack.com)
body.body:
(The audio to these rants is posted at 4:20 EST on Substack. Or you can read it here.) 

![cip soma rain 2.jpg](https://images.hive.blog/DQmTmqj9H7gbgbgFfDtC9pzrV2RoU6TpB3gTbEeZgkS4GMU/cip%20soma%20rain%202.jpg)

Sol-2-Soul my brothers and sisters. Welcome to one more day above ground. This is the 100th Sunday of our Sol-glowing soul enhancing series. The title is implicit of the connection between the Sun/Sol, our immortal soul and the light that both emit. Your soul & vessel already know this connection, even if what you call, You, do not. In our Simulatrix, the sun penetrates the vessel and forms the Earth equivalent of gold. It’s just a hypothesis, based on what we’ve heard, read, watched, and extracted from how gold on Earth is solidified sunlight, the healing properties gold is supposed to have in the vessel, and the way melanin interacts with the sun, and plays a role in detoxifying the vessel. Not to mention the placebo power of belief and the self-programming of the Simulatrix. Far be if from your humble vagabond to toss my neighbors into the sun, but it’s done wonders for our human starship. 

Here’s a late summer clean up project. We’re gathering all of the Substack audio letters we can find and combining them into a single file. I hesitate to call is an “audio book,” because it’s more like an album, but it’s too big to be an album. The month of August alone is nearly 4 hours long. Anyway, we will be posting August memoirs on our Substack Podcast page. I presume that subscribers will be alerted to these releases. 
The moon has left Pisces and we have completed our most successful three days of abstinence. We scored some herbal, caffeine-free teas, which kept us decaffeinated. We experienced no headaches during this series, and we never have a problem not eating meat. We decided not to abstain from supplements, which are mainly vitamins, (the letters), minerals, spices, mushrooms, bark extracts and liver cleansers. We get back to our regularly schedule diet today. 

Discipline came to mind. The psych profile describes the Noxsoma character as “highly disciplined.” Ego was wondering, “what changed?” We were anything but disciplined in our youth. The easy answers could be, “maturity.” Or maybe, “responsibility.” But I think there’s a deeper answer. Discipline is not a monolithic, discipline. The “rebel” description is not my own, although I do not disagree with it. We have embraced it. It’s the rebel nature that abstracts the concept of discipline. What we have is self-discipline. Or self-directed discipline. Like those assets in the Jason Bourne, only without the MK Ultra manipulation, the drugs and the headaches. When we, “put our Mind to it,” we are unstoppable. This is one of many things both my Dad and my teachers recognized in earlier versions of this vessel. We didn’t recognize it, even when we were doing it. 
Of course all teachers, especially those back in the day, told all students this. Didn’t they? Maybe that’s why it was so difficult to believe. Then someone, like a sibling, would recall how, “You were so into, this or that. You were so focused.” And you’re like. Well you didn’t notice it because you were so deeply into it. 
When I was a photographer, I could be in the darkroom for hours, getting my print just right. But when I was in the lab at the gig, I couldn’t wait to wrap it up and get out of there. 
That’s the matrix, the labyrinth, the combination behind every one of those virtues. Research without curiosity, is drudgery. But when it’s exploration, investigation and discovery, ten years can seem like a week. We anxiously await that next opportunity to learn something new. 

If I were not so disciplined, I could fill every minute of the day writing, working out, searching for answers to obscure questions, connections between seemingly unconnected words, the origin of the “syndromes” that have become real to the herd, and making videos. Alas, we must take care of the vessel. 
There’s an updated Summer Audio out today. And tomorrow, in our 17 day Health & Wellness update, the most in depth psychological profile of the digital native known as Noxsoma.    
Part Two. 
After being imprisoned by yesterday’s harsh weather, we are looking forward to getting out into this partly-sunny morning. The weather here in the deepest part of the United States is tropical. Near unpredictable, but when you get outside you can literally see it coming. The sky will be fluffy with puffy white clouds that look like pillows, and then, seemingly out of no where, this dark gray angry cluster shows up. The temperature drops and the winds pick up. And we’re like, “Don’t come over here.” Sometimes the clouds comply. We can watch the swelled mass move off into another direction. But then again sometimes, the weather system just dumps its load right where we are, and we’re running for cover. 
Even when Earth disrupts our playtime workout, it’s amazing to watch. And experience. 
Sundays have been gravity-strap workout days for close to a month now. We are still figuring out strategies, and methods and angles to maximize our strength, flexibility and balance, without doing damage to the vessel. Since Sunday’s are low traffic days in the park, we can set up the video and capture a few clips. We share this workout within the Full Metal Ox daily series, and also on Instagram, (@Noxsoma), if you’re curious. It’s a chronicle, not instructional. If you’re inspired, get yourself a set of these things, (or make your own), and go out and give it a try. Be mindful of your joints. If you purchase the product there will likely be a booklet that includes exercises you can do. I have one that I haven’t opened yet, as we, the vessel et al, are still experimenting on our own. And this isn’t our first set of grav-straps. 
Okay. That’s a wrap. 
 Have a most awesome week. 
 Stay sane, stay strong, stay safe, stay savvy, stay serene, stay sovereign, stay subscribed. 
 PEACE.

body.title: [Movie] Reviw: The Shape of Water (En-Es)
body.body:
What shape should love take? This is the question that sustains this entire film.
Because far from the epic fantasy or perhaps science fiction that we might expect from a premise where an anthropomorphic merman is found in the Amazon and taken to a United States laboratory to be studied, this film runs in a different direction, starting from a protagonist who is already peculiar in her own right.
This deaf-mute girl who cleans the scientific/military facilities and whom chance perhaps leads to cross paths with this creature that seems plucked from another world, but who undoubtedly shares bonds with us, something he demonstrates through a great humanity.

Humanity that cuts across the film with its lights and shadows. Perhaps each of the characters we find here, the protagonists, are a reflection of some extreme of humanity. Both that kindness, protection, and warmth that we can find in one of the co-protagonists, who without too many explanations is capable of giving up his personal space to give refuge to someone he does not fully understand, but whom he knows how to see as different without discriminating, because in this same character we could see another facet, another of the double readings that this film wants to give us, because it touches upon homosexuality in mild parts of the film.

But through this character, we have a reflection of otherness, of how in the era where the film takes place—the mid-20th century—this was still a taboo subject in the United States and in the world in general, and how through these discriminated, lonely people, in many ways, solidarity toward the different was more present. Counterposing him, we have the antagonist, who from his position of power pursues and intends to take advantage of that otherness, taking advantage through oppression, constant scrutiny for the sake of his own benefits or rather his own ego.

An ego that is hurt both physically and symbolically from the beginning of the film. With these issues only as background, the story revolves around unbridled love, an unusual passion between our protagonist and this Amazonian being.

A love that is built at first from curiosity, but quickly evolves into a voracious desire capable of flooding even the smallest corner where they meet. Because although between them not a word is spoken, no, it is not something they need.
An issue resolved fantastically through the protagonist's condition, which for the film serves as a vehicle for many matters. And this would have been a perfect resolution had it not been for the world in which we live and which the film tries to reflect.

Because almost inevitably, such a different love was condemned to be pursued. Because yes, perhaps like all the films of its director Guillermo del Toro, there is a question that always arises for us here: who is truly the monster?

Because in the face of a world that does not allow your happiness, simply because it does not understand it or does not accept it, what would be the best solution? To flee?

This film leaves us open with a possible final drama, where flowing like water itself, our protagonists try to escape from everything that does not allow them to be as one, and in that flight into the unknown, it makes us wonder once more about the shape that love ought to have.

The kind that can change depending on any circumstance, molds itself to the container that holds it, and flows just like the shape of water.


Versión en Español:

¿Qué forma debe tener el amor? Esta es la interrogante que sostiene toda esta película.

Porque lejos de la épica de fantasía o tal vez ciencia ficción, que podríamos esperarnos de una premisa donde se encuentra un sirenido de forma antropomórfica en el Amazonas y se lo lleva un laboratorio de Estados Unidos para estudiárselo, esta película corre en una dirección distinta, partiendo desde una protagonista ya de por sí peculiar.

Esta chica sordomuda que limpia las instalaciones científicas/militares y que tal vez el azar la lleva a encontrarse con esta criatura que parece sacada de otro mundo, pero que sin duda comparte lazos con nosotros y esto lo demuestra a través de una gran humanidad.

Humanidad que transversaliza la película con sus claros y oscuros. Tal vez cada uno de los personajes que encontramos aquí, protagónicos, son un reflejo de algún extremo de la humanidad. Tanto esa bondad, protección, calidez, que podemos encontrar en uno de los coprotagónicos, quien sin demasiadas explicaciones es capaz de entregar su espacio personal para darle refugio a alguien que no comprende del todo lo que es, pero que él sabe ver como diferente aunque no discrimina, porque en este mismo personaje podríamos ver otra de las aristas, otra de las dobles lecturas que nos quiere dar esta película, porque toca la homosexualidad en partes leves del filme.

Pero a través de este personaje tenemos un reflejo de la otredad, de cómo en la época donde transcurre la película, mediados del siglo XX, todavía este era un tema tabú en los Estados Unidos y en el mundo en general, y cómo a través de estas personas discriminadas, solitarias, en muchos sentidos, la solidaridad hacia lo distinto estaba más presente. Contraponiéndose a este, tenemos al antagonista, quien desde su posición de poder persigue y pretende aprovecharse de esa otredad, aprovechándose a través de una opresión, de un escrutinio constante en pro de sus propios beneficios o más bien de su propio ego.

Un ego que se ve lastimado tanto física como simbólicamente desde el principio de la película. Con estas cuestiones solo de trasfondo, la historia gira sobre un amor desenfrenado, una pasión insólita entre nuestra protagonista y este ser amazónico.
Un amor que se construye en un principio desde la curiosidad, pero que rápidamente evoluciona en un deseo voraz que es capaz de inundar hasta el más ínfimo rincón donde se encuentran. Porque aunque entre ellos no se media palabra, no, no es algo que necesiten.

Cuestión resuelta fantásticamente a través de la condición de la protagonista, la cual para la película sirve como vehículo para muchas cuestiones. Y esta hubiera sido una resolución perfecta de no ser por el mundo en el que vivimos y en el que la película intenta reflejar.

Porque casi de manera inevitable, un amor tan diferente estaba condenado a ser perseguido. Porque sí, tal vez como todas las películas de este, de su director Guillermo del Toro, hay una cuestión que siempre nos surge, aquí, ¿quién es verdaderamente el monstruo?

Porque ante un mundo que no permite tu felicidad, simplemente por el hecho de que no la entiende o no la acepta, ¿cuál sería la mejor solución? ¿Huir?
Esta película nos deja abierto así como un posible drama final, donde fluyendo como la propia agua, nuestras protagonistas intentan escapar de todo aquello que no los permite ser como uno solo, y en esa huida hacia lo desconocido nos hace preguntarnos una vez más por la forma que debería tener el amor.

Ese que puede cambiar en dependencia de cualquier circunstancia, se amolda al recipiente que le contiene y fluye así como la forma del agua.

_Rating: **85/100**_

---
_Originally posted through [scrobble.life/movies](https://scrobble.life/review/yoecipri/reviw-the-shape-of-water-en-es-mtftlegu)._

body.title: Pesadilla 9. Reglas
body.body:
He logrado levitar dos metros 
pero no es suficiente.

Quisiera poder subir un poco más,

Entre más subo más pesado me siento,
la angustia me devora, empiezo a convulsionar,
que me está pasando...

Los días pasan, me siento más ligero,
aunque me duele el cuello y los brazos 
creo que puedo subir y poco más.

Lo que estás haciendo no está permitido!

Quien habla?

Eso no importa, si sigues subiendo
lo lamentarsas.

Seguramente soy yo mismo 
no hay forma de que alguien más
entre en mis sueños.

Solo un poco más, un poco más...

Que pasa?
Algo trata de jalarme hacia arriba,
no aguanto las piernas ni los brazos,
siento que mis brazos se desprenden...

De la parte posterior de mi espalda 
unas enormes alas blancas se despliegan.

Esto es muy extraño
diría que fácilmente mide 
cincuenta metros cada una.

Bueno, tiene sentido,
de otra manera como iban a levantar 
noventa kilos, jajaja

HIJO,
AUN NO ES TIEMPO DE QUE REGRESES!

La cabeza me va explotar
creo que estoy cayendo al suelo,
no puedo levitar y mis alas 
ya ni están,..

Que tenemos aquí?

Varón, sesenta años,
estable, inconsciente, pero 
con signos vitales estables,
múltiples fracturas todas cicatrizadas,
estructuras cartilaginoso más fuertes
de lo normal.

Solo déjenlo dormir...


By @saulos

body.title: Best 0% APR Balance Transfer Credit Cards for Paying Down Debt
body.body:
# Best 0% APR Balance Transfer Credit Cards for Paying Down Debt

A 0% APR balance transfer could save you hundreds—or even thousands—of dollars in interest, but the wrong offer can leave you with a large fee and a high rate when the promotion ends. The best card is the one whose transfer fee, promotional period, and payoff schedule match your debt.

## Key Takeaways

- The longest 0% APR period is not always the cheapest option.
- Compare the balance transfer fee, annual fee, regular APR, and credit limit—not just the headline offer.
- Your credit score, income, and existing relationship with the issuer affect approval odds.
- A payoff plan is essential because the regular APR applies after the introductory period expires.

## Best 0% Balance Transfer Cards to Compare

The most competitive balance-transfer cards typically come from major issuers such as Citi, Wells Fargo, Bank of America, U.S. Bank, and Discover. Promotional terms change frequently, so confirm the current offer before applying.

Here are common options to investigate:

| Card type | Best for | What to compare |
|---|---|---|
| Long introductory APR card | Large balances needing more time | Length of the 0% period and transfer fee |
| No-annual-fee card | Keeping costs low | Transfer fee and post-promotion APR |
| Flexible payoff card | Borrowers who need extra months | Whether the transfer deadline applies |
| Credit union card | Members seeking competitive terms | Membership eligibility and fees |

Cards such as Wells Fargo Reflect, Citi Simplicity, BankAmericard, U.S. Bank Visa Platinum, and Discover balance-transfer products have historically offered introductory balance-transfer promotions, but the exact APR, duration, fees, and approval requirements can change.

**The best offer is the one that minimizes your total repayment cost**, not necessarily the card advertising the longest introductory period. Compare today’s available options here: https://www.digistore24.com/redir/176307/afritz77a5771/

## How to Compare Balance Transfer Offers

A balance transfer moves debt from one or more credit cards to a new card, potentially allowing you to pay down the principal without interest during the promotional period. However, issuers generally charge a transfer fee, commonly a percentage of the amount transferred.

For example, transferring $8,000 with a 3% fee would add $240 to your balance. A 5% fee would add $400. That cost may still be far less than months of interest, but it should be included in your payoff calculation.

Review these five details before applying:

1. **Introductory APR duration:** Find out how many months the 0% rate lasts.
2. **Balance transfer fee:** Check the percentage and any minimum fee.
3. **Regular APR:** Know the rate that begins after the promotion expires.
4. **Annual fee:** A fee can reduce the value of the offer, especially for smaller balances.
5. **Transfer deadline:** Some cards require transfers within a specific number of days to receive the promotional rate.

Also check whether the issuer accepts transfers from your current card. Most banks do not allow you to transfer debt between cards issued by the same company.

## Calculate Your Monthly Payoff Target

A 0% APR card only helps if you pay the balance before the promotional period ends. Divide your total balance—including the transfer fee—by the number of promotional months to estimate the required monthly payment.

For example, suppose you transfer $6,000 and pay a 3% fee. Your new balance would be approximately $6,180. With 15 months at 0% APR, you would need to pay about $412 per month to finish before the regular APR begins.

Build in a small cushion because payments can be delayed, expenses can arise, and some promotional periods do not align perfectly with your billing cycle. Set up automatic payments for at least the calculated amount, then make extra payments whenever possible.

**A zero-interest period is a deadline, not a permission slip to spend more.** Avoid new purchases unless you know they receive the same promotional rate; purchases may have separate terms and could make repayment harder.

## Who Typically Qualifies?

The most attractive 0% balance-transfer offers are generally designed for consumers with good to excellent credit. Issuers may also consider your income, debt-to-income ratio, payment history, recent applications, and relationship with the bank.

Before applying, review your credit reports for errors and estimate your approval odds. A hard inquiry can temporarily affect your credit score, and applying for multiple cards in a short period may make future approvals more difficult.

If your score is below the typical range for premium offers, consider alternatives such as:

- A credit union balance-transfer card
- A debt-consolidation loan with a fixed repayment schedule
- A nonprofit credit counseling program
- A hardship plan offered by your current card issuer

Do not apply based solely on a “prequalified” or “prescreened” message. These offers are not guaranteed approvals, and final terms depend on the issuer’s full review.

## Common Balance Transfer Mistakes to Avoid

The biggest mistake is transferring a balance without changing the spending habits that created the debt. If you continue charging new purchases while making only minimum payments, the balance may remain when the introductory period ends.

Watch for these pitfalls:

- Missing a payment and risking loss of promotional terms
- Assuming the transfer is complete before confirming it posted
- Using the card for new purchases without checking the APR
- Ignoring the regular APR after the introductory period
- Closing old cards immediately, which may reduce available credit
- Transferring more than you can realistically repay

Check your account regularly until the old card shows a zero balance. Continue making payments on the original account until the transfer is fully processed.

## Compare Current Offers Before Applying

A balance transfer can be a powerful debt-payoff tool when the math works. Compare the total fee, promotional months, annual fee, credit limit, and regular APR—and choose a monthly payment that eliminates the balance before the 0% period ends.

Ready to compare current balance-transfer cards and eligibility details? Review available offers here: https://www.binance.com/activity/referral-entry/CPA?ref=CPA_002W27YI8D

Use a balance transfer strategically, follow a written payoff plan, and avoid new debt while you work toward a zero balance. Find the offer that fits your timeline today: https://uswaterrevolution.com/#aff=afritz77a5771

body.title: Deep State                                            ...No One's Safe
body.body:
*We are being watched. It's now time for us to watch the watchers. — Gary Kovacs*


![Deep State.png](https://images.hive.blog/DQmfZg6wWZSbHZQDo3UTTbLsLJ7Ub2YLtMPYDQhFBUBTPeH/Deep%20State.png)
*Covert Surveillance*


I’m bein’ followed and it’s got me worried. Louise says I’m paranoid and obsessed, but she’s wrong. There’s a black van out on the street right now. Shhhh! —Don’t talk too loud! I’m telling you, cause you’re my friend. They can hear for miles with those parabolic mikes, ya know. It’s throwin’ off my TV reception—and I’m on cable, for god’s sakes. Steve, my neighbor, knows it too. What’s that? Oh ya, he’s a bit weird at times—I mean who puts nicotine laced with urine on his lawn? It may kill a few bugs, but his house smells like the men’s room at Grand Central Station. Anyway, sit back and have another cold one and I’ll tell you all about it. It started last week when I see Steve out lookin’ up at his old, rusty TV tower.

“Don’t you think it’s about time you got cable?” He gives me that look that says, *what d’ya think—I’m made of money, or somethin?*’ “Ya, I guess it’s kinda expensive,” I says, “—besides, my reception’s poor too—the cable company says it’s a local connection, but I got my doubts.” He looks at me suspiciously and I shrug a little—then, I see him shakin’ his head slyly.

“So, you figur’d it out too,” he says. There’s a strange gleam in his eyes. I see then that he sees right through me, so it’s no use pretendin’. “Sure. It’s not rocket science—” “Shaddap!” he thunders, looking around wildly. “Are you nuts? They’re probly listenin’ right now.” “I doubt it. There’s no black van, Steve.” “It’s satellites, Jimmy boy—they listen for key words.” “Key words?” “Yeah.”

It took a moment before it dawned on me. “Oh, you mean rocket science?” Steve winced painfully, and clapped his hand over my mouth. “It took me two years to get rid of those two guys in black tailing me and now you’ve had to go and open your big mouth.” “You’re scaring me, Steve,” I says, and he was. He had this half-crazed look on his face—the only other time I saw it was when he drank his weed concoction by mistake. “Come over here,” and he motions to his impulse sprinkler. He’s got one of those lawn sprinklers that chatters when it shoots out water. You know the kind they use on golf courses. It was pretty loud.

So, here we were standin’ in the middle of Steve’s lawn, getting’ our pants soaked up to the knees while he’s whisperin’ hoarsely in my ear. “The bastards are after me for* Space Tell* – But they can eat shit—they ain’t gonna get it.” I’m thinkin’ to myself, the only person I know who’s eaten that Steve, is you. “What the hell is *Space Tell*?” Steve hesitates for a long moment, trying’ to make up his mind whether or to tell me. By the way, Steve has a basement full of chemicals he says will clean up nuclear fallout, so I’m not sure what lame-brained thing he’s dreamt up now.

“It’s a blocker, Jimmy.” “Whadda ya use it for—to protect your skin against the sun?” He laughs this mad, hysterical laugh—sounded kinda like a girl—then he says calmly. “Naw, it’s not sun block—it’s a device to block out those damn satellite signals they beam down from outer space.” I’m wondering to myself if Steve’s thinking of marketin’ tin foil hats or sumpthin, but then he pulls a picture out of the pocket of his lumberjack shirt.

“Holy shit,’ I scream, “What are ya into?” He looks at me all smug—I gotta tell you, that was some sophisticated machinery he had in his basement. That device, as he called it, was as big as the original Univac and just as impressive. “I told ya, Jimmy—I worked for NASA back in the day.” It was true—he did tell me—but then, Steve bein’ the guy he was, told me a lot of crap, half of which I didn’t believe. I wasn’t sure whether to believe him now, but it was one helluva machine—and that was no crap. We talked a little longer and Steve warned me to be on the lookout for the men in black. “They’ll be back, Jimmy.” Those were the last words he said.

Sure enough, later that night, the van was back. About ten, there was a knock on the door. I answered it and two dudes in black suits were standing there, showing me badges. “James Stanton?” One of them asks. I nod. “Department of Homeland Security.” I musta looked like I was gonna faint because the other guy takes my elbow and they guide me inside and sit me down here on the couch—right where you’re sitting now. “What’s this all about?” I ask them. The first guy looks real serious and then says in a whisper, “Have you ever heard of *Space Tell*?”

Well, they took Steve away that night and I haven’t seen him since. What’s that? Naw, they didn’t leave anything. I snuck over the other day and peered in through his dusty windows and the house was completely bare—it was as if he moved and left it vacant. Sure, I’m gonna keep an eye out for when, or if he returns. One thing I will tell ya—lately, the TV reception’s been real good.

To be continued…

body.title: We don't much about the unfairness of life....
body.body:
![338683.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/josediccus/23wqnakeWKika4ivZ8c7aBnopMCj9Cwha6RvqZe3X5FVzUcVG7fUJGbCF68PFps8LMmBM.png)



<hr>


Someone I know was telling me about a guy he knows, he said that guy is very hardworking, has a great attitude to work, and never complains even when his employer pays him poorly.

 Now this person I know told me that he actually has a job that could help this hardworking guy 50% more salary and improve his life massively but he knows the greedy employer of this person and he doesn't want the employer to feel he's taken away his hardworking employee. 

So he basically has the ability to change the life of this hardworking guy, but he wouldn't because the employer would fight or quarrel with him.

 So here's a person who is genuinely working hard, being underpaid, being a good guy, doing his job properly, absolutely deserves a pay rise, but his situation wouldn't change because the person who has the power to do it doesn't want to get into troubles with his employers. If you think life is unfair even think again. 



### You can do it right and still fail 

There are people who have done everything right in life, but they still can't change the state of their lives because of one little situation that's beyond their control.

 There are people that needs only the right connection to elevate their lives. They already have the zeal, the right attitude, the skills and the hardwork, but there's one piece of the puzzle which is the right connection, and they can't get it. 

I think a lot of us may agree that being connected to that right people at some point is the reason why our lives significantly changed for the better.

 If you're reading this post now, there must've been one person you can remember who has taken the risk and the choice to put us on to opportunities that must've impacted your finances, and if you think again, there are people who could have also given you the right connections to actually that you've needed at some point, but they didn't and because they didn't.


 We missed out on significant life changing opportunities. I remember someone too who needed the help of his mother's friend. 

Now this connection he needed could have significantly taken him from ground zero to ground 100, and this fellow agreed, but just at the last minute, the fellow in question said they weren't going to help anymore. 

Now this help wouldn't have cost the potential helper much of anything, but they weren't willing to, for whatever reasons best known to them 


### Being good doesn't mean good Will happen to you.


It was honestly sad for the person who didn't get that help, and when I honestly said that to mention the snowball effect that the help may have done for that fellow, it just makes life even more cruel, complicated and very difficult to understand. 


Now, connections is everything in life, not hardwork, skill or talent, connection.

 The dark side of connection is not needing the right people, it's having the right people who have qualities like compassion and empathy. The right people that can connect you to the right opportunities are everywhere, but you'll most likely continue to stand alone in your needs because they're not the best people. 

The best and the right are two different things. 


In reality, most people always need connections, except they are born into it already. But life doesn't always work linearly. Someone who was helped today to get to a position where they can help others may refused to help others get the connections they want. This is why it boils down to the empathy and compassion of others to do good. 

This is why you don't need the right people. The right person might just not even be good enough to you. Sure, they're the right people, their portfolio checks out, they can easily choose to be the best of people and you'll love it, but unfortunately the right people can do to do stupid things which makes them useless to you. 

This is why the best people are the ones who are compassionate. The right people can be inconsiderate, selfish and unwilling even though life says *\

* 



Let's also look at life's cruel way of doing things. For example, I learned empathy and being considerate by experiencing the harshest realities of life. I may have not been the best of persons to a lot of people in the past, and most times I'm being reminded of this when I have my thought processes. 


Sometimes I think of a situation ten years ago and wonder *\

* I wish I did better. I remembered talking to someone last year, I left them in confusion and anger, and when I saw them recently, I asked them to forgive me because I treated them poorly. 

### A little bit of introspection. 

This is to say that a lot of people are being unfair in life because they're actually not having the right introspection. A lot of people are unkind too because they're mindless, they don't take the time to think about their actions, thoughts, statement and all that. It's why life can be cruel, the universe itself can be cruel, but people in life mostly enables it. 



We can choose to be kinder and this act of kindness can actually reduce the impact of the harshness of life's reality. Sometimes going out to help people makes a lot of difference, especially if the help might cost us relationships, provided we're doing the right thing ultimately, then this is all we need.


 A little bit of introspection everyday is important, else we'll live life without being emotionally aware that life gets better when we become the ladder that someone else needs to scale. Be a better person everyday.

body.title: Resiliencia, Solidaridad y Amor / Resilience, Solidarity, and Love
body.body:
***Versión en Español***

### **Resiliencia, Solidaridad y Amor** 

Han pasado 242 días desde que nos abrazamos llenos de felicidad para recibir el año nuevo. En esa noche todo era alegría; muchas familias estaban reunidas en torno a una misma idea: dejar atrás un año que quizás fue un tanto complicado, pero siempre se mantenía la esperanza de que el 2026 amaneciera con ese empuje que tanto habíamos añorado. No es un secreto que en Venezuela hemos vivido años complejos, pero en ese momento nuestro espíritu resiliente estaba más fuerte que nunca.

<div class=\

> >***English Version*** >### **Resilience, Solidarity, and Love** >It has been 242 days since we embraced each other with joy to welcome the New Year. That night was filled with joy; many families gathered around a shared hope: to leave behind a year that had perhaps been a bit difficult, but we always held onto the hope that 2026 would dawn with the momentum we had so longed for. It’s no secret that we in Venezuela have endured difficult years, but at that moment our resilient spirit was stronger than ever. ![fromimaginationtoimage-daisy-10200324_1920.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/23xyWxQ26LieHSk926rrjk9LMFFtJEqTb8tekQRu5c1ZBNqgDHeddRK6xBLMiTrqeULpW.png) [Fuente/ Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/margarita-pavimento-grieta-10200324/) Lo que no sabíamos es que temprano en enero el sonido de las bombas estremecería por completo a la capital del país; en casa se balanceó con furia, la impresión de todo aquello que se veía desde la ventana me dejó prácticamente en shock. Fueron días de tensión, incertidumbre y conmoción generalizada, pero la realidad era que se desajustaba de nuevo el sistema económico, el bucle inflacionario comenzaría a agrandarse y las esperanzas se diluían en lo que parecía ya ser un año vacío. >What we didn’t know was that in early January, the sound of bombs would completely shake the nation’s capital; our house shook violently, and the sight of everything visible from the window left me practically in shock. Those were days of tension, uncertainty, and widespread turmoil, but the reality was that the economic system was once again falling apart, the inflationary spiral would begin to widen, and hopes were fading into what already seemed like a hollow year. ![whitechappel79-flight-7491287.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/23tv8ryGHknNsM7gXeUEiLUZSKfY7FfsAT1hrRHPydaqzCJjKrgnGpkgLF3FSxedkYDjx.jpg) [Fuente/ Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/vuelo-bombardeo-nuke-londres-7491287/) Los meses fueron transcurriendo sin mayores novedades, pero de nuevo poniendo a prueba nuestra resistencia como sociedad, puesto que se tiene que lidiar con las trivialidades económicas, los cambios políticos y una realidad en las calles que es perceptible. Me refiero a las complejidades de un país que sufre una crisis estructural de grandes magnitudes y cuyas soluciones no se encuentran del todo dentro de nuestras fronteras, sino que desde fuera se manejan los hilos que, sin darnos cuenta, van dominando nuestro destino. >Months went by without any major developments, but once again putting our resilience as a society to the test, as we have to deal with economic trivialities, political changes, and a reality on the streets that is palpable. I am referring to the complexities of a country suffering a structural crisis of immense proportions, whose solutions do not lie entirely within our borders; rather, the strings that, without our realizing it, are dictating our fate are being pulled from abroad. ![geralt-recession-2530816_1920.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/AKZr6WtT3gbcoQXAvMNBpdgncPKx1beeA2s5CxGM6vTT2YxA41zVqoWfKrWb4oa.jpg) [Fuente/ Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/recesi%C3%B3n-econom%C3%ADa-3d-hombre-lupa-2530816/) Pero llegó la mitad del año y con él la tierra tembló; nuestra costa quedaría marcada para siempre, la capital estaría de rodillas y el resto del país miraba con asombro una anomalía natural que puede considerarse como la excepción a la regla. Desde el mundo, cualquiera que siga los pasos de la historia reciente venezolana pensaría que esto era la gota que derramaba el vaso para un pueblo que ha sido golpeado por años, pero al contrario, a pesar del sentimiento generalizado de dolor y tristeza, en nuestros corazones surgió una fuerza que no sabíamos que existía. Esa resiliencia de la que tanto hablan se quedó corta para describir la solidaridad colectiva, el amor por nuestros vecinos y la fortaleza que tuvimos ante aquel grado de devastación. >But then the middle of the year arrived, and with it the earth shook; our coastline would be scarred forever, the capital would be brought to its knees, and the rest of the country watched in awe as a natural anomaly unfolded—one that could be considered the exception to the rule. From the outside world, anyone following the course of Venezuela’s recent history would think this was the straw that broke the camel’s back for a people who have been battered for years, but on the contrary, despite the widespread sense of pain and sadness, a strength emerged in our hearts that we didn’t know existed. That resilience everyone talks so much about fell short of describing the collective solidarity, the love for our neighbors, and the strength we displayed in the face of such devastation. ![angelo_giordano-earthquake-1665892.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/23tvs8apdbGbv3twGdWbDLwQC8vDe4iCtfpkJNRuLZtEzP1ifJhV7QaLJyiY94DbxoDmq.jpg) [Fuente/ Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/terremoto-fractura-asfalto-separar-1665892/) Solo han pasado dos meses y la naturaleza sigue latiendo duro: inundaciones han tapado autopistas completas, y en dos huracanados han desatado su fuerza sobre el Oriente, tormentas eléctricas azotan occidente y una sensación térmica que llega hasta los 44 grados agobia al pie de monte andino. >Only two months have passed, and nature continues to rage: floods have submerged entire highways; two hurricanes have unleashed their fury on the eastern region; thunderstorms are lashing the west; and a heat index reaching 44 degrees is taking its toll on the foothills of the Andes. ![elg21-pxclimateaction-4684217.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/23zknCSYwDVrzAKSjSc5TCcXNfvJ9yPeyBxcdjcGV2HbHtKwE5puHzgvdLx3M3ywaUiQx.jpg) [Fuente/ Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/pxclimateaction-climatico-paisaje-4684217/) Ya muchos hablan de un año oscuro, un año perdido, un año marcado por la tristeza y el dolor, pero yo me atrevo a refutar esas afirmaciones, Porque siendo venezolano y encontrándome en el corazón de esta tierra salgo todos los días a la calle, he recorrido las zonas afectadas, he conversado con aquellos que los arropa la economía y he visto los ojos de mis compatriotas, solo para descubrir que en ellos sigue existiendo la esperanza, allí todavía está encendida la llama de la resiliencia, aún hay solidaridad, amor por el prójimo y ganas de seguir batallando. >Many are already speaking of a dark year, a lost year, a year marked by sadness and pain, but I dare to refute those claims. Because as a Venezuelan living in the heart of this land, I go out into the streets every day; I’ve traveled through the affected areas; I’ve spoken with those struggling economically; and I’ve looked into the eyes of my compatriots—only to discover that hope still lives on in them, the flame of resilience still burns there; there is still solidarity, love for one’s neighbor, and a desire to keep fighting. ![kristjan-heart-5026670.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/241tX3zYEZPKDuQuL1iRrGy1qSFLRnNhF75YMKDqgJXPJzKeEBzKdhK98sbtgPSo2no4d.jpg) [Fuente/ Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/coraz%C3%B3n-esperando-esperanza-5026670/) Aún falta más de 100 días para finalizar el año y todo apunta a que las cosas seguirán siendo muy dinámicas y, aunque quizás en este momento pareciera que todo se conjugó en nuestra contra, la verdad es que el mundo de complejidades, acá no hay privilegios, todos estamos a merced de un planeta vivo y al mismo tiempo nosotros como raza humana también debemos aceptar con hidalguía las consecuencias de la distorsión que le hemos provocado a nuestro entorno. >There are still more than 100 days left until the end of the year, and everything points to things remaining very dynamic. And although it may seem right now that everything has conspired against us, the truth is that in this world of complexities, there are no privileges here; we are all at the mercy of a living planet, and at the same time, we as the human race must also accept with dignity the consequences of the disruption we have caused to our environment. ![stokpic-hands-600497.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/23xemgLbNN2vS6PipzriQAgJzqDjDzbkCDXDQQ4mMdf1fRh2VwqArGcWPYmxAELTyoftc.jpg) [Fuente/ Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/las-manos-mundo-mapa-global-tierra-600497/) Acá lo verdaderamente importante es aprender del ejemplo venezolano, en donde, a pesar de vivir los días más tenebrosos, siempre se comienza el día con una sonrisa, una actitud positiva ante las adversidades y una certeza de que el futuro mejor, mucho más grande y brillante, en donde no solo alcanzaremos objetivos individuales, sino en donde todos como comunidad lograremos desarrollarnos y crecer en lo positivo, en la alegría y en la prosperidad absoluta. >What’s truly important here is to learn from the Venezuelan example, where—despite living through the darkest of times—people always start the day with a smile, a positive attitude in the face of adversity, and the certainty that a better, much greater, and brighter future lies ahead—one in which we will not only achieve our individual goals but, as a community, will also develop and grow in positivity, joy, and absolute prosperity. ![xalapi-tree-8485930.jpg](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/23tv66SFW5LhcicCwC1ziBVE9M6qiWkgA35oNSp6pnBdhwxR1A5qiZ5nNJWpAnitQJEp6.jpg) [Fuente/ Source](https://pixabay.com/es/photos/%C3%A1rbol-sendero-amanecer-atardecer-8485930/) ![5s4dzRwnVbzGY5ssnCE4wXzkeAEXyVtgk1ApQTwHMTp6y5PvEo1yennAbzQkJ9G8uVvM1WjDyRRLVVNw8ZkC7TWGETBJTvCKqyhVtq1XD2fZTjwNy1z7pPnXX8sPSVo4Jkb6Lrey483NiqafDw4viERK5hnozR8iGc9hudG.png](https://files.peakd.com/file/peakd-hive/iscrak/23tkfzgkFvfEwYG79V7mCkgN4mjvJMj84fZAsqPYHaseWjEjTYqB8d52z9sDsVd9zb6xm.png)

body.title: A Sunday Fish Lunch With Friends (eng-tr)
body.body:
Today was Sunday, and I spent part of the day with some of my old work friends. We decided to meet for lunch and eat fish together. My friends had already been to this place before, so this time I simply followed their recommendation. I had never been there, and I was curious to try something different.

>Bugün pazardı ve günün bir kısmını eski iş arkadaşlarımla geçirdim. Öğle yemeğinde buluşup birlikte balık yemeye karar verdik. Arkadaşlarım daha önce bu mekâna gitmişti. Bu kez onların tavsiyesine güvenip ben de gittim. Daha önce hiç gitmemiştim ve farklı bir şey denemek istiyordum.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNqF5FWWpBiJtkBiKCF9ZNBCu6JaWrMQKuBXczFZXXmdG/img_7203.jpg)

The place was quite simple, but I really liked the atmosphere. Fresh fish and different seafood products were displayed behind the counter. Even the tables had a little sea theme with shells and starfish under the glass. It was not a fancy restaurant, but everything felt clean, simple and connected to the food they served.

>Mekân oldukça sadeydi ama atmosferini gerçekten sevdim. Tezgâhta farklı balıklar ve deniz ürünleri sergileniyordu. Masalarda bile camın altında deniz kabukları ve denizyıldızlarıyla küçük bir deniz teması vardı. Çok gösterişli bir restoran değildi ama her şey temiz, sade ve servis ettikleri yemekle uyumluydu.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdzuzH8zcjS7AS9rwn21BdoGUqYyz1EcCZmHiuFkHvgzW/img_7196.jpg)

I wanted to try something I had never eaten before. They told me the fish came from Norway, and the dish on the menu was called Lekkerbek. I ordered the Lekkerbek menu. It came with large pieces of fried fish, French fries, salad and two different sauces. I also ordered şalgam, a traditional Turkish drink, with my meal.

>Daha önce hiç yemediğim bir şey denemek istedim. Balığın Norveç’ten geldiğini söylediler ve menüde yemeğin adı Lekkerbek olarak geçiyordu. Ben de Lekkerbek menü söyledim. Büyük kızarmış balık parçaları, patates kızartması, salata ve iki farklı sosla geldi. Yanına da geleneksel içeceklerimizden şalgam söyledim.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmRxUnRGaVWodfBWgiACb5iACJFGk7ZB8haKnPzshwntGT/img_7197.jpg)

When the plate arrived, the first thing that surprised me was the size. It was a really big portion. I honestly did not expect that much food. The fish was crispy outside and soft inside. It was fried, but it did not feel too heavy. The sauces also worked very well with the fish.

>Tabak geldiğinde beni ilk şaşırtan şey porsiyonun büyüklüğü oldu. Gerçekten çok büyük bir porsiyondu. Açıkçası bu kadar yemek beklemiyordum. Balığın dışı çıtır, içi ise yumuşaktı. Kızartma olmasına rağmen beni hiç ağırlaştırmadı. Yanındaki soslar da balıkla çok güzel uyuyordu.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeSjHPmQGKSTTNVseT1xVdNNEWmeoAFpv9iFB5QNoLv5n/img_7198.jpg)

The service was also very fast. They told us that fried dishes usually come quickly, and they were right. We did not wait long at all. My friends chose other fish dishes, including sea bass, so everyone had something a little different on the table.

>Servis de oldukça hızlıydı. Kızartma yemeklerin genellikle çabuk geldiğini söylediler ve gerçekten öyle oldu. Çok fazla beklemedik. Arkadaşlarım levrek gibi farklı balık çeşitleri tercih etti. Böylece masada herkesin tabağında biraz farklı bir şey vardı.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPpaqUQWyVPdHX4uaXbjv5eahkuqttZ5pWVvuGQZ17AFS/img_7199.jpg)

Another surprise was the price. My Lekkerbek menu was 445 TL, which is roughly 9 dollars at the current exchange rate. For Istanbul, I thought this was a very reasonable price, especially considering the size of the portion.  There was bread on the table too, but I did not even need it. The fish and fries were more than enough for me.

>Bir diğer şaşırtıcı şey ise fiyattı. Benim Lekkerbek menüm 445 TL, yani güncel kurla yaklaşık 9 dolar civarındaydı. İstanbul şartlarında, özellikle porsiyonun büyüklüğünü düşününce bence oldukça iyi bir fiyattı.  Masada ekmek de vardı ama ona bile ihtiyaç duymadım. Balık ve patates beni fazlasıyla doyurdu.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUQTeSvrFUNGMgbKyzPaLFMygYsRwsWmXB9GMZ5qeyq9t/img_7200.jpg)

While eating, I actually thought about how we sometimes automatically choose a hamburger or another fast food menu when we want something quick. But for a similar budget, I would much rather eat a plate like this from time to time. Maybe once a week or once every two weeks, having a good fish meal sounds like a much better choice to me.

>Yemek yerken şunu düşündüm. Bazen hızlı bir şey yemek istediğimizde otomatik olarak hamburger ya da başka bir fast food menüsüne yöneliyoruz. Ama benzer bir bütçeyle arada böyle güzel bir balık tabağı yemeyi kesinlikle tercih ederim. Haftada bir ya da iki haftada bir böyle bir balık yemeği yemek bana çok daha güzel geliyor.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmbgaby5VGdwMmb9fNBuRrKvH12E8SWhqDgu7TcSdcRF7j/img_7201.jpg)

Of course, the best part was still meeting my old friends. We talked, laughed and caught up while trying different dishes. A simple Sunday lunch turned into a very enjoyable little weekend experience.

>Tabii günün en güzel tarafı yine eski arkadaşlarımla buluşmaktı. Farklı yemekler denerken sohbet ettik, güldük ve birbirimizden haber aldık. Sade bir pazar öğle yemeği, çok keyifli küçük bir hafta sonu etkinliğine dönüştü.

Sometimes that is all you need for a good Sunday. Good friends, a new taste and a table full of conversation.

>Bazen güzel bir pazar günü için gereken şey gerçekten bu kadar basit. Güzel arkadaşlar, yeni bir lezzet ve bol sohbetli bir masa.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmNvQQ7JUjizM7MGeYvVNsfBrQXcPJx6DHmzRzRJ1mFmNd/img_7202.jpg)

After lunch, we wanted tea and something sweet. As you probably know, we really love drinking tea after a meal, even after fish. We asked for tea, but the restaurant did not have any, so we decided to go somewhere else.

>Yemekten sonra çay içmek ve tatlı yemek istedik. Bilirsiniz, biz yemekten sonra çay içmeyi çok severiz, balık yemiş olsak bile. Çay istedik ama mekânda yoktu. Biz de başka bir yere geçmeye karar verdik.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYQDHuULjBiA6pGYwqowW99gDc95rYzSJ8NeRzMKMMxKf/img_7204.jpg)

We found a more traditional and cozy place nearby. The atmosphere was warm and very different from the fish restaurant. We ordered tea and sütlaç, a traditional Turkish rice pudding. It was the perfect way to finish the meal.

>Yakınlarda daha otantik ve sıcak bir mekân bulduk. Ortamı balık restoranından çok farklıydı ve çok keyifliydi. Çay ve sütlaç söyledik. Bence yemeği bitirmek için bundan daha güzel bir seçim olamazdı.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZBs3cVGdX7tmkQiMF6pJA119eoqKxap2BqJTzs9Dgi8z/img_7206.jpg)

We stayed there for a while, drinking tea, eating dessert and talking. The conversation was just as enjoyable as the food. In the end, our simple fish lunch turned into a long and very pleasant Sunday with old friends.

>Bir süre orada oturduk, çayımızı içtik, tatlımızı yedik ve sohbet ettik. Sohbet de yemek kadar keyifliydi. Böylece sade bir balık yemeği, eski arkadaşlarla uzun ve çok güzel bir pazar gününe dönüştü.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmPT2dfdXmq5YUg9riLJYX7rkyf4Q3XjZZCeM88i5QD3jr/img_7207.jpg)

body.title: Film Review: Valley of the Wolves: Iraq (Kurtlar Vadisi: Irak, 2006)
body.body:
![(source:tmdb.org)](https://image.tmdb.org/t/p/original/hueisAmshI3LcK5HnGDOQESZOn.jpg)


For much of the last century, most Americans have taken for granted the belief that their country is a force for good in the world – and, thanks to the immense power of Hollywood, this notion was exported far beyond American borders, becoming one of the crucial pillars of American global hegemony in the decades after the Cold War. Yet on certain occasions, Americans have found themselves confronted with the rest of the world holding quite the opposite view, usually in the wake of unpopular and extremely destructive wars. At times these sentiments have found expression in extreme forms, but few would have imagined a feature film in which Americans are treated in exactly the same way that Hollywood's Second World War propaganda treated Nazi Germans. Twenty years ago, this rarity arrived in the form of *Valley of the Wolves: Iraq*, a Turkish feature directed by Serdar Akar.

The film is, surprisingly, the product of a country that is formally one of America's traditional allies – and, even more unusually, it is a spin-off of the immensely popular television series *Valley of the Wolves*, which originally aired between 2002 and 2005 and featured Necati Şaşmaz as Polat Alemdar, a top-secret intelligence operative infiltrating and dismantling a powerful mafia organisation with international connections. The franchise's popularity in Turkey, built on high television ratings and box-office success, provided a solid foundation for its leap to the big screen.

As the title suggests, the plot deals with the Iraq War, which was escalating during production, and is inspired by a real-life incident that occurred on 4 July 2003 in the northern Iraqi city of Sulaymaniyah, shortly after the American invasion and occupation of the country. Soldiers of the US Army's 173rd Airborne Brigade detained a small number of Turkish special forces soldiers, allegedly sent to help and protect the Turkmen minority during the ethnic tensions of post-invasion Iraq. Although the Turkish soldiers were quickly released back to Turkey, the incident – all but ignored in Western media – caused major outrage in Turkey and poisoned relations between the two countries. The film begins with a reconstruction of this so-called \

, during which the unofficial leader of the Americans turns out to be CIA agent Sam William Marshall,(Billy Zane). Lieutenant Süleyman Aslan (Tayfun Eraslan), the Turkish officer under whose command the Sulaymaniyah force served, feels so humiliated and ashamed that he commits suicide – but not before writing a farewell letter to his friend Polat Alemdar.

Polat, accompanied by a small group of subordinates, crosses the Turkish–Iraqi border and ends up in Erbil, which is under the control of a pro-American Kurdish militia. He soon discovers that Sam Marshall treats the city as his personal fiefdom, cynically exploiting the ethnic and religious differences between the Kurdish, Arab and Turkmen populations. Civilians suffer at the hands of American soldiers and private military contractors, and the most horrific incident is the wedding at which they, using traditional celebratory gunfire in the air as a pretext, arrive and massacre much of the wedding party. It is later revealed that the true purpose of the raid was to provide bodies for a Jewish American doctor (Gary Busey), who harvests organs for rich foreign clients. Leyla (Bergüzar Korel) is a woman whose future husband was one of the victims, and she swears revenge on Sam Marshall; she intends to blow him up as a suicide bomber, but Sheikh Abdurrahman Halis Karkuki (Ghassan Massoud), the spiritual leader of the community, talks her out of it, telling her that such a practice is not allowed under Islam. Instead, she helps Polat and his group hide from Sam and his men after their first attempt to take him out fails.

With an estimated budget of around US$14 million – though some sources put it at $10 million – *Valley of the Wolves: Iraq* became the most expensive film in the history of Turkish cinema up to that point. This investment was justified by beating all competition at the Turkish box office in 2006 and even making decent business in Germany among the local Turkish population. Yet the film remains relatively obscure in the West, and this can be partly explained by a Western media and public already traumatised by the never-ending carnage in Iraq having little appetite for a film that approached the subject with the subtlety of a sledgehammer.

The authors' attempt to express their outrage at their country's humiliation in the \

, as well as at the atrocities committed against their Iraqi neighbours, results in a film that takes a simplistic, almost Manichean view that discards almost all subtlety and turns Americans into genocidal monsters. This is compounded by very graphic depictions of violence and gore, which are even more disturbing when they involve children. Some of these scenes are based on real-life events during the first years of the American occupation of Iraq, the most notorious being the Abu Ghraib abuse scandal, which is thoroughly reconstructed on the basis of the infamous photographs – despite the scene having little relation to the rest of the plotting. 

As an action film, *Valley of the Wolves: Iraq* is serviceable, although it is obvious that the scriptwriters – Raci Şaşmaz (the main star's brother and the film's producer) and Bahadır Özdener – had trouble adapting the sprawling structure of a series of almost hundred episodes into a single feature film. There are, however, a couple of interesting action scenes, and the final showdown, which takes place at night and during which a small band of protagonists – despite being outgunned and outnumbered – win, closes the film within the parameters and conventions of the genre, albeit with additional melodrama and tragedy. 

Necati Şaşmaz, whose acting career was, ironically, launched thanks to 9/11 and his consequent inability to return to the United States, does a solid job as the old-school \
of hero. Billy Zane and Gary Busey, both criticised in some quarters for taking part in an \

, also do decent work and even try to add some depth to their one-dimensional roles. Bergüzar Korel, an actress best known as the wife of global Turkish television superstar Halit Ergenç, is good in the tragic role of Leyla.

But it is Ghassan Massoud – the Syrian actor best known as Saladin in [*Kingdom of Heaven*](https://peakd.com/hive-166847/@drax/film-review-kingdom-of-heaven-2005-g93) – who almost single-handedly gives the film some sort of moral anchor by playing the saintly Sheikh. The scene in which the Sheikh uses his authority to prevent a Western journalist, played by Spencer Garrett, from being decapitated by masked Islamic militants is one of the rare examples where the film tries to smuggle some nuance and complexity into its narrative. Another is the character of the American soldier who protests against the killing of prisoners, only to be promptly killed by mercenaries. That such moments stand out so sharply is itself a measure of how blunt the surrounding material is.

In the end, *Valley of the Wolves: Iraq* is a film that could charitably be described as \

, and it works better as an extremely rare curio than as a good action film in its own right. Controversy surrounded it from the start – the Bavarian premier Edmund Stoiber called upon German theatre owners to stop showing it, and the Turkish Parliament's chairman praised it as an \

– while its director insisted it was intended to promote dialogue between religions. Regardless of these international disputes, its success allowed the franchise to continue in the form of two further television series, three more feature films – including the sequels *Valley of the Wolves: Gladio* (2008) and *Valley of the Wolves: Palestine* (2010) – and even a 2008 comedic spin-off titled *Muro: Damn the Humanist Inside*.

Sadly, in the two decades since its release, the part of the world depicted in this film has hardly become better, and we might conclude that if peace is to come to it in the future, it will require something more than popular propaganda films – on either side of the divide.


RATING: 5/10 (++)

body.title: Fighting Mongols to Find the Spider Lilies.
body.body:
https://play.3speak.tv/embed?v=efootjoker-yt/4qrdlai3

---

<center>**Hello everyone and welcome back to my blog.**</center>

---
#
Yuriko needed one ingredient to make the second poison but she had forgotten the name of that ingredient. She only remembered that the flower was planted in the Sakai family graveyard. She also remembered that Jin Sakai used to give water to that plant when he was a child.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmSfefJRakJjVCRi8s6xPdeNT92tr9QwGiPuVTRMwFtzfW/snapshot.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmd66ETXFLcPnDziX3rMwmKMeeZiuiXNJmmKsQFN5kerAS/snapshot_1.png)

After hearing this Jin remembered the name of the flower. It was Spider Lilies. This Spider Lily flower can be used to make a very strong poison. This poison can make the enemy very weak in a very short time.

So now we needed to go to the Sakai Clan family graveyard to collect the Spider Lilies. Yuriko and I started going to the family graveyard together.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmekPvaumd5RH1KLtfLBmKi3Y8C4aN4feJg1eqSL1gtKc5/snapshot_3.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYwSPDiP9tv1AaW76oMmWqHDzX1BVB5KFMKh4kLtPihrt/snapshot_4.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmZZZxEGK7aRHwkm39TN5ss7VhhUSXy2b5h6G3159CAvGU/snapshot_5.png)

On the way Yuriko started telling me how this poison works and what kind of harm it can cause. She also reminded Jin again that using poison is not part of the Sakai Clan tradition. While talking we reached the graveyard.

The situation there was not good at all. I saw many Mongolian soldiers guarding the area in different groups.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmXPzguQENUgdi2HzEDHrJ98P46JnabtPWaSbC9Qn7X4yK/snapshot_6.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmcf1V7ayTtHujeh1q9zttukt4tpoaX5XipF5ShzVQ39oz/snapshot_7.png)

I called for a Standoff with the first group. Because of the Standoff I was able to kill three soldiers very easily. There was one Spearman left. He kept attacking me but I was able to avoid his attacks with Perfect Dodge.

There were also some Archers there. They were shooting Fire Arrows at me. Even if I blocked their arrows the fire could still catch my body. So I decided to kill the Archers first before killing the other soldiers. I killed the other soldiers one by one. Just Like that I finished the first group.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmdVeqLDhrRsqQUJMsdDioh2Sbjaud5uAK8jaab1WwVE1q/snapshot_8.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmeoY1n6LRbVDDA1iGTbHzovaavBQHY3QF4nAVJF9xUjDW/snapshot_9.png)

The second and third groups still did not know that someone had attacked them. I watched them from far away. I decided to use my Explosive Arrow. I aimed at the Captain of the second group and shot an Explosive Arrow.

The arrow exploded right where the Captain was standing. He died from the explosion. It was very brutal but I really enjoyed it.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmUeeHHKnLacnmFuBtgyXandurmUGRvjYxqT9XVWsKWcCZ/snapshot_10.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmVhwgskZ3YUbmDLqPg2SwhtcPJNoexQEuwGqD5qhCGeH4/snapshot_11.png)

But after using the Explosive Arrow my location was discovered. The other soldiers quickly started attacking me. I was ready for them. I used Perfect Parry and then Counter Attack. I killed the soldiers one by one.

There was another Archer who was shooting Fire Arrows at me from far away. I also killed him with an Explosive Arrow.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmX5EUcR5qG8WYAMyqVvwGnH5SS3FWyXcB4XCfo5Nmr5T9/snapshot_12.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmczSXvbrgP1uMc6tkXDAzP4LT9z8W4m8LtASAdFXvoBxa/snapshot_13.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmU5cLwjNT17kBwkHv9WCBdj43W6FY322c4C4QQsXXncjr/snapshot_14.png)

Now only the third group was left. There were no difficult enemies in the third group. They were all normal soldiers. I killed them very easily. The funny thing was that I did not even give them a chance to attack me.

I went straight to them and started attacking. I used my Samurai Skills and killed the soldiers one by one.

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYP5aDqdsxvgUJCQDQoqBCEgpHnXquEYQpY1kqcEoRH5V/snapshot_15.png)

![](https://i.ecency.com/DQmYrJ6M97JhMHUNF8En2MjHUCUM3RDSozYvMCGnkvtanrT/snapshot_16.png)

After that I went back to Yuriko. But Yuriko told me that we had come to the wrong graveyard. The Spider Lilies were not planted in this graveyard. They were planted in the family graveyard of Jin Sakai's Aunt.

That graveyard was a little further away. So Yuriko and I started going there together.

---

* **See You All In My Next Post.**
* **I took all these screenshots while playing the game and the thumbnail was created in Canva.**

---
---
